A question for you, what is your favorite chapter and favorite event? And why is it your favorite chapter?
Click to expand...
still unsure if I prefer chapter 2 or 3, but chap 2 has my favorite event chain with the 2nd christmas party and introduces so much of the cast that I'd have to give it the edge until I fully re-read chap 3

as for favorite events, there's so many obvious ones so I'll try to point out some that not everyone would think of (maybe lol)

Reconciliation/Neon Heart (If I Close My Eyes):
Yuki's attempts at being a better person not functionning on the one part she cares the most being her daughter, and Yumi's absolutely valid feelings to not want to let her in life after all these years of neglect
it's also one of the first moment of self reflection on Akira's part with the kiss and whatnot, but also his whole relation with Yumi and the girls, and his "thing of mine ressembling a life"

The Bending of Italics:
at first when I saw the Molly scene during Halloween, I thought the person who was going to come into the room would be Maya, to minimize the impact of the scene since she said she has seen him do much worse (and she would probably understand he didn't actually wanted to do it) but to my surprise, it was Tsuneyo. so I was a bit surprised to see so much time pass without her confronting Akira about what happened but glad to say it wasn't for nothing with the comedy show being so horrible to witness yet understandable from her point of view
the talk itself is self explanatory, why I'm choosing this event is mostly due to Akira's rare expression when faced with his actions that stick with me

All Eyes On Me:
not much to say about this one, I just like the emotion packed speech and how he's clearly changed since the last reset, with the song sensei.mp3 playing in the back which always gives me shivers

All Kinds of People, All Kinds of Things/Caterpillar:
rather funny to include this on my part since Io is one of my least favorite character now but with my current opinion aside, Io's introduction is by far my favorite.
the way the scene plays out, the fear and anxiety, the heartbeat followed by the all sounds music, it's truly a great introduction to her complex, self depracating, contradictory character I grew to despise (and love)

7. Go to developer island and use the same strategy for beating the bonus boss, to make yourself happy
8. For the final boss, the code is in chap4.rpy under label orbfight

There are some calls for flags during the update, but nothing major. Relevant flags are Amifingered, Ayane and/or Tsubasa threesome and Stomachache (this is the big variant). But you don't get locked out of anything, these just change dialogue.

The hexadecimal translation for Tsuneyo's event is "slip" and "hope". The vigenere cipher for Yasu's event is "the walls are closing in".

New outfits can be bought during the puzzle:
Picture messages are from Molly and Noriko:
Now that that's settled, let's get into the puzzle. So, this is one of the worst puzzles in LiL depending on how you'll play it. This is a puzzle that plays like an adventure game. You have to grind currency until you have enough money to get all the items on both shops, to then go on to defeat a number of bosses and clear the puzzle.

First thing is the currency, don't bother fighting the enemies on Fields of Despair. Instead do this, open URM and search for:

now change it to a ridiculous amount:

If you really don't want to cheat you'll have to grind for like a month, so good luck with that I guess. Either way, now go to both shops and buy everything (you'll get kicked out of the shops a few times, just come back until you've bought everything):

Now that you have everything, let's go to field of regrets for the one actual relevant thing here:

go to the suit guy (you don't really have to do this to clear the puzzle) but it's the one interesting bit here. After going through that once we can move on.

Now let's go in the order they appear:

Basically, in each of them you'll have to choose a very specific order of actions (while having all the items) in order to win. If you mess up you'll just respawn at the town. You should however pay attention to the dialogue between attacks and evades because it's interesting lore-wise.

posts.content_html_raw:
A few things about the update, so, first of all:
Sekai's mom is Miu. Which begs a lot of questions, for instance, is Sekai even from our reality? Or is she from a reality where Yuu chose Miu instead of Saki?

Also called the Kaori sex just before the update, but that was more of a joke and we'll take it.
Now onto actual relevant things:

So, basically, replay the entire game. We've gained enough knowledge to understand A LOT OF STUFF again. What follows are minor points on most of the events that maybe people missed on, so I thought to share.
Rubik's Cube: Yasu lost her power by taking medication, which begs the question, why don't the gods want to use her as a hotel room as well?

More than her: From how Maya acts here and her conversation with Akira, it lowers the probability of her being a mastermind as a child by a lot. Ami later aknowledges that she can put Akira on a leash, but I just felt that she was way too fragile in their talk about the past and their dynamic. Also Ami apparently has known all along? (I feel like this might be a retconn, and I'll look into it during next replay).

Action/Inaction: Chika is completely insane, but hey, Yumi has two blessings to fuck Akira, we'll take it. More importantly, Ami has pictures of all the girls in costumes they don't recall. My guess is that this is from previous cycles, is Ami aware of those cycles then? And more importantly, does being locked inside of boxes preserve things between cycles? Is that why Maya had her stuff in boxes?

Empty heart appeal: I think Selebus made a weird choice here. I saw both variations of the scene, and the red path is one of the most uplifting things in LiL - and out of place. I don't know, it just didn't feel like LiL to me. It's like those games in which you have a True End that makes sense, and then you see a Good Ending that was just to make everyone happy even though it made less to no sense. Green path was alright I guess, what I expected more or less. It was nice to see Io recognizing that she pretty much forced the whole thing.

Soon another nightmare/Art of tribadism: Interesting insight into Maya Prime. I am sort of confused as to if Ami is hearing gods or not, but I like this development for her to take Akira back from Niki (it's still early to know if even this one is true though). Also Chika can call him Akira now.

Four walls, a garden: The music made it hard to read again. We still don't know enough to correctly understand this there is nothing.

Friend: So, Pareidolia was a good guy all along (sort of). I mean, he wasn't good, but he was a god and only a god for Akira. This however begs so many questions. Because if he was so weak how come he managed to get an entire season for himself, and what happens to Spring with him gone? Also, who else is inside Kaori? Oh, and Maya not existing has been hinted so many times by so many people now. Mostly by Pareidolia, but Kaori couldn't see Maya earlier and she wasn't being controlled by Pareidolia then.

More importantly, Sekai is very much alive inside Kaori, and to an extent, likely merged with Kaori. The scene of having sex with both of them at the same time, especially after you've watched the happy event, made me feel things for Sekai and Akira's relationship that I didn't think possible. I'm conflicted.

Kittens: The actual sex and Nao-chan just hanging there giving a thumbs up is both hilarious and very thought provoking. What is this being?

Nao-chan's events: So, she sent Akira "home", which is Terminal 22. Which is also where "Maya" sends him during the first reset. So that's sort of confirmation that at the time, she sent him to Terminal 22 as well, to meet Saki in school (so it was way earlier than what he sees with Miu).

Tsuneyo's event was uncomfortable, but also not? I think by the end the "it should have been me" was worth it. Also Sekai was confirmed as a narrator.

Nodoka's event: So, a few minor things. Himawari was trying to save Nodoka, but she slipped out as Pareidolia showed up using Kaori's skin. When she slips it says "redacted has left the chat". The chat. Which puts into perspective what the narration even is. And Nodoka should be gone now, maybe her mind was broken for good or she won't even be there after the events.
Sensei quest has a lot of stuff around it as well, but most importantly, I think what really messed me was the Sekai stuff. Obviously it doesn't excuse the things she did. But man, I felt so much for her character.
A daughter of Yuu, clearly suffering from hearing voices as well, getting beaten by her husband - and it wasn't a fucking lie. She really tried to run with Akira, that part was never a lie. The only time the voices stopped was when she was with Akira, and from what we gather it was because it was corrupting her (and the voices wanted her corrupted as to make herself a hotel for them eventually). Akira says she had episodes for the longest time.

She wanted to get away with him, wait for him to become an adult, marry him, have a house. Yet, why didn't she leave Nozomu? Akira says she made the wrong decision for years, and the whole way she goes about this is obviously wrong. There were many ways she could have made this work, and this really wasn't it. It didn't become clear to me if Ami is Nozomu's or Akira's though.

Also can you imagine if Akira thought that same Ami was Nozomu's child and he ended up having to adopt her more or less? The same Ami that he told Sekai would be the reason for him not to run with her? It's fucking tragedy all around.

My interpretation of it is that Sekai is pregnant with Akira's child, and she finally chose to run away because eventually Nozomu was going to find out that the child wasn't his (maybe that's what killed them both, and tragedy again, because if so it was her remaining in kumon-mi that made her "break" the promise to Akira). She chooses to keep the child exactly because she's Akira's, and that's why she is so adamant on being unable to leave him regardless. It's their child.

As she reveals she's pregnant, she's really shocked about Akira telling her he isn't going to go anywhere with her if she's with her abuser's child. But it sucks because he keeps going about how he has an appropriate love interest here, and he can't just leave on a whim - and I think Sekai realises that if she tells him it is his child, he'll hop on the train with her, and that's the wrong thing to do.

See, the reason as to why I'm able to feel things for her character is that she's a real human here, not a ghost, but an actual person that is complex. She's aware of how much she has put on this child's shoulders and she's refusing to put more. She doesn't want to ruin his chance of a healthy relationship with Niki, she doesn't want to tie him down by forcing him to be a father and... Again, it does not excuse her, but it sells me on the tragedy of it. She actually loved him and seemed to have a conscience regarding what she already put him through and not wanting to add to it (when met with resistance) at the very least.

Edit: Also, it goes to show how Ami knows shit about Nozomu, and the theories about Nozomu being the father of half the town got a lot stronger now. It also fits that they were talking about Nozomu when they said things about a boy growing to make his mission to ruin every flower.

Edit2: If Sekai is Yuu's daughter, then she's Nozomu's sister, and potentially either Akira's sister of aunt (if the theory about Nozomu having sex with Saki holds true). This is getting super convoluted. We might have to revisit the evidence that Yuu is Akira's father, cause at the moment, I think evidence seems more in the way of him being Sekai's father than Akira's (and both seems strange).
Well, there is a lot that is unclear about Sekai and why she remained there for so many years if this was the situation. But yeah, I think this update was really special to me because I see her character in a much much more complex light.

spoilers.title: Sekai
spoilers.html:
A daughter of Yuu, clearly suffering from hearing voices as well, getting beaten by her husband - and it wasn't a fucking lie. She really tried to run with Akira, that part was never a lie. The only time the voices stopped was when she was with Akira, and from what we gather it was because it was corrupting her (and the voices wanted her corrupted as to make herself a hotel for them eventually). Akira says she had episodes for the longest time.

She wanted to get away with him, wait for him to become an adult, marry him, have a house. Yet, why didn't she leave Nozomu? Akira says she made the wrong decision for years, and the whole way she goes about this is obviously wrong. There were many ways she could have made this work, and this really wasn't it. It didn't become clear to me if Ami is Nozomu's or Akira's though.

Also can you imagine if Akira thought that same Ami was Nozomu's child and he ended up having to adopt her more or less? The same Ami that he told Sekai would be the reason for him not to run with her? It's fucking tragedy all around.

My interpretation of it is that Sekai is pregnant with Akira's child, and she finally chose to run away because eventually Nozomu was going to find out that the child wasn't his (maybe that's what killed them both, and tragedy again, because if so it was her remaining in kumon-mi that made her "break" the promise to Akira). She chooses to keep the child exactly because she's Akira's, and that's why she is so adamant on being unable to leave him regardless. It's their child.

As she reveals she's pregnant, she's really shocked about Akira telling her he isn't going to go anywhere with her if she's with her abuser's child. But it sucks because he keeps going about how he has an appropriate love interest here, and he can't just leave on a whim - and I think Sekai realises that if she tells him it is his child, he'll hop on the train with her, and that's the wrong thing to do.

See, the reason as to why I'm able to feel things for her character is that she's a real human here, not a ghost, but an actual person that is complex. She's aware of how much she has put on this child's shoulders and she's refusing to put more. She doesn't want to ruin his chance of a healthy relationship with Niki, she doesn't want to tie him down by forcing him to be a father and... Again, it does not excuse her, but it sells me on the tragedy of it. She actually loved him and seemed to have a conscience regarding what she already put him through and not wanting to add to it (when met with resistance) at the very least.

Edit: Also, it goes to show how Ami knows shit about Nozomu, and the theories about Nozomu being the father of half the town got a lot stronger now. It also fits that they were talking about Nozomu when they said things about a boy growing to make his mission to ruin every flower.

Edit2: If Sekai is Yuu's daughter, then she's Nozomu's sister, and potentially either Akira's sister of aunt (if the theory about Nozomu having sex with Saki holds true). This is getting super convoluted. We might have to revisit the evidence that Yuu is Akira's father, cause at the moment, I think evidence seems more in the way of him being Sekai's father than Akira's (and both seems strange).

Holy fucking shit my dudes, this was one banger of an update. Good thing I just started another play-through of BG3 with the new patch to keep me entertained until the next update drops.

One thing that really got to me was that part about "I was everything you wanted me to be - a scapegoat", "something you could hate so you could stop hating yourself". I'm paraphrasing, but it's pretty much what was said, and this small interaction says a lot of things while also creating even more questions in so little time. So it's basically saying the Concerned one appeared because Akira needed something/someone to blame other than himself, and that it was just a way for him to do things that could easily be disregarded as "He/It made me do it".

At least, this is how I'm understanding this. In a way, this made me think about SH2 with Pyramid Head being a creation of James as a way to punish him until it was no longer needed because of James accepting his actions instead of choosing to ignore them or blaming it on something out of his control as "she died of that stupid sickness". So how exactly has Pareidolia's role come to an end when Akira is still blaming Him/It for many things? While Akira has had some growth, he still blamed everything on Pareidolia, even during that same scene; how does it stop being the scapegoat he needed when, under that same logic, it is still being treated as one?

I do not know if I'm missing something or if it was just more lies or not, but I still found it very interesting nonetheless.

Please feel free to correct me or share your insight, I am far less smart than many of the Lore-Overlords in this forum. Because you used the phrase "epistemic learned helplessness" I'm going to boldly assume you might be able to understand some basic probabilities:

The odds of making a single correct choice are 1/11 or 9%, but needing to get four 1/11 chance choices correct, in the correct order and given those choices might repeat, your odds of clearing a single encounter through random choices are 0.007% or about 15,000:1. I'm not going to do the math for the 6 and 11 choice encounters, but it's ugly. I can't even find an odds converter that goes that low.

Sure, it's not random - the game gives you feedback about what works... until it doesn't.

My point is, other games don't get "critically lambasted due to grinding" because they don't work on math like this, period. Judging by Dragon Quest's wiki, it looks like it has multiple classes for the player to pick, so there are already multiple ways to clear encounters. I'm embarrassed I even have to point that out. Terrible analogy.

Sensei Quest isn't serious, it's a cobbled-together, surreal meta-game joke pushed to the extreme for shock value that ups the ante from other resets that did similar. Lighten up, don't preach about telling ppl to harden the fuck up when any idiot with a notepad can do this "mini"game given enough time.

Not every repetitive task you have the opportunity of wasting a ton of time on is an opportunity to build character, it's usually just an opportunity to waste a ton of time. SO GROW! indeed... out of your boomer phase, please.

posts.content_html_raw:
Aside from being insanely creepy by each update, there are two scenes that got me very confused.

1. A box with Ami's name on it in Ayane's mansion, and with pictures of Noriko and Miku inside. Those are pictures that they don't remember taking, and with costumes they don't recognized.

Not remembering pictures being taken feels small but not recognizing costumes you allegedly wore before seems large. Combining these two, and this might indicate that whatever is in the picture is something that:
1) has never happened to our Noriko and Miku but had happened to other Noriko and Miku (from other cycles).
2) has not happened to our Noriko and Miku yet.
3) Noriko and Miku in those pictures wore costumes we remember, but they are forced to forget about them because LiL demands it.

I didn't think the last option (as in, direct and crude memory tampering) fits here because there are plenty of instances where girls without cosmic perception freely talk about things they did last year without noticing anything bizarre, so a memory wipe specifically about costumes on these two seems very out of nowhere and unnecessary.

However, the first two options also mean "too much", the boxed universe starts cracking and people start receiving information they shouldn't have type of "too much". Especially the first option; there technically shouldn't be other "Noriko and Miku" because Noriko never became a part of the picture again until our Sensei began his journey (of course this will bank on Prime Maya's memory being correct).

Most importantly, why are those in a box with Ami's name on it and why is it there in the Amamiya mansion already when Ami wasn't there yet? Who did that?
(though for the time being I am disregarding these questions because I don't think I am going to get anything reasonable)

2. Ignoring the borderline feelings that Ami is directly challenging the status of New Maya's memories, were these two ever dressed as Madoka and Homura???

I'm not that well-versed in anime anymore and it's been awhile since I watched Madoka Magica, but none of Ami and Maya's custom rang any bell.
1st Halloween: Sailor Moon/Sensei
2nd Halloween: Genshin person/Genshin person
3rd Halloween: IDK/IDK
4th Halloween: Maya/IDK
5th Halloween: some dude/Haruhi

The 3rd one were two characters I don't know but they don't feel like mahou shoujos, and the rest Halloween won't even accommodate the combination Madoka/Homura. More importantly, Maya seemingly doesn't remember Ami and and Ayane dressed as her before and Ami seemingly was testing her about it...What is happening here?

anyway I just want to make sure that these questions isn't just a misunderstand or misremembering that can be fixed by some weebnotes; because to me, these two scenarios are almost like characters talking about things that have never happened before, and Ami is a part of both scenarios.

1. A box with Ami's name on it in Ayane's mansion, and with pictures of Noriko and Miku inside. Those are pictures that they don't remember taking, and with costumes they don't recognized.
...
Most importantly, why are those in a box with Ami's name on it and why is it there in the Amamiya mansion already when Ami wasn't there yet? Who did that?
(though for the time being I am disregarding these questions because I don't think I am going to get anything reasonable)

The implication is that the box has been there for a WHILE.  Which would imply that Ami is aware of the resets, and has been for a very long time.  This may also be a hint that Noriko has been present in past cycles, and Maya had either forgotten (live long enough, and you forget important shit), or it happened before Maya became aware of the resets, or Maya was straight up lying about it.
And also -- Ami is absolutely testing Maya throughout that scene to see if this Maya has any knowledge of the resets.  Those are all VERY loaded questions.

About the boxes, i don't know if any of you played "cross channel" which is a game that sel recommended and this game is about people stuck in a time loop too.

In that game, there's a shrine that keeps you / objects from getting reset at the end of the week.

Blud thinks you should spend your time on "Sensei Quest" when Elden Ring exists.
Click to expand...
It's just strange how the most basic of artistic intentions are lost even upon those who have spent hundreds of hours in a game. I'm imagining someone watching Nostalghia by Tarkvosky and holding fast forward whenever they get bored by an extended metaphorical sequence. I'm imagining someone reading Moby Dick and skipping all the cetology chapters while complaining about how boring whales are. I'm imagining someone listening to an ambient music album and complaining that there isn't a strong enough melody. It just comes off as absurd on the face of it because it reflects engagement on the level of a child playing with toys, one who's entire motive and goal is to temporarily entertain oneself, and one who's method of judgement is how much fun they are feeling in the moment. In a sense it is not wrong to have such a child-like view but I would expect an adult to hold it more quietly and with shame, not proudly proclaiming it for all to see with the arrogance of a teen confidence they understand philosophy on a level deeper than any scholar. I mean, fucking ELDEN RING? What the hell are you talking about? Are you 12 and taking a break from watching your favorite Twitch streamer to post here? Are you going to be halfway through a Dostoevsky then murmur "Eeeh you know what it's actually rather tedious how many pages are dedicated to boring stuff. I could be playing Elden Ring! That would be WAAAY more fun!" Like, what? Do you actually need colorful blocks to absentmindedly stack with one hand the moment any piece of art demands something from you? You approached SENSEI QUEST in particular with a brand of ridiculous thoughtlessness because you had not engaged whatsoever; you acted like it was an impossible problem of math when in reality you can pass it with ease using basic save/load functions any player would be familiar with. Then when this was identified - your post being worthy of no serious response since it came from one who had, functionally, skipped half the pages in a book then complained about how fragmented the plot was - you retreat to something as absurd 'Why do something not fun when you could do something fun?" I mean, that's PRECISELY THE HEDONISM THE ENTIRE GAME IS CRITICIZING? Have you been paying attention for any of the last 300 hours? Are you a fucking utility zombie sucking up pleasure from Lessons in Love while groaning in displeasure and discomfort any time there is a rock in your cum soup? What the hell, man? What the fuck is even going on? That is precisely why the point is... TO GROW! You really gotta grow outta this. And never make a post this ridiculous again.

A few preliminary thoughts about gods in general and our true bro Pareidolia.
1. So, in this update it was revealed that the gods wish to take a ride in people's bodies, and that there are conditions to doing so. It could be that Sekai was plagued by supernatural interference from birth to groom her into a predator, in an effort to corrupt her enough that she became the perfect gate for them - resulting in Kaori.

Furthermore, Nozomu, definitely Yuu, Tsuneyo's father, Ami, Yasu, Tsubasa and others might have gods inside of them from time to time - and if they have gods inside of them while impregnating someone that might result in the cotton tails, and if they're women, that might result in them speading the corruption to a male (Sekai x Akira situation). Basically, Tsuneyo's father might have been a human that was suitable for Wires to reside in, which makes him both Wires and not Wires.

What this changes is that when replaying the game, through the events of say, "somnambula" (Ami's backwards bus ride), Yasu's being creepy, and definitely Kaori's retorts off camera - those are gods. What exactly are the conditions for this corruption to achieve sufficient levels for them to get in is unclear. Why Akira has only had one god inside of him is also unclear (although it is said that they messed with his head constantly). And that HOPE also broke the rules by speaking to him directly through Yasu, and yet there seems to have been no repercussion to that.
2. Now moving on to the second relevant aspect of a god. A god has absolutely no power unless it's given to it. If a god truly has no believer anymore it goes to rest at the bottom of the wishing well until it is eventually reincarnated into a human/or worse. A new theory is that Maya might be such a case, hold that thought and I'll come back to it soon.

When we saw knife boy, we saw how as Sana ended his "legend" by removing all his knives, he ceased to be. That would mean that he was a very very minor "god", and that he was sent to the bottom of the well, or straight up reincarnated on the spot. Given that Sana might be Akira's sister and knife boy is replaced by Akira, then by Sekai (which might also be Sana's sister) makes this case a specific one.

But that aside, the legend part means that the gods are restrained by their very legend. A Calm god has no choice but to be calm, as a Callous god has no choice but to be callous. To not do so would be to risk cancelling its own existance. Furthermore, a being that is "corruption and worms" has no chance but to be so, otherwise she'd disappear altogether. Therefore it's possible that the ghost Sekai we see is also a legend bound to be the manifestation of a predator.

On Sekai, she's in a curious position because she seems to be Kaori. As it was said so many times, she lives. So is Sekai the ghost the same as actual Sekai inside of Kaori? Are there two Sekais? Or just the one that is alive but also able to go around?

Finally on to our bro, Pareidolia. Was he a good guy? I think the answer is wonderfully complex. Pareidolia was the Concerned god, and by abiding his legend, he had no choice but to be concerned. It was an existence summoned out of concern for Akira, one that only existed because of Akira, and until the end was sustained only by Akira. Calling him good would imply that he could be evil, and really he had no choice but to simply be. And he could only be what Akira needed, because at the core he was pure concern for him.

His sacrifice, if true, also abides by his nature. I have to replay in order to take in all his actions, but it seems that he jumped at the chance to talk to Akira face to face in order to properly convey what Akira needed to save himself. Pareidolia was then thrown to the bottom of the well because he failed to be the voice inside of Akira's head, thus cancelling himself in the eyes of his one believer. Well, what was his plan throughout this whole season?

Other gods seemed to listen to his commands, and Himawari is more or less confirmed in my eyes as the one that ended the auto-pilot early given her reaction to being face-to-face with Pareidolia. In fact, all Pareidolia's actions might have been the greatest tsundere arc ever, doing everything for Akira and yet having to play the villain. This is clearly the case during the auto-pilot, and maybe Himawari pissed off Pareidolia because he really was concerned about Akira during the auto-pilot. I feel like next update we'll learn more about Himawari's plan so I'll let that rest for now though.
3. Finally, Kaori. Well, Kaori is god. Multiple gods in fact. When she enters New Hope's church, Yasu says in hexadecimal that god has arrived.

What this means for the rest of the game I have no idea. Apparently there was no direct interference from the gods inside of her with Akira for the longest time, and yet it would be really funny is in the downtime the gods were using a laptop from Kaori's body to log in as users
4. Well, to finish up, let's talk about Maya. Pareidolia says Akira stole a color and corrupted her. Long Maya says that Maya is a result of chance, not clockwork. Ghost Sekai hates her with a passion that is way overblown. And Kaori cannot even see Maya. Well, what if Maya isn't human?

There was something about what New Maya said this update that sprung this line of thinking, that if Akira didn't need her anymore she had no reason to be. Well, that's just like what was explained to us. Going back to many things said about Maya "some say she should never have been here in the first place". And her connection to the idea of a stray (god?) How she fit perfectly with what Akira needed when he needed it.

Pareidolia says it was Akira that pulled him up from the bottom of the well, but that he has no idea how he did it. That likely took place during his childhood, so when Maya showed up, it wouldn't have been the first time he "saved" a forgotten god. Or maybe he even created one.

Those are just some of the ideas right now on my mind, maybe that springs a discussion in some way.

Regarding Maya:
Fallen Angel theory -- Maya is a divine entity who willingly forsook her divinity to be with Akira. Support: The Altair and Vega story. To use the language of the recent update, she defied her Legend, yet continues to exist. Since this cannot be by the rules the gods play by, she is one who should not and can not exist. Yet she does.
Illusion theory -- Inspired by her name, this implies that Maya isn't real, and never has been. She's something that Akira willed into existence by sheer need, and his conviction was such that everyone else perceives her as well. As a divine host, Kaori pierces the illusion and does not realize she's there.

I lean more toward the Fallen Angel theory, because Kaori in this update made it clear that she knows that Maya exists, but that Maya shouldn't exist.

The things about her that drive Akira's trauma are external from Kaori and wholly independent of her. they represent the two directions her life might have taken had it not been cut short.

spoilers.title: taking a ride
spoilers.html:
1. So, in this update it was revealed that the gods wish to take a ride in people's bodies, and that there are conditions to doing so. It could be that Sekai was plagued by supernatural interference from birth to groom her into a predator, in an effort to corrupt her enough that she became the perfect gate for them - resulting in Kaori.

Furthermore, Nozomu, definitely Yuu, Tsuneyo's father, Ami, Yasu, Tsubasa and others might have gods inside of them from time to time - and if they have gods inside of them while impregnating someone that might result in the cotton tails, and if they're women, that might result in them speading the corruption to a male (Sekai x Akira situation). Basically, Tsuneyo's father might have been a human that was suitable for Wires to reside in, which makes him both Wires and not Wires.

What this changes is that when replaying the game, through the events of say, "somnambula" (Ami's backwards bus ride), Yasu's being creepy, and definitely Kaori's retorts off camera - those are gods. What exactly are the conditions for this corruption to achieve sufficient levels for them to get in is unclear. Why Akira has only had one god inside of him is also unclear (although it is said that they messed with his head constantly). And that HOPE also broke the rules by speaking to him directly through Yasu, and yet there seems to have been no repercussion to that.

spoilers.title: the legend aspect and why our bro was concerned
spoilers.html:
2. Now moving on to the second relevant aspect of a god. A god has absolutely no power unless it's given to it. If a god truly has no believer anymore it goes to rest at the bottom of the wishing well until it is eventually reincarnated into a human/or worse. A new theory is that Maya might be such a case, hold that thought and I'll come back to it soon.

When we saw knife boy, we saw how as Sana ended his "legend" by removing all his knives, he ceased to be. That would mean that he was a very very minor "god", and that he was sent to the bottom of the well, or straight up reincarnated on the spot. Given that Sana might be Akira's sister and knife boy is replaced by Akira, then by Sekai (which might also be Sana's sister) makes this case a specific one.

But that aside, the legend part means that the gods are restrained by their very legend. A Calm god has no choice but to be calm, as a Callous god has no choice but to be callous. To not do so would be to risk cancelling its own existance. Furthermore, a being that is "corruption and worms" has no chance but to be so, otherwise she'd disappear altogether. Therefore it's possible that the ghost Sekai we see is also a legend bound to be the manifestation of a predator.

On Sekai, she's in a curious position because she seems to be Kaori. As it was said so many times, she lives. So is Sekai the ghost the same as actual Sekai inside of Kaori? Are there two Sekais? Or just the one that is alive but also able to go around?

Finally on to our bro, Pareidolia. Was he a good guy? I think the answer is wonderfully complex. Pareidolia was the Concerned god, and by abiding his legend, he had no choice but to be concerned. It was an existence summoned out of concern for Akira, one that only existed because of Akira, and until the end was sustained only by Akira. Calling him good would imply that he could be evil, and really he had no choice but to simply be. And he could only be what Akira needed, because at the core he was pure concern for him.

His sacrifice, if true, also abides by his nature. I have to replay in order to take in all his actions, but it seems that he jumped at the chance to talk to Akira face to face in order to properly convey what Akira needed to save himself. Pareidolia was then thrown to the bottom of the well because he failed to be the voice inside of Akira's head, thus cancelling himself in the eyes of his one believer. Well, what was his plan throughout this whole season?

Other gods seemed to listen to his commands, and Himawari is more or less confirmed in my eyes as the one that ended the auto-pilot early given her reaction to being face-to-face with Pareidolia. In fact, all Pareidolia's actions might have been the greatest tsundere arc ever, doing everything for Akira and yet having to play the villain. This is clearly the case during the auto-pilot, and maybe Himawari pissed off Pareidolia because he really was concerned about Akira during the auto-pilot. I feel like next update we'll learn more about Himawari's plan so I'll let that rest for now though.

It's just strange how the most basic of artistic intentions are lost even upon those who have spent hundreds of hours in a game. I'm imagining someone watching Nostalghia by Tarkvosky and holding fast forward whenever they get bored by an extended metaphorical sequence. I'm imagining someone reading Moby Dick and skipping all the cetology chapters while complaining about how boring whales are. I'm imagining someone listening to an ambient music album and complaining that there isn't a strong enough melody. It just comes off as absurd on the face of it because it reflects engagement on the level of a child playing with toys, one who's entire motive and goal is to temporarily entertain oneself, and one who's method of judgement is how much fun they are feeling in the moment. In a sense it is not wrong to have such a child-like view but I would expect an adult to hold it more quietly and with shame, not proudly proclaiming it for all to see with the arrogance of a teen confidence they understand philosophy on a level deeper than any scholar. I mean, fucking ELDEN RING? What the hell are you talking about? Are you 12 and taking a break from watching your favorite Twitch streamer to post here? Are you going to be halfway through a Dostoevsky then murmur "Eeeh you know what it's actually rather tedious how many pages are dedicated to boring stuff. I could be playing Elden Ring! That would be WAAAY more fun!" Like, what? Do you actually need colorful blocks to absentmindedly stack with one hand the moment any piece of art demands something from you? You approached SENSEI QUEST in particular with a brand of ridiculous thoughtfulness because you had not engaged whatsoever; you acted like it was an impossible problem of math when in reality you can pass it with ease you basic save/load functions. Then when this was identified - your post being worthy of no serious response since it came from one who had, functionally, skipped half the pages in a book then complained about how fragmented the plot was - you retreat to something as absurd 'Why do something not fun when you could do something fun?" I mean, that's PRECISELY THE HEDONISM THE ENTIRE GAME IS CRITICIZING? Have you been paying attention for any of the last 300 hours? Moonflare said:
4. Well, to finish up, let's talk about Maya. Pareidolia says Akira stole a color and corrupted her. Long Maya says that Maya is a result of chance, not clockwork. Ghost Sekai hates her with a passion that is way overblown. And Kaori cannot even see Maya. Well, what if Maya isn't human?

There was something about what New Maya said this update that sprung this line of thinking, that if Akira didn't need her anymore she had no reason to be. Well, that's just like what was explained to us. Going back to many things said about Maya "some say she should never have been here in the first place". And her connection to the idea of a stray (god?) How she fit perfectly with what Akira needed when he needed it.

Pareidolia says it was Akira that pulled him up from the bottom of the well, but that he has no idea how he did it. That likely took place during his childhood, so when Maya showed up, it wouldn't have been the first time he "saved" a forgotten god. Or maybe he even created one.
Click to expand...
I don't have anything clever to add, just remembered that at various points in game Maya was called a "Dream Baby", as in being conceived in a dream two times by Happy Ami, as well as "honorary angel" by her hexadecimal self.

Moonflare said:
Basically, this update introduced the idea that Yuu (Akira's assumed father) is also the father of Sekai (whose mother is Miu, the highschool friend of Yuu and Saki). That would mean Sekai is half-sister to both Nozomu and Akira. There are way more complicated family trees, but these are born out of speculation, those two are the currently supported in-game.

Edit: A minor point we haven't addressed yet is that the family name Sekai despised is either Arakawa or Miyahara. That she chose to marry into the Arakawa family would suggest her original family name was Miyahara though. Also the house by the lake is Sekai's family home.
Click to expand...
Again, just randomly remembered that in some Happy Scene, hex Maya actually addressed Sensei as either "World", or "Sekai" for reasons I still don't understand.

lolbob3 said:
I feel like the millionPC h scene flags will be used by sel to fk with ppl who cheated for PC, even if you use URM I would just buy all other items and leave the h scenes there. As by doing it normally it would take like 5~ish hours just for 1, there's no way the flags be used for good.
Click to expand...
It's possible that it was bait, but if so, it's also kind of whatever. Someone that is able to use URM to make it through the sequence would find it to be a piece of cake to simply disable whatever flag he could set up as a trap. I echo what Bingoogus has said before, all of this Selebus dumb crap only affects, ironically, his little cult of "if you share things about the reset I'll ban you from discord".

We aren't really affected by any of it, my walkthrough was out way before most of the folks would have gotten to sensei-quest, and I took a really long time playing through the update. So, I mean, who's this even for? We have walkthrough mods, URM to skip any and every grind, view replays the way they were meant to be replayed, puzzle answers, basically everything he preaches against just a few hours from release.

He could embrace his community instead of some self-indulgent selection of worthy ones, but instead he doubles down on making idiotic puzzles even when it's kind of a general opinion that even people that like puzzles would prefer it to be questions that reward you for knowing the lore instead of some random shit. I'm not even sorry to say it at this point, having to waste your time trying a thousand combinations through every boss in this puzzle adds absolutely nothing to whatever immersion crap people tell me when I say the replays should work properly.

It's just very sad how a writer that is so good is also so blind to some basics about game-design, and it only gets worse as time goes on. Try to open the restart event right now to see the end of the update, and you'll have to do the boss fight again even though it should be part of the reset puzzle instead

Which under the light of this update could either be 1. a walking hotel for gods, in Yuu's case, and what Pareidolia implied in his last conversation; 2. or possibly a god in Nozomu's case? posts.content_html_raw:
Before I get into the wall of text, let me say that New Maya speaks for us all.
Starting off with some lore stuff that I think is important but easy to miss.
Sensei & Makoto, Ayane, and New Maya are each thrown back in time to a different Halloween. But I'm not sure any of these are from our timeline. Ayane's definitely isn't.
Restart:

"Everyone" from Chapter 3:
Ami and Molly have swapped places I presume because the rape never happened, and this Sensei sat through Ayane's rehearsals which also never happened.

The other two timelines are less certain, but in both we overhear Ayane making the same joke that we didn't hear in the original events.

I'm really interested to see how Sel handles this in 0.45. Somehow they have to get back to the main timeline unless he wants to abandon the character development for all of the other girls.
In the Tsuneyo event we get the revelation that young Sekai was a regular at Tojo Ramen.
We finally get a connection between Wires and the Arakawa family, completing the trinity: Nozomu for obvious reasons and Pareidolia because he's in... basically all of their heads? Yuu, Akira, apparently Sekai, probably Nozomu based on some clues from 0.43, probably Ami, Sana if you believe she's an Arakawa (I do), maybe Nodoka and Rin if you believe they're Arakawas (I do).

Just before Sekai shows up, Tsuneyo hears a mystery voice which is probably her.
The agreement part is interesting: maybe an agreement between the gods that Tsuneyo won't be messed with.

More interesting though is the implication that the speaker was molested by a man. There was an old Sekai poem that also suggested this:
(Though if you want to get real tinfoil, "girl with broken wings" is the exact phrase Nodoka used to describe Otoha)

So connecting these things: Sekai went to Tojo Ramen when she was young (and references "whoring herself out"), Sekai was sexually abused, and she brought that fact up apropos of nothing just before talking to Tsuneyo about her father. How tinfoil is it to think that Mr. Tojo might have been her abuser?

One other strange thing here: Purple Hat Guy aka Tsuneyo's Friend just watches as she gets violated. Does that mean that Wires is fine with what's happening? The fuck?
Sekai is driving a yellow car.

Sensei Quest ends with Meowri's car getting T-boned (the worst letter), which happened to the white car in the accident, probably indicating it was Kaori's family.

So was "Ami" just lying in "Rain King" when she said that "the white car was ours"? Which could mean that Maya actually killed a "kitten", i.e. had an abortion.

Also, Akira thinking about driving Sekai around might be foreshadowing that he was driving in the accident, which was kind of hinted at in "First Contact".
I'm not even sure how to lead into this one, so just look at this comparison:

Beyond the smile and head tilt, we've even got the same lens flares, all while talking about leaving Akira. And Sara keeps smiling in this weird way in this one short section of the scene, something she never does any other time.

In context this is about Sara becoming Ami's new mother figure, and thus replacing Sekai. So maybe that's the only parallel being drawn here... but surely there's some deeper meaning?
This one will probably sound a bit tinfoil. This is my understanding of the symbolic connection between gods and colors:
  • Green is Wires, reinforced by his connection with Maya.
  • Red is Pareidolia, reinforced by his connection with Sekai.
  • Blue is USER1, not to be confused with the light blue of Himawari/Ayane. There's no blue moon because Nozomu is fucking dead and HOPE's a fake (how's that as a teaser for a future post).
  • Purple is USER4, reinforced by their connection to Nao, whose color is purple according to Kaori.
Just before he fucks off, Pareidolia shows Sensei an image with a "happy family" of stick figures representing the trinity: red, green, and blue. There's no stick figure for USER4, but there is a white cat.

I wrote before about how the white cat shows up in some events where characters act uncharacteristically. At this point, I'm leaning toward Maya in "Trinity Pt. I", Kaori in "Wither", and Makoto in "T is for Time" all being manifestations of USER4 - which is doubly interesting because I think whoever appears as Maya in Trinity is the game's primary narrator.

Right after the happy family image, the colors are used again in Nao's mugs on the roof.

Red, green, and purple for the three gods that now exist - no blue because, again, there is currently no USER1.
And here's the rest of my observations. Sorry no context for these because I didn't want to upload a million screenshots.
  • Ghost Sekai praises what Nodoka's doing, then later Pareidolia (apparently) erases her. First sign I've seen that they might disagree on something (though maybe it's just "I respect what she's doing but I can't allow it to continue.")
  • Sekai was about to reveal something about Nodoka to Sensei before being cut off. Revelation that Yuu's her dad?
  • Holy fuck Chika is insane.
  • Ami has a box of Halloween photos at Ayane's house for some reason? And Noriko/Miku don't recognize the costumes, implying they're from a previous cycle - I had suspected that Maya Prime lied about Noriko never showing up before, this would confirm it.
  • The narrator says New Maya doesn't care much for gods, so it wasn't just Maya Prime becoming jaded after millions of years. Calls into question how the Maya in "Baby Finches" wanted to tell Sensei about Wires.
  • The narrator for the Ami/Maya events was probably Sekai - only other real option I see is Ami herself. I think that's the first time that we have confirmation of Sekai narrating events instead of just talking directly to Sensei.
  • I did not think it would be possible for me to be creeped out by the prospect of an Ami+Maya threesome, but here we are.
  • Ami and Maya being compared to the sun and moon respectively probably means something, but I can't think of what at the moment.
  • I'm going to need to read through it again, but the narrator in "Infinity House" seems like they're talking about Akira's childhood. Important points:
    • "Before he left": might suggest that Yuu left the family rather than dying.
    • A pair of twins wearing purple are apparently important - might be connected to the mysterious twin mentions early in the game.
    • The narrator speaks like they were also there.
    • The narrator mentions "a grandparent's infinity house". Could be Ami talking about Yuu/Saki/Miu, could maybe be Himawari talking about the Amamiya house, but I'm not sure how to fit this with the above.
  • In Chapter 3 Yasu welcomed spring as something that Hope was bringing back, now she calls it something that shouldn't exist. Is she aware she was being manipulated? Possibly because of the Priestess of Fallen Snow message.
  • The narrator implies Mr. Tojo is dead - increased smell at Tojo Ramen, no more blackouts. Though there may have been a recent blackout - in TSS III there's the blown transformer sound which causes Pegasus to disappear.
  • Apparently Maya Prime was getting freaky with Ami on a regular basis. Didn't see that one coming.
  • It's confirmed that Nodoka was affected by her mother's books - perhaps a waterlogged journal? - but also that she was influenced by a second set of words - Sekai's writings?
  • Apparently the dead body in the upside down house's boiler room is Shiori. I know time is funny in different planes, but it's odd that she's Nodoka's evil twin and Himawari's coworker, both referred to in the present tense after the body was first referenced. Also, I was completely convinced the body was Sekai for reasons that I'll probably still talk about in a future post.
  • RIP Nodoka. I wonder how completely she was erased - will she cease to exist even in the past, like Sensei has been threatened with? Or will she return as a "normal girl"?
  • Nodoka is erased by Pareidolia under Pareidolia's red moon. Maya Prime was erased under Wires's green moon. Could that mean that Wires was actually behind her death?
  • Sensei's phone had no service when Ami called him at the school.
  • Apparently Terminal 22 is the world of Nothing is Beautiful, and was Sensei's original home. This confuses me a lot:
    • Sensei isn't from a "real world" outside of the terminals
    • The terminals aren't just alternate timelines for Sensei, Terminal 22 is in the past. Would any of the girls even exist there?
    • What does that mean for Ami looking forward to 24? Would it be an entirely new cast of characters?
  • It seems to be confirmed that Sekai is the daughter of Yuu and Miu. In addition to the conversation with Miu, there was a narrated poem mentioning "Mother's lake". I kind of hate this revelation since it means she was married to one half-brother and having sex with another. Also, what does this mean for her maiden name? The one that she apparently wouldn't answer to in school?
  • Not sure what it means, but the colors on the roof are the exact same as the first reset.
  • I don't believe a single word that Pareidolia said, especially that he's gone now. Too much of the supernatural plot has been set up as a conflict between him and Wires for that to be true. But if he somehow is gone, I would guess that Sekai is the new god of spring.
  • One thing he said that did strike me was that gods can turn into humans - is that what happened to USER4?
  • We got confirmation that Nozomu Arakawa was a piece of shit, can't say I'm really surprised, whether it's good for the story or not remains to be seen. What I found more interesting about this event is that Sekai's personality seems just completely different from what we've seen from Ghost Sekai, YaSekai, SeKaori, etc. I get she's really emotional and that even bad people can have tender moments (just look at Akira), but this still makes me wonder if we're finally seeing the "real Sekai".
  • Sensei died in a terrible accident with Meowri and was only able to return because the game was rewritten. Mirroring how Kaori actually died in the accident and was only brought back after the past was rewritten?
  • I hesitate to bring this up because I hate the theory, but any believers in "Sensei is secretly gay" are absolutely feasting with this update.
I think there's a lot I missed, I'm looking forward to reading through this update again.

Ami and Maya being compared to the sun and moon respectively probably means something, but I can't think of what at the moment.
I'm going to need to read through it again, but the narrator in "Infinity House" seems like they're talking about Akira's childhood. Important points:
"Before he left": might suggest that Yuu left the family rather than dying.
A pair of twins wearing purple are apparently important - might be connected to the mysterious twin mentions early in the game.
The narrator speaks like they were also there.
The narrator mentions "a grandparent's infinity house". Could be Ami talking about Yuu/Saki/Miu, could maybe be Himawari talking about the Amamiya house, but I'm not sure how to fit this with the above.
In Chapter 3 Yasu welcomed spring as something that Hope was bringing back, now she calls it something that shouldn't exist. Is she aware she was being manipulated? Possibly because of the Priestess of Fallen Snow message.
The narrator implies Mr. Tojo is dead - increased smell at Tojo Ramen, no more blackouts. Though there may have been a recent blackout - in TSS III there's the blown transformer sound which causes Pegasus to disappear.
Apparently Maya Prime was getting freaky with Ami on a regular basis. Didn't see that one coming.
It's confirmed that Nodoka was affected by her mother's books - perhaps a waterlogged journal?  - but also that she was influenced by a second set of words - Sekai's writings?
Apparently the dead body in the upside down house's boiler room is Shiori. I know time is funny in different planes, but it's odd that she's Nodoka's evil twin and Himawari's coworker, both referred to in the present tense after the body was first referenced. Also, I was completely convinced the body was Sekai for reasons that I'll probably still talk about in a future post.
RIP Nodoka. I wonder how completely she was erased - will she cease to exist even in the past, like Sensei has been threatened with? Or will she return as a "normal girl"?
Nodoka is erased by Pareidolia under Pareidolia's red moon. Maya Prime was erased under Wires's green moon. Could that mean that Wires was actually behind her death?
Sensei's phone had no service when Ami called him at the school.
Apparently Terminal 22 is the world of Nothing is Beautiful, and was Sensei's original home. This confuses me a lot:
Sensei isn't from a "real world" outside of the terminals
The terminals aren't just alternate timelines for Sensei, Terminal 22 is in the past. Would any of the girls even exist there?
What does that mean for Ami looking forward to 24? Would it be an entirely new cast of characters?
It seems to be confirmed that Sekai is the daughter of Yuu and Miu. In addition to the conversation with Miu, there was a narrated poem mentioning "Mother's lake". I kind of hate this revelation since it means she was married to one half-brother and having sex with another. Also, what does this mean for her maiden name? The one that she apparently wouldn't answer to in school?
Not sure what it means, but the colors on the roof are the exact same as the first reset.
Spoiler
I don't believe a single word that Pareidolia said, especially that he's gone now. Too much of the supernatural plot has been set up as a conflict between him and Wires for that to be true. But if he somehow is gone, I would guess that Sekai is the new god of spring.
One thing he said that did strike me was that gods can turn into humans - is that what happened to USER4?
We got confirmation that Nozomu Arakawa was a piece of shit, can't say I'm really surprised, whether it's good for the story or not remains to be seen. What I found more interesting about this event is that Sekai's personality seems just
completely
different from what we've seen from Ghost Sekai, YaSekai, SeKaori, etc. I get she's really emotional and that even bad people can have tender moments (just look at Akira), but this still makes me wonder if we're finally seeing the "real Sekai".
Sensei died in a terrible accident with Meowri and was only able to return because the game was rewritten. Mirroring how Kaori actually died in the accident and was only brought back after the past was rewritten?
I hesitate to bring this up because I hate the theory, but any believers in "Sensei is secretly gay" are absolutely
feasting
with this update.
I think there's a lot I missed, I'm looking forward to reading through this update again.

I feel like it's treading dangerously close to Selebus not knowing what he's writing about and just adding stuff. We're still far from that, but with every update I feel like we get closer, and I really hope Himawari's plan will allay a lot of that worry by providing us with some form of overall explanation that ties things together cause, at the moment, it's a mess. The moment you start thinking about "proper game design," "immersion," etc you've already lost because you're on the completely wrong track. It is blindingly obvious that the purpose of the puzzles is not to provide a fun and engaging experience. They reflect that fact that the further one goes into Lessons in Love, the more the world rejects the player (this goes for both the literal player and Sensei). It becomes increasingly hard to progress, increasingly unfun, increasingly grindy - it would be reductive to state there is only one ludonarrative purpose for this, but that is the design. The artistic purpose. It is an experience the developer is attempting to convey through mechanic. It is axiomatic to say that "video games should be fun," "puzzles should test innovative thinking," etc, which is to say that they are not fundamental truths - they are platitudes liable to become thought-terminating cliches. Looking at systems clearly designed to reject the player and make their life difficult then complaining about how they aren't fun enough is so foolish I balk that one so invested in the story and theory-crafting would be so blind to this point. Let us examine once again Moby Dick.

https://melville.electroniclibrary.org/editions/versions-of-moby-dick/32-cetology

In chapter 32 there is a lengthy chapter devoted to the physiology of whales. This is a highly dull chapter to read and a well-known roadblock for prospective readers of the work (yet I must explain it in detail here because it is dubious whether any poster in this thread has ready even such a fundamental cornerstone a literature such as Moby Dick). However, in this context of literature removed from "a porn game that should be fun and get my pee pee hard," we see immediately how foolish it would be to critique it from a lens as those critiquing SENSEI QUEST and other resets are. Can you imagine going to Melville and saying, good sir, it is all well and good that you wish your novel to be a testimony to every aspect of whales from the physical aspects of their being to the mythological image they come to represent, but this chapter was quite dull! Could you not make it a bit more fun and exciting? In fact, quite a few of your chapters could be shaved down, let's have more action scenes and whale hunting, you would really get more readers that way! It is rather obnoxious that you should even think to force me to read some boring chapter on whales when I can in fact simply flip the pages! Do you not know I will just flip the pages? You are not listening to me sir, I am telling you to make your novel more fun for me!

It really is just that simple: think, for one moment, the purpose. Now, it is entirely fair if you look at Lessons in Love rejecting the player and making it increasingly hard/unpleasant to make progress as a foolish thing. Some people think whales are dumb. However, this is not what is happening. The angle of attack is so completely off base it's like one is seeing reality on an entirely different level. Like one's mind is so boxed in by platitudes that any time something isn't fun and satisfying their every urge for what they want it to be that the entire world starts to seem wrong. How can one profess themselves to be a deep thinker, a lover of thought and figuring things out, so proud of each theory and confirmed idea, if such basic mental walls blind them so deeply? Such that they look upon a rock and see a mountain, or they look upon a mountain and see a rock? You really think for one fucking second the puzzles are meant to be fun tests of knowledge? You really think they contain anything but spite and hostility? You really think this is supposed to be a good time? You really think that 'all media must be fun' is a God-like axiom that subsumes all other purposes one may have? What? WHAT???????????? The populace is rendered infants before the most basic and blunt artistic purpose which itself is literally stated directly over and over. Shocking! Nothing really is beautiful!

I lowkey didn't like this twist, that Pareidolia was actually being thoughtful for Akira in his own concerning way. I got similar feelings when reading some manga from the early 2000s where antagonists were later revealed to be "the good guys with bad methods who's done horrible things to protagonists for the sake of some big pictures". It's too forced with minimal justification, and thus my attitude is more or less the same as Akira (as in, "yea yea sure sure go fuck yourself").

Regardless, his final words lead me to attempt to justify for him, focusing on whether Pareidolia in the past events only pretended to be the bad guy in times of need or is still capable of deliberately committing heinous deeds so that Akira can hate him instead of himself (in a yandere sense I guess). Essentially, I want to see whether his last words can be used to figure out what Pareidolia did or didn't do, all under the assumption that Pareidolia, in his final moments, is indeed truthful.

If Pareidolia only pretends to be the bad guy in times of Akira's need, that means Pareidolia should not be the cause of said detriment; he should not be the one that threw Akira on Maya Prime and had her killed. Otherwise, it becomes a laughable matter where you attempt to use questionable methods to solve a problem YOU yourself created for somebody else.

If Pareidolia is aiming for Akira's general trend of self-loathing and would not hesitate to perform drastic measures to transfer Akira's self hate to the God of Concern, then Pareidolia might still be the one responsible for Prime Maya's death, though in this case it's less of a scapegoat but more of a distraction. Alas, I didn't think this route make much sense because this feels so out of proportion and, at the same time, willingly overlooks the dramatic rise to power and nature reveal of Pareidolia immediately after Maya Prime's death.

An extension from both of these routes is that Pareidolia's claim might also clear his name in all of his past allegations such as Molly's rape arc. To me, it makes no sense as a self-proclaimed scapegoat to create scenarios that might actively initiate Akira's self hatred without announcing the mastermind's name loud and clear to Akira. This is in contrast to Karin's incident, an event took place after Maya Prime's death and where Pareidolia made his presence known.
(I assume that Pareidolia's true goal and nature has always been consistent throughout; otherwise it makes even less sense to say something like "I want to help you in Ch4 but I just wanted to rape girls in Ch2")

PrincessEuphy said:
The moment you start thinking about "proper game design," "immersion," etc you've already lost because you're on the completely wrong track. It is blindingly obvious that the purpose of the puzzles is not to provide a fun and engaging experience. They reflect that fact that the further one goes into Lessons in Love, the more the world rejects the player (this goes for both the literal player and Sensei). It becomes increasingly hard to progress, increasingly unfun, increasingly grindy - it would be reductive to state there is only one ludonarrative purpose for this, but that is the design. The artistic purpose. It is an experience the developer is attempting to convey through mechanic. It is axiomatic to say that "video games should be fun," "puzzles should test innovative thinking," etc, which is to say that they are not fundamental truths - they are platitudes liable to become thought-terminating cliches. Looking at systems clearly designed to reject the player and make their life difficult then complaining about how they aren't fun enough is so foolish I balk that one so invested in the story and theory-crafting would be so blind to this point. Let us examine once again Moby Dick.

https://melville.electroniclibrary.org/editions/versions-of-moby-dick/32-cetology

In chapter 32 there is a lengthy chapter devoted to the physiology of whales. This is a highly dull chapter to read and a well-known roadblock for prospective readers of the work (yet I must explain it in detail here because it is dubious whether any poster in this thread has ready even such a fundamental cornerstone a literature such as Moby Dick). However, in this context of literature removed from "a porn game that should be fun and get my pee pee hard," we see immediately how foolish it would be to critique it from a lens as those critiquing SENSEI QUEST and other resets are. Can you imagine going to Melville and saying, good sir, it is all well and good that you wish your novel to be a testimony to every aspect of whales from the physical aspects of their being to the mythological image they come to represent, but this chapter was quite dull! Could you not make it a bit more fun and exciting? In fact, quite a few of your chapters could be shaved down, let's have more action scenes and whale hunting, you would really get more readers that way! It is rather obnoxious that you should even think to force me to read some boring chapter on whales when I can in fact simply flip the pages! Do you not know I will just flip the pages? You are not listening to me sir, I am telling you to make your novel more fun for me!

It really is just that simple: think, for one moment, the purpose. Now, it is entirely fair if you look at Lessons in Love rejecting the player and making it increasingly hard/unpleasant to make progress as a foolish thing. Some people think whales are dumb. However, this is not what is happening. The angle of attack is so completely off base it's like one is seeing reality on an entirely different level. Like one's mind is so boxed in by platitudes that any time something isn't fun and satisfying their every urge for what they want it to be that the entire world starts to seem wrong. How can one profess themselves to be a deep thinker, a lover of thought and figuring things out, so proud of each theory and confirmed idea, if such basic mental walls blind them so deeply? Such that they look upon a rock and see a mountain, or they look upon a mountain and see a rock? You really think for one fucking second the puzzles are meant to be fun tests of knowledge? You really think they contain anything but spite and hostility? You really think this is supposed to be a good time? You really think that 'all media must be fun' is a God-like axiom that subsumes all other purposes one may have? What? WHAT???????????? The populace is rendered infants before the most basic and blunt artistic purpose which itself is literally stated directly over and over. Shocking! Nothing really is beautiful!
Click to expand...
Just because there's an artistic vision doesn't mean the vision isn't shit

PrincessEuphy said:
It's just strange how the most basic of artistic intentions are lost even upon those who have spent hundreds of hours in a game. I'm imagining someone watching Nostalghia by Tarkvosky and holding fast forward whenever they get bored by an extended metaphorical sequence. I'm imagining someone reading Moby Dick and skipping all the cetology chapters while complaining about how boring whales are. I'm imagining someone listening to an ambient music album and complaining that there isn't a strong enough melody. It just comes off as absurd on the face of it because it reflects engagement on the level of a child playing with toys, one who's entire motive and goal is to temporarily entertain oneself, and one who's method of judgement is how much fun they are feeling in the moment. In a sense it is not wrong to have such a child-like view but I would expect an adult to hold it more quietly and with shame, not proudly proclaiming it for all to see with the arrogance of a teen confidence they understand philosophy on a level deeper than any scholar. I mean, fucking ELDEN RING? What the hell are you talking about? Are you 12 and taking a break from watching your favorite Twitch streamer to post here? Are you going to be halfway through a Dostoevsky then murmur "Eeeh you know what it's actually rather tedious how many pages are dedicated to boring stuff. I could be playing Elden Ring! That would be WAAAY more fun!" Like, what? Do you actually need colorful blocks to absentmindedly stack with one hand the moment any piece of art demands something from you? You approached SENSEI QUEST in particular with a brand of ridiculous thoughtlessness because you had not engaged whatsoever; you acted like it was an impossible problem of math when in reality you can pass it with ease using basic save/load functions any player would be familiar with. Then when this was identified - your post being worthy of no serious response since it came from one who had, functionally, skipped half the pages in a book then complained about how fragmented the plot was - you retreat to something as absurd 'Why do something not fun when you could do something fun?" I mean, that's PRECISELY THE HEDONISM THE ENTIRE GAME IS CRITICIZING? Have you been paying attention for any of the last 300 hours? Are you a fucking utility zombie sucking up pleasure from Lessons in Love while groaning in displeasure and discomfort any time there is a rock in your cum soup? What the hell, man? What the fuck is even going on? That is precisely why the point is... TO GROW! You really gotta grow outta this. And never make a post this ridiculous again.
Click to expand...
- Lessons in Love isn't Moby Dick, man. It's not Nostalghia, it's not Dostoevsky, it's not even Breaking Bad. Perhaps it comes closest to these in the context of western adult visual novels (something LiL tries not to be), but these are even more outrageously absurd comparisons than Dragon Quest. LiL has an interesting amount of depth, a huge amount of potential, and can be charming in its own way, but for as long as the developer decides to keep showing his ass by doing shit like self-inserting his own petty grievances - not around things like "boy the lines at the DMV sure are long," but literally things like "I treated this one specific person at Patreon like a fucking idiot and they banned me for it, how unfair" - it can never be taken even remotely seriously. The developer's antagonism towards his audience, resentment of the business model in the industry he exists in, and his own personal dissatisfaction with his income are all completely unmasked and spoken verbatim by his characters. The funny thing is is that you can actually do those kinds of things in a work like this that's intended to be meta and surrealist, but Selly goes so overboard with it that it only serves to directly paint him as a childish narcissist megalomaniac and is only worthy of an eyeroll. The reason why so few people on the outside knew that James Corden, Oprah, or Ellen Degeneres are such assholes is because they maintained professional distance. There's very little here.

- You have never played Elden Ring and are not familiar with it at all, especially if you think that's what 12 year olds are watching on Twitch. Your original argument hinged upon the completion of ostensibly arduous tasks in a "simple RPG" in order to gain some reward at the end. Soulslike action RPGs, which Elden Ring is the pinnacle of, are the standout examples of this exact philosophy in video gaming. They're not the dopamine firehoses most people would rather play than do homework or read a book unless those people are absolute chads. They're games that you need to lock into and settle down for a long haul of frustration and adversity, and only give you delayed gratification after mastering the extremely complex skillsets they require. Elden Ring and Bloodborne especially reward this earned mastery with incredibly rich lore and storylines. George RR Martin worked on Elden Ring for fuck's sake.

- The "artistic intention" you're clinging onto in this instance is save-scumming to accomplish a task as deep and as nuanced as a game of sudoku. I don't find that installing URM and using it to breeze through arbitrary time-sucks to be that far removed from needing to save-scum, both are cheesy workarounds for poor game design, and I don't give a shit what the developer's intention is, because he's proved he can be a fucking idiot in equal measures to his genius. The mere fact that I'm spending this long to address your points one by one is prima facie evidence that I'm not the quivering, dopamine-insufficient, TikTok-brained "child playing with toys" you'd like to uncharitably paint me as, and I would argue that the mere act of slogging through the immense length of this game and posting in this thread at all was enough to defeat that standard.
