PrincessEuphy said:
The moment you start thinking about "proper game design," "immersion," etc you've already lost because you're on the completely wrong track. It is blindingly obvious that the purpose of the puzzles is not to provide a fun and engaging experience. They reflect that fact that the further one goes into Lessons in Love, the more the world rejects the player (this goes for both the literal player and Sensei). It becomes increasingly hard to progress, increasingly unfun, increasingly grindy - it would be reductive to state there is only one ludonarrative purpose for this, but that is the design. The artistic purpose. It is an experience the developer is attempting to convey through mechanic. It is axiomatic to say that "video games should be fun," "puzzles should test innovative thinking," etc, which is to say that they are not fundamental truths - they are platitudes liable to become thought-terminating cliches. Looking at systems clearly designed to reject the player and make their life difficult then complaining about how they aren't fun enough is so foolish I balk that one so invested in the story and theory-crafting would be so blind to this point. Let us examine once again Moby Dick.

https://melville.electroniclibrary.org/editions/versions-of-moby-dick/32-cetology

In chapter 32 there is a lengthy chapter devoted to the physiology of whales. This is a highly dull chapter to read and a well-known roadblock for prospective readers of the work (yet I must explain it in detail here because it is dubious whether any poster in this thread has ready even such a fundamental cornerstone a literature such as Moby Dick). However, in this context of literature removed from "a porn game that should be fun and get my pee pee hard," we see immediately how foolish it would be to critique it from a lens as those critiquing SENSEI QUEST and other resets are. Can you imagine going to Melville and saying, good sir, it is all well and good that you wish your novel to be a testimony to every aspect of whales from the physical aspects of their being to the mythological image they come to represent, but this chapter was quite dull! Could you not make it a bit more fun and exciting? In fact, quite a few of your chapters could be shaved down, let's have more action scenes and whale hunting, you would really get more readers that way! It is rather obnoxious that you should even think to force me to read some boring chapter on whales when I can in fact simply flip the pages! Do you not know I will just flip the pages? You are not listening to me sir, I am telling you to make your novel more fun for me!

It really is just that simple: think, for one moment, the purpose. Now, it is entirely fair if you look at Lessons in Love rejecting the player and making it increasingly hard/unpleasant to make progress as a foolish thing. Some people think whales are dumb. However, this is not what is happening. The angle of attack is so completely off base it's like one is seeing reality on an entirely different level. Like one's mind is so boxed in by platitudes that any time something isn't fun and satisfying their every urge for what they want it to be that the entire world starts to seem wrong. How can one profess themselves to be a deep thinker, a lover of thought and figuring things out, so proud of each theory and confirmed idea, if such basic mental walls blind them so deeply? Such that they look upon a rock and see a mountain, or they look upon a mountain and see a rock? You really think for one fucking second the puzzles are meant to be fun tests of knowledge? You really think they contain anything but spite and hostility? You really think this is supposed to be a good time? You really think that 'all media must be fun' is a God-like axiom that subsumes all other purposes one may have? What? WHAT???????????? The populace is rendered infants before the most basic and blunt artistic purpose which itself is literally stated directly over and over. Shocking! Nothing really is beautiful!
Click to expand...
Moby Dick was an intricate work of years, each chapter, even the boring ones, fulfilling a well-rounded purpose. LiL reset puzzles are works of a week, hastily cobbled together and by your own admission, only serving one singular-dimensional purpose. You are comparing Starry Night to the wallpaper behind it.

You read a chapter in Moby Dick about the science of whales and come out the other side knowing more about whales, having been given a pleasant intermission and a palate cleanser from the chapters previous, and a sort of tongue-in-cheek rational, scientific contrast from the rest of the book's thematic elements. What do you come out the other side of a LiL reset having gained, other than a redundant reinforcement of the previously-well-established knowledge that the game is hostile to you? Is understanding that to an even further degree worth the time it takes to accomplish resets unaided? If there's some grander design, and anywhere near the nuance of Melville that you've somehow neglected mentioning so far, feel free to chime in with it.

You keep uncharitably shadowboxing, so arguing with you is largely pointless - no one is either saying or implicitly expecting that "video games should be fun" or "puzzles should test innovative thinking" in this context, people just want the barest experience of having the time they put into a "literary" work be respected. Melville put a huge amount of research, love, and care into the "dull" chapters of Moby Dick you love so much, which means that yes, people skipping those parts is unreasonable.

But again... the comparisons you're making are fundamentally outrageous. Works like Moby Dick are so great and near perfection of their craft that the reader has no reasonable choice except to have the book dictate a change in their first impression of something, like the viability of purely scientific-oriented chapters in a work of fiction. I'm not extending that same charity to the developer of a game who demonstrably can't keep his mood on a particular day out of the story he's writing, in the naive hope that this attempt is materially different than his prior attempts.

And I can only speak for myself, but this game has never once served as porn for me or made my pee pee hard. I find it to be almost astoundingly unerotic, even with the non-taboo characters. (0.44)Kaori is one of my favorite characters, and the fact that her sexual awakening came in the form of "a god inhabited my body and put me on his dick and I really liked it"... yeah man, peak erotic fiction right there. It uses sex as a horror element instead, like the works that inspired it.

Given you see us all as childish, porn-addled degenerates who can't appreciate good literature, normally I wouldn't know why you would keep wasting your time interacting with us, but every one of us in this thread enjoys wasting our time on hopeless endeavors - that's why we play this game at all. Most of us just maintain some degree of healthy, informed boundaries with the content we consume.

I feel like, at times, we might forget that parts of this game might be more like... interpretations of things not supernatural but more like hallucinations or altered mental states. Like, i'm more keen to lean on Sekai 'taking control' and making Akira kiss Yumi being less literal, Sekai is his abuser, his groomer, the ghost of his trauma, in a broken headcase like him, that situation with Yumi could cause flashbacks of his trauma and in that altered state, he'd just be on autopilot, copying what was done to him but to her. Like, i know with all the timelooping stuff there's got to be more to this than it turning out he's just a dude in a psychward dealing with his insanity, that'd be the lamest cop-out of an ending Selly could go for, but always assuming shit is exactly what it is on face value kind of strikes me as going too far the other way, some of the shit he does and goes through has got to be manifestations of his abuse trauma... replicating past experiences is beyond common in long term abuse victims, particularly those abused in their formative years, i myself enjoy getting physically hurt in the bedroom as a form of twisted and soothing replication of all the times my father beat the shit out of me growing up.

We know that Kaori was in a car crash that killed her parents, immediately after which she received Sekai's heart, so the two accidents had to have happened at approximately the same time. The most logical conclusion is that Kaori's family was in the other car.

Though I do see some appeal in both cars belonging to the Arakawas, since that would explain the white car/yellow car confusion, so maybe I'm wrong.

Just a reminder I type this out as I think of it then edit it later. It may make no sense and also all is subject to change 5 mins later.

Here we go:

1st time since I started that I haven't replayed the last update just before the new drop. I actually wasn't really wanting to read it when I got home from work today which is new. Especially after seeing the reset stuff, yikes. I fear I am frustrated with this, not really liking ch4 much overall. Will read it later tonight after I sleep some.

10 hours later...
Cant lie, I do feel good at the start with Io and Uta chatting.

Kirin does look cute. Always like naughty looking Chika but I still prefer her other hair color.

Touka looks awesome!

I don't like seeing Maya cry! Even if I am having trouble with this version!

Reading the picture messages, I sit and wonder. Is waiting for things to progress the most annoying thing about this story? Does Sel drag things out that should be happening by now? Why is the pic stuff with Rin not progressing?

The Makoto and Yumi chat was great!

Yumi is spot on, Chika is delusional.

Molly looks very cute! I still think she is one of the prettiest girls in the story.

I'm not really interested in Prince Ami and her doing stuff with the girls. I sure hope nothing happened off screen there.

I feel like Sel throws a lot of threads out there and then just drops them for months or all together.

There are way too many characters and it's very frustrating. Do you think devs make so many characters because they get bored with the ones they have? Another update with very limited time with some girls and no or little Akira interaction.

Sel torturing me/us with Maya Prime is also extremely frustrating.

I suppose that was a nice scene with Io.

I have long given up trying to understand what Yasu is saying.

The Tsuneyo scene is pissing me off. Fuck Sekai. This is not the kind of story I like, why did I start reading this! A shitty lewd memory I will never watch and then Sel leaves out Maya memories. Also, Fuck You Sekai.

Ami is still one of my least liked characters. Fuck you Ami, stop flashing her. Maya don't fall for it!

Chika is still insane. I miss the mating season event.

Yumi and Kirin chat was cute.

When she isn't assaulting someone, I find the Nodoka search interesting. Its ok to cuss out Otoha

Ohh I figured that was Himawari, wonder if Nodoka got a hard reset/death

Your right Uta, Kirin does look pretty!

Like the band song until the 20th time it replayed. Wish is was just the music.

I don't feel like I can believe anything ParryKaori is saying, I have no trust left.

Yeah good scene with Karoi but I just want Sekai to go away.

I love DQ/DW and plan on buying the HD 2D remakes that come out this and next year. I hope they remake 4, was my favorite.

The shop girl dialogue is funny. I am liking the reset dialogue. Long Maya and Moyo were fun. Would have sucked without URM or a guide.

Yeah it sucks what happened to Sekai, but just like Akira, the stuff she has done later is hard to get past. Maybe when I know even more.

Weird end but maybe new Maya is hanging around for the reset which is cool.

Sel still doesn't confirm if Akira is the father, as far as I could tell.

Didn't hate the update or anything, enjoyed several scenes. Just confused again.

Thanks for the guide Moonflare!

Sorry I haven't been posting or interacting much lately. I admit I have just been skimming the pages. I started watching some anime and reading some LNs, which I have never done much of before other than a couple animes over the years. The genres I have been trying are more my speed, no horror or psychological shit, more romance and adventure stuff, mostly Isekai. I think I am getting burnt out on AVNs, I have cut down on the time I spend with them a bunch recently. I am not ready to abandon anything yet and I very much want to know what happens next with LiL, I just don't think I like this chapter much so have been down on the story. I know the dark route will be worse and I hated the Tsunecchi event so I can expect more shit like that which I am not looking forward to. Ohh well, we will see how I feel after 45.

Until next time!

PrincessEuphy said:
The moment you start thinking about "proper game design," "immersion," etc you've already lost because you're on the completely wrong track. It is blindingly obvious that the purpose of the puzzles is not to provide a fun and engaging experience. They reflect that fact that the further one goes into Lessons in Love, the more the world rejects the player (this goes for both the literal player and Sensei). It becomes increasingly hard to progress, increasingly unfun, increasingly grindy - it would be reductive to state there is only one ludonarrative purpose for this, but that is the design. The artistic purpose. It is an experience the developer is attempting to convey through mechanic. It is axiomatic to say that "video games should be fun," "puzzles should test innovative thinking," etc, which is to say that they are not fundamental truths - they are platitudes liable to become thought-terminating cliches. Looking at systems clearly designed to reject the player and make their life difficult then complaining about how they aren't fun enough is so foolish I balk that one so invested in the story and theory-crafting would be so blind to this point. Let us examine once again Moby Dick.

https://melville.electroniclibrary.org/editions/versions-of-moby-dick/32-cetology

In chapter 32 there is a lengthy chapter devoted to the physiology of whales. This is a highly dull chapter to read and a well-known roadblock for prospective readers of the work (yet I must explain it in detail here because it is dubious whether any poster in this thread has ready even such a fundamental cornerstone a literature such as Moby Dick). However, in this context of literature removed from "a porn game that should be fun and get my pee pee hard," we see immediately how foolish it would be to critique it from a lens as those critiquing SENSEI QUEST and other resets are. Can you imagine going to Melville and saying, good sir, it is all well and good that you wish your novel to be a testimony to every aspect of whales from the physical aspects of their being to the mythological image they come to represent, but this chapter was quite dull! Could you not make it a bit more fun and exciting? In fact, quite a few of your chapters could be shaved down, let's have more action scenes and whale hunting, you would really get more readers that way! It is rather obnoxious that you should even think to force me to read some boring chapter on whales when I can in fact simply flip the pages! Do you not know I will just flip the pages? You are not listening to me sir, I am telling you to make your novel more fun for me!

It really is just that simple: think, for one moment, the purpose. Now, it is entirely fair if you look at Lessons in Love rejecting the player and making it increasingly hard/unpleasant to make progress as a foolish thing. Some people think whales are dumb. However, this is not what is happening. The angle of attack is so completely off base it's like one is seeing reality on an entirely different level. Like one's mind is so boxed in by platitudes that any time something isn't fun and satisfying their every urge for what they want it to be that the entire world starts to seem wrong. How can one profess themselves to be a deep thinker, a lover of thought and figuring things out, so proud of each theory and confirmed idea, if such basic mental walls blind them so deeply? Such that they look upon a rock and see a mountain, or they look upon a mountain and see a rock? You really think for one fucking second the puzzles are meant to be fun tests of knowledge? You really think they contain anything but spite and hostility? You really think this is supposed to be a good time? You really think that 'all media must be fun' is a God-like axiom that subsumes all other purposes one may have? What? WHAT???????????? The populace is rendered infants before the most basic and blunt artistic purpose which itself is literally stated directly over and over. Shocking! Nothing really is beautiful!

So I just finished my playthrough last night and now got around to read up on all the feedback and theory crafting.
As per usual, our lore masters Moonflare, aramaug and bargle didn't disappoint, some very nice theories and thought experiments, wonderful!

However, before I start with my general feedback post, I wanted to touch on one subject that I was personally surprised to find a heated discussion for:
The reset puzzle.

Now, please bear with me, because I will actually take a bit of an opposed stance on this from the general consensus in this thread.
I, and please forgive me for this, did actually not mind the reset puzzle this time.

But, and this is a huge caveat, in the context of previous reset puzzles.

What I mean by this is that this was the first bigger reset puzzle that I was able to "solve" by myself without immediately feeling defeated and knowing I will have to rely on outside help.

Was it therefore a fun and engaging experience?
Fuck no.
Was it a clever way of conveying the Sisyphusian philosophy of the game that whatever you do will just lead to pain and is useless and yadda yadda?
No, absolutely not.
Was it at least beatable and gave me vague reminiscent nostalgia for the Dragon Quest series and shitty old-school RPGs?
Well yeah, I guess.

I think that in Sel's weirdly WIRED wired brain, he envisioned a different kind of experience. I am convinced that if he had the resources, time and technical foundation (i.e. not Renpy) to actually create a small turn-based RPG within the game for this reset, he would have done a half-decent job that would have been mostly enjoyed by the community. I do think that his idea was fine and his heart was at the right place.

However, as Moonflare mentioned, while his intentions may have been good, the implementation was, as usual, dog shit.
It just turned out to be a click fest, no animations, no clever systems, just grind.

Now what I disliked about the discussion here regarding this was mostly one thing:
That this reset puzzle would take many hours to complete without URM or cheats.

I finished the puzzle within around 2 hours, including the Fred fight. Now going back to the previous points, was it worth it or a fun use of 2 hours? No. But it didn't take as long as a lot of people make it out in this thread. It's literally just trial & error and fast clicking + CTRL. You don't even have to use the save & load function if you just memorized the previous steps (though of course you can).
And the 1 milion coins for the two sex scenes each were such obvious baits that it was clearly futile to even try to change the variables manually. At worst it would have been some kind of evil trick of Sel's to punish cheaters.

And, to come to my main argument for this:
The previous reset puzzles were worse.

They were inherently worse, because they were not only grindy, like this one, but they were unlimited in their grindiness.
What do I mean by this?

A few users pointed out the mathematical chances to guess the correct choices for the order of attacks. It's true that guessing it right takes time. However, you knew that you would get there by brute forcing it, in addition to taking into account some common sense (using attacks that weren't used in the previous fight, not repeating attacks, except for Fred).

With, I believe, all of the previous reset puzzles, you had a lot more variables. You either had open-text answers to provide, so technically an infinite amount of answers if you were unable to come up with the answer naturally. Or you had weird combinations of having to do certain things at the right day of the week, doing a certain thing 15 times, but only that one thing, while avoiding another etc.
Brute forcing was basically unapplicable in those cases, or would at least take a lot longer to solve the puzzle. You wouldn't even know where to start.

So in that regard, I liked the reset puzzle more than previous ones.
Again, was it a good puzzle? No.

What would make the reset puzzles enjoyable?
As Moonflare mentioned, and as Sel used once during the shorter TV kids show puzzle section, rewarding the player for paying attention and remembering lore from the game.
Setting the puzzle up around having to remember or revisit scenes and details about the story or girls. Engaging the player in some (light) detective work that revolved around becoming more familiar with the characters and the lore.
I assume it would still scratch Sel's itch for testing the players and forcing them to prove their "worth", in his eyes, to continue the story, without having to sacrifice all of the player's enthusiasm and excitement.

Also, on another note, did someone find out if you are able to save Kenji?
I obviously clicked through all mobs right at the beginning, but figured there would be some alternative dialogue if you waited to face him when you have more spells and equipment later on. Just obviously couldn't bother to reload as it was clear it would not be crucial to getting through the puzzle.

spoilers.title: My "hot" take
spoilers.html:
I, and please forgive me for this, did actually not mind the reset puzzle this time.

But, and this is a huge caveat, in the context of previous reset puzzles.

What I mean by this is that this was the first bigger reset puzzle that I was able to "solve" by myself without immediately feeling defeated and knowing I will have to rely on outside help.

Was it therefore a fun and engaging experience?
Fuck no.
Was it a clever way of conveying the Sisyphusian philosophy of the game that whatever you do will just lead to pain and is useless and yadda yadda?
No, absolutely not.
Was it at least beatable and gave me vague reminiscent nostalgia for the Dragon Quest series and shitty old-school RPGs?
Well yeah, I guess.

I think that in Sel's weirdly WIRED wired brain, he envisioned a different kind of experience. I am convinced that if he had the resources, time and technical foundation (i.e. not Renpy) to actually create a small turn-based RPG within the game for this reset, he would have done a half-decent job that would have been mostly enjoyed by the community. I do think that his idea was fine and his heart was at the right place.

However, as Moonflare mentioned, while his intentions may have been good, the implementation was, as usual, dog shit.
It just turned out to be a click fest, no animations, no clever systems, just grind.

Now what I disliked about the discussion here regarding this was mostly one thing:
That this reset puzzle would take many hours to complete without URM or cheats.

I finished the puzzle within around 2 hours, including the Fred fight. Now going back to the previous points, was it worth it or a fun use of 2 hours? No. But it didn't take as long as a lot of people make it out in this thread. It's literally just trial & error and fast clicking + CTRL. You don't even have to use the save & load function if you just memorized the previous steps (though of course you can).
And the 1 milion coins for the two sex scenes each were such obvious baits that it was clearly futile to even try to change the variables manually. At worst it would have been some kind of evil trick of Sel's to punish cheaters.

And, to come to my main argument for this:
The previous reset puzzles were worse.

They were inherently worse, because they were not only grindy, like this one, but they were unlimited in their grindiness.
What do I mean by this?

A few users pointed out the mathematical chances to guess the correct choices for the order of attacks. It's true that guessing it right takes time. However, you knew that you would get there by brute forcing it, in addition to taking into account some common sense (using attacks that weren't used in the previous fight, not repeating attacks, except for Fred).

With, I believe, all of the previous reset puzzles, you had a lot more variables. You either had open-text answers to provide, so technically an infinite amount of answers if you were unable to come up with the answer naturally. Or you had weird combinations of having to do certain things at the right day of the week, doing a certain thing 15 times, but only that one thing, while avoiding another etc.
Brute forcing was basically unapplicable in those cases, or would at least take a lot longer to solve the puzzle. You wouldn't even know where to start.

So in that regard, I liked the reset puzzle more than previous ones.
Again, was it a good puzzle? No.

What would make the reset puzzles enjoyable?
As Moonflare mentioned, and as Sel used once during the shorter TV kids show puzzle section, rewarding the player for paying attention and remembering lore from the game.
Setting the puzzle up around having to remember or revisit scenes and details about the story or girls. Engaging the player in some (light) detective work that revolved around becoming more familiar with the characters and the lore.
I assume it would still scratch Sel's itch for testing the players and forcing them to prove their "worth", in his eyes, to continue the story, without having to sacrifice all of the player's enthusiasm and excitement.

posts.content_html_raw:
NicolasL4D said:
Sekai in the past and Sekai now seem like completely different people personality wise.
Click to expand...
This is the update that has me thinking, either:
1) perhaps the ghost Sekai that haunts Akira isn't a "natural product" of a dead person's spirit, but a curse that Akira subconsciously placed on himself,
2) or simply the voices in her head and/or the life she was in haven't gotten to her yet.

Option 1 has been discussed quite a lot, but mostly in the direction of simply deciding whether the free floating Sekai is real or only exists in Akira's head; since we can find more than one scene where Sekai could directly or indirectly interact with other characters, we presumed ghost Sekai is "real to everyone".

However, after revealing the human side of Sekai in this update, I can't help wondering about additional questions like "Why does a woman who supposedly only cared about Akira then Ami and probably nothing else when she was alive, become this evil sex nymph that we see today after her death?" Could it be that the ghost Sekai isn't a 100% representation of her original self, but a twisted conjured entity with her darkest traits emphasized and amplified?

Essentially, this is the application of some rather common ideas in media when it comes to interacting with dead spouses' spirits. Either their imagery is infested in a horrifying manner by alive spouses' negative emotions like resentment and guilt toward the dead ones, or you simply cannot summon a 100% representation of a dead one's original self anyway; you'd always summon something that feels like her but not her.

Combining other information in this update, namely "how to become a god", "everything you can imagine is real" by Pareidolia and the eerie end of this happy event (Sekai's funeral photo as soon as she said "I don't think I'd be able to [leave you] if I tried"), it feels like the ghost Sekai is literally a curse Akira placed on her that results in a terrifyingly twisted dead girlfriend spirit who not only haunts Akira but also is capable of free roaming and pestering others.

Option 2 on the other hand is a lot more straightforward; her descending into madness at that point was far from completion.

So, on to my general recap of this update. Or more so, things I found interesting and were not talked about yet (or enough).

Starting with one thing that really warmed my heart and gave me confidence that maybe not following the green path might actually be viable in some form. At least that's my copium for now, because this scene was just too beautiful:




Chika is even more delulu and bat-shit insane than I thought after the last update. This is bound to become interesting. Or is it?
Because, hear me out, now that the story, judging by the cliffhanger and the previews so far, is being split and played out in alternative cycles (as some have mentioned, I don't think these will be just previous "states" of the current "canon" cycle) what will happen with current cycle? Will it be "paused", in a perpetual state of limbo until the RAS return somehow from the other cycles? Will they create a new cycle that is shaped by their individual actions in their different timelines?

I'm very interested in how Sel attempts to weave everything back together, as time fuckery is often something writers mess up in the end and that causes the plot to crumble and plot holes to amass.
I'm not as pessimistic as Moonflare on this and believe Sel still has control over this and manages to make sense of it, but I also still get the feeling that it gets more and more convoluted and more difficult to fit into everything else.
We will see.

Now on to a few points that I would like to ask the help of the lore master squad (LMS) for.
There is a few things here. First off, who is the handsome man planting the tree supposed to be?

This whole section where Sekai narrates Tsuneyo's "wet dream" of having sex with Akira is confusing me. Is Sekai projecting her experience on her? Is she talking about how she was deflowered at a young age by her father (Yuu?)? How it made her hear the voices of the gods, i.e. letting the gods reside in her? Is that why Yuu did it, because the gods told him to do so, like the gods told Sekai to molest Akira so they can reside in him? And why they tell Akira to cum inside the other girls, so the gods can use them as vessels as well? Is this all just a perpetual chain of gods finding vessels in which they can take form?

Why else would Akira be so obviously possessed and driven to impregnate Molly in this scene? This gives very clear HOPE vibes.

Now I really liked this scene. Not only because I like both of the girls a lot, I feel like the narrator's words will become very significant. I just can't tell who it is.

I feel like this line specifically suggests it would be someone who actually was invited to this specific party, as they stress that there are other alternate timelines/cycles/planes of this version of the event taking place where they are technically not invited, but another version of them. Am I reading too much into it?
In that case I would say it could be either current Maya (not Maya Prime) from the future with her knowledge returned. Or current Akira, again with future knowledge, who has become a god/narrator of some sort. Or even Ayane or Makoto with a similar fate. Or even Sana? Nodoka?

Now let's look at the transcript so far:

This is pretty obviously foreshadowing the cliffhanger, that the RAS is spread around different timelines, different parties "they were not invited to". That it's not important only where they are but when they are.
What is additionally mentioned is that what is going to happen in those other timelines might be more dangerous or worse than what happens in this one. That there or "other walls" that are "even harder to scale". That gods don't want them to just slip jump to other planes and timelines, fearing that, they will end up too close to the truth, just like Nodoka? That sometimes it's better to remain unaware and be happy with what you have, to just be complacent.

Now the next section becomes even more interesting and more personal:

So the narrator says that this opinion is just the ones of the gods, basically. Though the narrator still comes to the same conclusion, just even more drastic. They don't want you to stand out, to do anything at all, just remain in place because they fear you might leave. Also someone who wants to suffocate? That brings to mind the image of Maya hanging in the room full of clocks...
Who are they addressing now anyway? Is it Akira? Or maybe the player directly? After all, the end of Sensei Quest suggests that there is a player who is playing the game.

It could all be a simulation after all. An experiment.
Though, it could just as likely be Sel throwing in red herrings and misguiding us.

But let's leave it at that for now and focus on the rest of the narrator's monologue:

So here they clearly mention that they built this world. It has been mentioned several times that the world has been built for Akira, but never that he was the one building it. At this point I really don't think Akira is the narrator.
One thing I absolutely didn't get is what the multicolored glow is supposed to mean. Could this be a reference to the trinity of gods? The only character that would really fit here directly would be Nao I guess.
This would will remain as long as the rules are followed. A.k.a. as long as nobody makes it break like Maya did with several of the ones she destroyed when trying to explain it to Akira, etc. Would that suggest it's Maya, since she knows all about the rules?
And maybe the most significant line: "Don't leave me alone again."
Who was left alone? Prime Maya when she was snapped out of existence and forced into another plane? Or Ayane, who has now slipped jumped to another cycle? Makoto is still with Akira in hers. But New Maya isn't.
Or, was Himawari the narrator all along?

I'm really confused by this, someone with a wrinklier brain needs to spoon-feed me answers to this eventually.

This was quite beautiful. First of all, I have to send my apologies to our man Pareidolia. My very first message in this thread was about comparing him to a user who posted a negative review for this game on here. If the things he said this update are true, and they surprisingly make sense actually, then it seems like he was a scapegoat and didn't deserve the hate I harbored for him. Let's see if this will remain true.

Similarly, I found it very satisfactory that we got some direct lore for Sekai, showing her "true" self and making her more humane and understandable in my eyes now. Given that she has been most likely plagued by the same voices/gods as Yuu and Akira, it paints her past actions in a different light.
I also am 100% convinced now that Ami is Akira's child. Here is where, I believe, Sekai is excited to tell Akira about how the child is his once they are in Kyoto, she really looks like she considers the pregnancy a good thing, like it's a manifestation of their love and an anchor that will hold them together.

It's only once she realizes that he would be unhappy when forced away from Niki, that she decides not to tell him Ami is his, as it would make him change his mind and go with her. She knows she would be the one that made him unable to fulfill his desires, robbing him of the chance of a somewhat normal life with a partner his age, without the burden of a scandalous child, so in a twisted sense, her love for him made her keep it a secret from him. Which becomes even more tragic considering she dies basically because she stayed.

I really liked this scene, it was one of the very few ones that shows how she was really a good person deep down. And it makes me question whether the ghost Sekai really is the true Sekai or some other, more obsessed, form.

Also on a side note: The party scenes where Good Kid was playing made me realize once more that those songs clash with having to read text and being able to process them properly, it's just too distracting. Even though that particular song wasn't that bad.
In fact, I actually really liked the 8bit version in Sensei Quest. Call me a filthy millennial, but it was a bop.
So in conclusion, I like their music. It just doesn't always fit unfortunately.

Will they create a new cycle that is shaped by their individual actions in their different timelines?
I'm very interested in how Sel attempts to weave everything back together, as time fuckery is often something writers mess up in the end and that causes the plot to crumble and plot holes to amass.
I'm not as pessimistic as Moonflare on this and believe Sel still has control over this and manages to make sense of it, but I also still get the feeling that it gets more and more convoluted and more difficult to fit into everything else.
We will see.

spoilers.title: Uta & Kirin scene feat. Good Kid
spoilers.html:
Now I really liked this scene. Not only because I like both of the girls a lot, I feel like the narrator's words will become very significant. I just can't tell who it is.

I feel like this line specifically suggests it would be someone who actually was invited to this specific party, as they stress that there are other alternate timelines/cycles/planes of this version of the event taking place where they are technically not invited, but another version of them. Am I reading too much into it?
In that case I would say it could be either current Maya (not Maya Prime) from the future with her knowledge returned. Or current Akira, again with future knowledge, who has become a god/narrator of some sort. Or even Ayane or Makoto with a similar fate. Or even Sana? Nodoka?

Now let's look at the transcript so far:

This is pretty obviously foreshadowing the cliffhanger, that the RAS is spread around different timelines, different parties "they were not invited to". That it's not important only where they are but when they are.
What is additionally mentioned is that what is going to happen in those other timelines might be more dangerous or worse than what happens in this one. That there or "other walls" that are "even harder to scale". That gods don't want them to just slip jump to other planes and timelines, fearing that, they will end up too close to the truth, just like Nodoka? That sometimes it's better to remain unaware and be happy with what you have, to just be complacent.

Now the next section becomes even more interesting and more personal:

So the narrator says that this opinion is just the ones of the gods, basically. Though the narrator still comes to the same conclusion, just even more drastic. They don't want you to stand out, to do anything at all, just remain in place because they fear you might leave. Also someone who wants to suffocate? That brings to mind the image of Maya hanging in the room full of clocks...
Who are they addressing now anyway? Is it Akira? Or maybe the player directly? After all, the end of Sensei Quest suggests that there is a player who is playing the game.

It could all be a simulation after all. An experiment.
Though, it could just as likely be Sel throwing in red herrings and misguiding us.

But let's leave it at that for now and focus on the rest of the narrator's monologue:

So here they clearly mention that they built this world. It has been mentioned several times that the world has been built for Akira, but never that he was the one building it. At this point I really don't think Akira is the narrator.
One thing I absolutely didn't get is what the multicolored glow is supposed to mean. Could this be a reference to the trinity of gods? The only character that would really fit here directly would be Nao I guess.
This would will remain as long as the rules are followed. A.k.a. as long as nobody makes it break like Maya did with several of the ones she destroyed when trying to explain it to Akira, etc. Would that suggest it's Maya, since she knows all about the rules?
And maybe the most significant line: "Don't leave me alone again."
Who was left alone? Prime Maya when she was snapped out of existence and forced into another plane? Or Ayane, who has now slipped jumped to another cycle? Makoto is still with Akira in hers. But New Maya isn't.
Or, was Himawari the narrator all along?

I'm really confused by this, someone with a wrinklier brain needs to spoon-feed me answers to this eventually.

spoilers.title: The redemption arc of Pareidolia & Sekai
spoilers.html:
This was quite beautiful. First of all, I have to send my apologies to our man Pareidolia. My very first message in this thread was about comparing him to a user who posted a negative review for this game on here. If the things he said this update are true, and they surprisingly make sense actually, then it seems like he was a scapegoat and didn't deserve the hate I harbored for him. Let's see if this will remain true.

Similarly, I found it very satisfactory that we got some direct lore for Sekai, showing her "true" self and making her more humane and understandable in my eyes now. Given that she has been most likely plagued by the same voices/gods as Yuu and Akira, it paints her past actions in a different light.
I also am 100% convinced now that Ami is Akira's child. Here is where, I believe, Sekai is excited to tell Akira about how the child is his once they are in Kyoto, she really looks like she considers the pregnancy a good thing, like it's a manifestation of their love and an anchor that will hold them together.

It's only once she realizes that he would be unhappy when forced away from Niki, that she decides not to tell him Ami is his, as it would make him change his mind and go with her. She knows she would be the one that made him unable to fulfill his desires, robbing him of the chance of a somewhat normal life with a partner his age, without the burden of a scandalous child, so in a twisted sense, her love for him made her keep it a secret from him. Which becomes even more tragic considering she dies basically because she stayed.

I really liked this scene, it was one of the very few ones that shows how she was really a good person deep down. And it makes me question whether the ghost Sekai really is the true Sekai or some other, more obsessed, form.

Hey, guys! Remember this?

Fire Lord Zuko said:
As soon as October 1st hits, I'm gonna stay off the thread the entire month to avoid any spoilers while waiting for Part 2 to drop.
Click to expand...

Seriously, fuck this game for being so addicting. I was doing so well too. At least, at first I was.

I was having a good ol' time, playing The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, trying to keep my mind off the update. And as I'm playing, every time I would use the ocarina to reset the three-day cycle in Termina, my mind was just like:

"Y'know, that kind of reminds me of the Lessons in Love reset... Like... the one that's going on right now."

"...I wonder what's happening in the latest update."

Sooo long story short, I cracked. Quite easily at that. Womp womp. Oh well. I have to deal with a cliffhanger now, but it's all good.

On the bright side, I can actually review this thing, because ohhhhhh man, was this update something...

I did read everyone's posts on here, and something I'm surprised no one has mentioned yet is wtf happened to Futaba's parents. Are they gone with the reset shenanigans as well? Did they get Masahiro'd somehow and died in a really tragic way, and no one has been able to contact Futaba about it?

The way it's being set up, I'm led to believe that's the direction Sel is heading. And considering Futaba's mind is already in a dark place?


Futaba - "I just want it to end."
- "I just want it to be over."
- "And so sometimes I imagine what that would be like. Or how I would do it.
- "Or what would become of people like Rin or Nodoka or my family or you. And that calms me down a little."
- "I love all of you guys. It's myself that I can't stomach."
- "So please continue to be kind to me, as I am only reluctantly here."

Event Name: "My Curse" (Chapter 4 Futaba Event)

Yeahhhhh, it's not looking good for her in the near future, I don't think... Not to mention her TSS experience and the conversation immediately afterwards with Nodoka also likely weighing on her mind.
So... now New Maya is aware that Niki is moving in. And as we all could have expected, it didn't go well at all. And though some good came of it since she was finally willing to hear Akira out on the 'old Maya' and 'time stuff', well...

What was it the narrator said during the "Rubik's Cube" event? At the very start of the update?


Mysterious Narrator - "Oh, and remember -- seeing is believing. Hearing is not."

Soooo yeah. New Maya's gonna learn allll about how real the 'time stuff' is very soon, as the ending reveals to us. I'll get to the ending in a bit, though.
Chika is fucking nuts! Moving on.
Ami is fucking nuts! Moving on-

Okay fine.

So I'm gonna honest. I love this new direction that Ami is going in. The Prince Ami stuff has an appeal all on its own in that it opens the doors to plenty of interesting threesomes down the line. But beyond that... what's been happening recently is us seeing exactly how good Ami is as an actor and manipulator.

You can hate her for it, sure. You can think she's crazy as hell, fine. But she's smart. Ami is someone who's smart that feigns a lack of intellect. I'm not claiming her to be a super genius on Nodoka or Tsubasa's level, but she knows how to get what she wants, and she knows Akira better than most people in the game.

Not to mention that Ami was clearly testing New Maya in their dorm room to see whether or not she knew about the resets. We may not have a clear cut answer just yet, but Ami definitely is aware of the resets and time loops. There's no way she isn't. As far as her plan with New Maya and 'dragging Akira back'? Well... I suppose we'll see how that pans out.

Be extra mindful of her, especially in the near future. Ignore this. Ami Arakawa is so cute and perfect.

You remember. The one that Noriko and Miku were looking at. The one that had the photos of them in costumes they didn't recognize. What could this mean?

A Halloween from a past update? Unlikely, since the girls in class reference past special events all the time. Even just this update, Kirin poked fun at Chika for rejecting Rin, which was very obviously at the Beach. So okay, no. That possibility is out.

Is it a Halloween from a different cycle entirely? I like this possibility the best, and as another user speculated, perhaps these boxes are able to act as time capsules that carry items over in perfect condition, completely unaffected. Hence why Maya Prime did the same with her boxes.

We know for a fact that items disappear otherwise, as evidenced in Reset 3 with Ami's blanket that Maya used for a picnic:


Sensei - "Are we going to get it back? I think Ami really likes this blanket."
Maya - "Possibly."
- "I've never brought a blanket to the apocalypse before."

Event Name: "Sayonara" (Chapter 2 Main Event)

*One Reset Later*


Maya - (regarding Ayane) Gone with the reset, I suppose."
- "Also, your blanket is gone."
- "Sorry."

Event Name: "Before the Sun Comes Up" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)

So to reiterate: Boxes = potential time capsule for important items or mementos. And seeing as the box in question that Noriko found has Ami's name on it, that just adds more credibility to the fact that she's aware of the loops as well.
I really loved Yumi's conversation with Makoto in this update. No, actually, I loved Yumi in general this update. It's fascinating that we had some actual time to breathe with Yumi's revelation of the time loops, and just... got to see how she takes it all in.

Yumi wants to play shit out normally and see how it goes, and I don't blame her for that. "Seeing is believing", right? Not hearing? I'm optimistic Yumi will make it through the reset this time... She's been through it twice now, and to see her not make it yet again would be... admittedly disheartening.

But again, I'll touch more on the reset aspects when I discuss the actual ending of the update.

Oh, and apparently Yumi has both Makoto and Chika's blessing to fuck Akira now... If that's not a sign, I don't know what is.
I thought the nudes Rin sent Akira were super hot this update-

Wait...

They're still not in the game?? Really??

Bro... Even just... I dunno. A hot picture with Rin's Halloween costume posing all sexy or something would have been enough to hold that one over until the Reset stuff was done. Like, I understand. The reset is extremely important. I won't dispute that at all.

But c'mon... It's been, like...

*checks wiki*

Three whole updates... And sure, it doesn't sound like a long time when I put it that way, but it really is such a quick thing to do...

Sexy Rin render. Sent as a picture message. Some funny and flirty responses to hold us over until Rin's next event. Bam. Our imagination can keep us satisfied now that we know it's happening in-universe.

I'm not that torn up about it, really. I just hope that once everything is back to 'normal' in the game, maybe that subplot will finally pick up some steam again.
Wow, okay... That is... not what I expected at all out of this event. Nor did I expect this would be Tsuneyo's first ever h-scene/memory. Sekai's ghost is getting more active, it seems. She wants the collection to be completed, just like our good friend Pareidolia did (more on him soon).

The references to 'The Letter T' Happy Event and also to "Lavender's Green" were especially trippy and jarring... So Tsuneyo has been pretending not to care about love this entire time? About not wanting to fall? Sounds a lot like Maya Prime and her feigned disdain for Sensei...

"It should have been me." Well damn. I did... not see that one coming.

How this changes Akira and Tsuneyo's dynamic in the future remains to be seen, but now she has a lust value when she didn't before. So...

I don't think it'll take very long to add Tsuneyo to the collection at this rate. Which shocks me to say, considering I thought she'd be one of the last to ever put out... Time will tell, though.
I'll be honest, I don't have much to say about Yasu this update, but one thing of note is that I couldn't help but find the fact that she was once again put on medication to 'help' her 'delusions' quite sad. What Yasu sees? What she hears? That's real. We know for a fact it is.

Is HOPE good for Yasu? Fuck no, but that's not what I'm getting at. Yasu clearly has a troubled past with her father who was 'haunted' and her mother who hated her for her 'condition'. Not to mention what that creepy doctor did to her as a wizard by taking lewd pictures of her for his own pleasure...

Yasu Yasui's backstory is super depressing. She has no family she can count on. All she has is God. And with that now stripped away from her... she just doesn't know how to cope properly.

Yasu needs genuine rehabilitation and needs to learn how to live a life where she isn't solely reliant on her God... one step at a time. Of course, this won't happen overnight, but I'm confident that Touka in particular can eventually be a big help with this.
...Yeah.

I wish that the 'Walk Away' option was the Green Path too.

That conversation between them for seemingly the 'wrong' choice was so fucking wholesome, and honestly one of the most genuinely touching conversations in all of LiL. Io's immediate marriage proposal despite finding marriage a stupid concept? The fact she realizes she's a person again and not a 'tool'? It was some amazing stuff, man... 50 affection afterwards to top it off.

But of course, like many here, despite how much it hurts... I stuck with the Green Path. And I mean... their conversation was still... okay. But it had a bitter sort of aftertaste to it, y'know what I mean? We know Stomachache still happened. We know Io is still putting herself through Hell just to appease Akira so she doesn't lose him. It's just... depressing.

And I genuinely like Io... I've expressed as much since way before Stomachache was in the game. Sure, she was bitchy, but she didn't deserve what happened to her, and she especially doesn't deserve to relive it to appease someone. I hope even Green Path Akira can see this, but I have my doubts on that one.

Poor Io...
Nodoka was so close to the truth! She made it to the rooftop and everything, and honestly would have probably remembered post-reset. But of course... PareiKaori said 'nuh uh'.

The way my jaw dropped when the Otoha on the roof was revealed to be Himawari was something spectacular. XD It seems obvious in hindsight. I mean... we know Nodoka isn't 'crazy'. We know she's onto the truth. It was just sort of an effective mind-fuck.

For a moment in time, I was gaslit just like Nodoka and thought she was just talking to absolutely nobody on the phone. That transition was smooth asf.

I wonder what this means for Nodoka, though... Is she dead? I mean, obviously not forever, but... is Nodoka reset? Or is there any possible chance she could remember?

...Guess we'll see if Part 2 can shed some light on that.
Nao's events... okay, so... first off.

John is fucking gigantic again. And Akira and Nao rode on top of him like a steed.



...Wicked.

Secondly, apparently Nao can open gates between completely different worlds/terminals... and she sent Akira to Terminal 22, to his home. To find 'the answers he was looking for'. All because... she wants him to be happy?



...For what reason, exactly?

I mean, Akira asks her this, but we never do get a clear-cut answer. Who is Nao-chan, exactly? What are her motivations? There are still so many unknowns about this character, and I hope we can get some further insight very soon.
Alright, so so so much happened here, so I don't quite know where to start...

How about the Pareidolia stuff? Okay. Wow...

Guys, when that Pareidolia reveal first occurred, I was floored. I thought Kaori was Pareidolia this entire fucking time and all of us were dead wrong. Do you know how absolutely insane that would have been?

I gasped, y'all. I'm not a man who gasps at anything. But that did it.

Of course, as we learn soon after, Kaori is just a 'hotel' for gods/entities, including Pareidolia and obviously Sekai, to take up residence in. True Kaori still exists, she just has to... share her body with these entities who have burrowed their way inside her like parasites.

I feel really bad for her, in all honesty. It reminds me of Yasu, and how HOPE has done the same thing with her. Only Kaori's body houses multiple guests who don't feel up to leaving anytime soon.

Well... except for Pareidolia, I guess, who... was a good guy all along?

Now maybe I just have a pea brain, but isn't Pareidolia literally the one who killed Maya Prime? I mean... that's still factual... isn't it? He was also behind the Molly rape in Lavender's Green, yeah? How is Pareidolia a 'scapegoat' now?

I dunno... I'm gonna have to let this one simmer in my mind a bit longer.

As far as the Kaori sex scene, first of all, it was also unexpected, but... kind of not? Due to the lack of Kaori previews leading up to the update, I was sure something bad was gonna happen to her, but luckily everything seemed... more or less consensual.

The sex was okay... Nothing groundbreaking beyond the setting and timing of everything. They're on the school rooftop fucking as the apocalypse goes down. That's pretty cool. And no one popped out of existence this time! So good.

I wasn't really into the fact Kaori was just suddenly on top of him and immediately into everything. Like... it just felt kinda out of nowhere. You could say Sekai is affecting her libido, but personally I would have preferred a different approach to the build-up of the sex itself.



This was hilarious, though. XD Future Kaori/Nao threesome?
Ah yes... The Reset Puzzle.

To anyone who knows me on here, you may be aware that I actually enjoy the Reset Puzzles because I'm a masochist who lives for mental agony and problem solving.

...Not this time, though. I was not about to waste precious hours grinding that currency legit, nor was I gonna even try to trial and error my way through those battles.

Moonflare had an excellent guide for this puzzle, and I'd like to thank him for saving me valuable time. Even without his guide, though, the URM can pretty much get you through this one. It's a life saver for a reason.

What do I think of Sensei Quest overall? It's... alright. I'm not gonna foam at the mouth and call it a shit puzzle that should die, but I'm not gonna praise it as the best thing ever, because the truth is it's honestly neither of those things. The battle mechanics? Shit. The visuals? Interesting to look at. The grind? Shit. The dialogue itself? Freaking hilarious and got plenty of chuckles out of me. It's pure LiL.

Like c'mon... don't tell me you didn't click on Kenji the Suit Guy in the Fields of Despair and laugh your ass off at the absurdity of his overly dark backstory and at Akira's ridiculous appearance:



See what I mean? It has its ups and downs. The fighting and gameplay was clearly the low points, but the visuals and dialogue more than made up for the time spent in Fucklador.

...And speaking of things found in Sensei Quest...
...Guys...

Am I jumping the gun by calling this one of the best LiL events in the game? Because this answered so many things about Sekai, about Nozomu, about Akira's past and why he feels the way he does...

What an emotional trip, man...

I'm not gonna sing Sekai's praises or justify any of what she's done, but this situation is just really depressing...

Nozomu found out Sekai was pregnant with someone else's child. He goes on to beat her for it. Sekai tries to run away with the one person she feels safe and secure with, the one she loves, in a last ditch effort to leave it all behind...

Akira is understandably upset and calls her out for such a rash plan. He's angry she would carry his brother's child, when Sekai promised that she loved him. It felt to him like a betrayal. Little did he know... the child was his all along.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course knowing the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.

Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...


Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."

A question that was mirrored to Niki in "End of the Tour (Glasswalker)":


Sensei - "You really won't leave?"

Jesus...
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at minimum has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).

This opens up a lot of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?

Maya Prime is also clearly there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is that going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime also at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left?


Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.

So many questions... So many days to wait...

But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.

I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

Chika is fucking nuts! Moving on.
Ami is fucking nuts! Moving on-

Okay fine.

So I'm gonna honest. I love this new direction that Ami is going in. The Prince Ami stuff has an appeal all on its own in that it opens the doors to plenty of interesting threesomes down the line. But beyond that... what's been happening recently is us seeing exactly how good Ami is as an actor and manipulator.

You can hate her for it, sure. You can think she's crazy as hell, fine. But she's smart. Ami is someone who's smart that feigns a lack of intellect. I'm not claiming her to be a super genius on Nodoka or Tsubasa's level, but she knows how to get what she wants, and she knows Akira better than most people in the game.

Not to mention that Ami was clearly testing New Maya in their dorm room to see whether or not she knew about the resets. We may not have a clear cut answer just yet, but Ami definitely is aware of the resets and time loops. There's no way she isn't. As far as her plan with New Maya and 'dragging Akira back'? Well... I suppose we'll see how that pans out.

Be extra mindful of her, especially in the near future. Ignore this. Ami Arakawa is so cute and perfect.

You remember. The one that Noriko and Miku were looking at. The one that had the photos of them in costumes they didn't recognize. What could this mean?

A Halloween from a past update? Unlikely, since the girls in class reference past special events all the time. Even just this update, Kirin poked fun at Chika for rejecting Rin, which was very obviously at the Beach. So okay, no. That possibility is out.

Is it a Halloween from a different cycle entirely? I like this possibility the best, and as another user speculated, perhaps these boxes are able to act as time capsules that carry items over in perfect condition, completely unaffected. Hence why Maya Prime did the same with her boxes.

We know for a fact that items disappear otherwise, as evidenced in Reset 3 with Ami's blanket that Maya used for a picnic:


Sensei - "Are we going to get it back? I think Ami really likes this blanket."
Maya - "Possibly."
- "I've never brought a blanket to the apocalypse before."

Event Name: "Sayonara" (Chapter 2 Main Event)

*One Reset Later*


Maya - (regarding Ayane) Gone with the reset, I suppose."
- "Also, your blanket is gone."
- "Sorry."

Event Name: "Before the Sun Comes Up" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)

So to reiterate: Boxes = potential time capsule for important items or mementos. And seeing as the box in question that Noriko found has Ami's name on it, that just adds more credibility to the fact that she's aware of the loops as well.
I really loved Yumi's conversation with Makoto in this update. No, actually, I loved Yumi in general this update. It's fascinating that we had some actual time to breathe with Yumi's revelation of the time loops, and just... got to see how she takes it all in.

Yumi wants to play shit out normally and see how it goes, and I don't blame her for that. "Seeing is believing", right? Not hearing? I'm optimistic Yumi will make it through the reset this time... She's been through it twice now, and to see her not make it yet again would be... admittedly disheartening.

But again, I'll touch more on the reset aspects when I discuss the actual ending of the update.

Oh, and apparently Yumi has both Makoto and Chika's blessing to fuck Akira now... If that's not a sign, I don't know what is.
I thought the nudes Rin sent Akira were super hot this update-

Wait...

They're still not in the game?? Really??

Bro... Even just... I dunno. A hot picture with Rin's Halloween costume posing all sexy or something would have been enough to hold that one over until the Reset stuff was done. Like, I understand. The reset is extremely important. I won't dispute that at all.

But c'mon... It's been, like...

*checks wiki*

Three whole updates... And sure, it doesn't sound like a long time when I put it that way, but it really is such a quick thing to do...

Sexy Rin render. Sent as a picture message. Some funny and flirty responses to hold us over until Rin's next event. Bam. Our imagination can keep us satisfied now that we know it's happening in-universe.

I'm not that torn up about it, really. I just hope that once everything is back to 'normal' in the game, maybe that subplot will finally pick up some steam again.
Wow, okay... That is... not what I expected at all out of this event. Nor did I expect this would be Tsuneyo's first ever h-scene/memory. Sekai's ghost is getting more active, it seems. She wants the collection to be completed, just like our good friend Pareidolia did (more on him soon).

The references to 'The Letter T' Happy Event and also to "Lavender's Green" were especially trippy and jarring... So Tsuneyo has been pretending not to care about love this entire time? About not wanting to fall? Sounds a lot like Maya Prime and her feigned disdain for Sensei...

"It should have been me." Well damn. I did... not see that one coming.

How this changes Akira and Tsuneyo's dynamic in the future remains to be seen, but now she has a lust value when she didn't before. So...

I don't think it'll take very long to add Tsuneyo to the collection at this rate. Which shocks me to say, considering I thought she'd be one of the last to ever put out... Time will tell, though.
I'll be honest, I don't have much to say about Yasu this update, but one thing of note is that I couldn't help but find the fact that she was once again put on medication to 'help' her 'delusions' quite sad. What Yasu sees? What she hears? That's real. We know for a fact it is.

Is HOPE good for Yasu? Fuck no, but that's not what I'm getting at. Yasu clearly has a troubled past with her father who was 'haunted' and her mother who hated her for her 'condition'. Not to mention what that creepy doctor did to her as a wizard by taking lewd pictures of her for his own pleasure...

Yasu Yasui's backstory is super depressing. She has no family she can count on. All she has is God. And with that now stripped away from her... she just doesn't know how to cope properly.

Yasu needs genuine rehabilitation and needs to learn how to live a life where she isn't solely reliant on her God... one step at a time. Of course, this won't happen overnight, but I'm confident that Touka in particular can eventually be a big help with this.
...Yeah.

I wish that the 'Walk Away' option was the Green Path too.

That conversation between them for seemingly the 'wrong' choice was so fucking wholesome, and honestly one of the most genuinely touching conversations in all of LiL. Io's immediate marriage proposal despite finding marriage a stupid concept? The fact she realizes she's a person again and not a 'tool'? It was some amazing stuff, man... 50 affection afterwards to top it off.

But of course, like many here, despite how much it hurts... I stuck with the Green Path. And I mean... their conversation was still... okay. But it had a bitter sort of aftertaste to it, y'know what I mean? We know Stomachache still happened. We know Io is still putting herself through Hell just to appease Akira so she doesn't lose him. It's just... depressing.

And I genuinely like Io... I've expressed as much since way before Stomachache was in the game. Sure, she was bitchy, but she didn't deserve what happened to her, and she especially doesn't deserve to relive it to appease someone. I hope even Green Path Akira can see this, but I have my doubts on that one.

Poor Io...
Nodoka was so close to the truth! She made it to the rooftop and everything, and honestly would have probably remembered post-reset. But of course... PareiKaori said 'nuh uh'.

The way my jaw dropped when the Otoha on the roof was revealed to be Himawari was something spectacular. XD It seems obvious in hindsight. I mean... we know Nodoka isn't 'crazy'. We know she's onto the truth. It was just sort of an effective mind-fuck.

For a moment in time, I was gaslit just like Nodoka and thought she was just talking to absolutely nobody on the phone. That transition was smooth asf.

I wonder what this means for Nodoka, though... Is she dead? I mean, obviously not forever, but... is Nodoka reset? Or is there any possible chance she could remember?

...Guess we'll see if Part 2 can shed some light on that.
Nao's events... okay, so... first off.

John is fucking gigantic again. And Akira and Nao rode on top of him like a steed.



...Wicked.

Secondly, apparently Nao can open gates between completely different worlds/terminals... and she sent Akira to Terminal 22, to his home. To find 'the answers he was looking for'. All because... she wants him to be happy?



...For what reason, exactly?

I mean, Akira asks her this, but we never do get a clear-cut answer. Who is Nao-chan, exactly? What are her motivations? There are still so many unknowns about this character, and I hope we can get some further insight very soon.
Alright, so so so much happened here, so I don't quite know where to start...

How about the Pareidolia stuff? Okay. Wow...

Guys, when that Pareidolia reveal first occurred, I was floored. I thought Kaori was Pareidolia this entire fucking time and all of us were dead wrong. Do you know how absolutely insane that would have been?

I gasped, y'all. I'm not a man who gasps at anything. But that did it.

Of course, as we learn soon after, Kaori is just a 'hotel' for gods/entities, including Pareidolia and obviously Sekai, to take up residence in. True Kaori still exists, she just has to... share her body with these entities who have burrowed their way inside her like parasites.

I feel really bad for her, in all honesty. It reminds me of Yasu, and how HOPE has done the same thing with her. Only Kaori's body houses multiple guests who don't feel up to leaving anytime soon.

Well... except for Pareidolia, I guess, who... was a good guy all along?

Now maybe I just have a pea brain, but isn't Pareidolia literally the one who killed Maya Prime? I mean... that's still factual... isn't it? He was also behind the Molly rape in Lavender's Green, yeah? How is Pareidolia a 'scapegoat' now?

I dunno... I'm gonna have to let this one simmer in my mind a bit longer.

As far as the Kaori sex scene, first of all, it was also unexpected, but... kind of not? Due to the lack of Kaori previews leading up to the update, I was sure something bad was gonna happen to her, but luckily everything seemed... more or less consensual.

The sex was okay... Nothing groundbreaking beyond the setting and timing of everything. They're on the school rooftop fucking as the apocalypse goes down. That's pretty cool. And no one popped out of existence this time! So good.

I wasn't really into the fact Kaori was just suddenly on top of him and immediately into everything. Like... it just felt kinda out of nowhere. You could say Sekai is affecting her libido, but personally I would have preferred a different approach to the build-up of the sex itself.



This was hilarious, though. XD Future Kaori/Nao threesome?
Ah yes... The Reset Puzzle.

To anyone who knows me on here, you may be aware that I actually enjoy the Reset Puzzles because I'm a masochist who lives for mental agony and problem solving.

...Not this time, though. I was not about to waste precious hours grinding that currency legit, nor was I gonna even try to trial and error my way through those battles.

Moonflare had an excellent guide for this puzzle, and I'd like to thank him for saving me valuable time. Even without his guide, though, the URM can pretty much get you through this one. It's a life saver for a reason.

What do I think of Sensei Quest overall? It's... alright. I'm not gonna foam at the mouth and call it a shit puzzle that should die, but I'm not gonna praise it as the best thing ever, because the truth is it's honestly neither of those things. The battle mechanics? Shit. The visuals? Interesting to look at. The grind? Shit. The dialogue itself? Freaking hilarious and got plenty of chuckles out of me. It's pure LiL.

Like c'mon... don't tell me you didn't click on Kenji the Suit Guy in the Fields of Despair and laugh your ass off at the absurdity of his overly dark backstory and at Akira's ridiculous appearance:



See what I mean? It has its ups and downs. The fighting and gameplay was clearly the low points, but the visuals and dialogue more than made up for the time spent in Fucklador.

...And speaking of things found in Sensei Quest...
...Guys...

Am I jumping the gun by calling this one of the best LiL events in the game? Because this answered so many things about Sekai, about Nozomu, about Akira's past and why he feels the way he does...

What an emotional trip, man...

I'm not gonna sing Sekai's praises or justify any of what she's done, but this situation is just really depressing...

Nozomu found out Sekai was pregnant with someone else's child. He goes on to beat her for it. Sekai tries to run away with the one person she feels safe and secure with, the one she loves, in a last ditch effort to leave it all behind...

Akira is understandably upset and calls her out for such a rash plan. He's angry she would carry his brother's child, when Sekai promised that she loved him. It felt to him like a betrayal. Little did he know... the child was his all along.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course knowing the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.

Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...


Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."

A question that was mirrored to Niki in "End of the Tour (Glasswalker)":


Sensei - "You really won't leave?"

Jesus...
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at minimum has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).

This opens up a lot of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?

Maya Prime is also clearly there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is that going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime also at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left?


Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.

So many questions... So many days to wait...

But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.

I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course
knowing
the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.
Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...
Spoiler
Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."
A question that was mirrored to Niki in "End of the Tour (Glasswalker)":
Sensei - "You really won't leave?"
Jesus...
Spoiler:
The Ending
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at
minimum
has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).
This opens up a
lot
of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?
Maya Prime is also
clearly
there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is
that
going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime
also
at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left?
Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.
So many questions... So many days to wait...
But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.
I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

Ami is fucking nuts! Moving on-

So I'm gonna honest. I love this new direction that Ami is going in. The Prince Ami stuff has an appeal all on its own in that it opens the doors to plenty of interesting threesomes down the line. Be extra mindful of her, especially in the near future. Ignore this. Ami Arakawa is so cute and perfect.

spoilers.title: That Weird Ass Box
spoilers.html:
You remember. The one that Noriko and Miku were looking at. The one that had the photos of them in costumes they didn't recognize. What could this mean?

A Halloween from a past update? Unlikely, since the girls in class reference past special events all the time. Even just this update, Kirin poked fun at Chika for rejecting Rin, which was very obviously at the Beach. So okay, no. That possibility is out.

Is it a Halloween from a different cycle entirely? I like this possibility the best, and as another user speculated, perhaps these boxes are able to act as time capsules that carry items over in perfect condition, completely unaffected. Hence why Maya Prime did the same with her boxes.

We know for a fact that items disappear otherwise, as evidenced in Reset 3 with Ami's blanket that Maya used for a picnic:


Sensei - "Are we going to get it back? I think Ami really likes this blanket."
Maya - "Possibly."
- "I've never brought a blanket to the apocalypse before."

Event Name: "Sayonara" (Chapter 2 Main Event)

*One Reset Later*


Maya - (regarding Ayane) Gone with the reset, I suppose."
- "Also, your blanket is gone."
- "Sorry."

Event Name: "Before the Sun Comes Up" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)

So to reiterate: Boxes = potential time capsule for important items or mementos. And seeing as the box in question that Noriko found has Ami's name on it, that just adds more credibility to the fact that she's aware of the loops as well.

spoilers.html:
Wow, okay... That is... not what I expected at all out of this event. Nor did I expect this would be Tsuneyo's first ever h-scene/memory. Sekai's ghost is getting more active, it seems. She wants the collection to be completed, just like our good friend Pareidolia did (more on him soon).

The references to 'The Letter T' Happy Event and also to "Lavender's Green" were especially trippy and jarring... So Tsuneyo has been pretending not to care about love this entire time? About not wanting to fall? Sounds a lot like Maya Prime and her feigned disdain for Sensei...

"It should have been me." Well damn. I did... not see that one coming.

How this changes Akira and Tsuneyo's dynamic in the future remains to be seen, but now she has a lust value when she didn't before. So...

I don't think it'll take very long to add Tsuneyo to the collection at this rate. Which shocks me to say, considering I thought she'd be one of the last to ever put out... Time will tell, though.
