spoilers.title: Yasu
spoilers.html:
I'll be honest, I don't have much to say about Yasu this update, but one thing of note is that I couldn't help but find the fact that she was once again put on medication to 'help' her 'delusions' quite sad. What Yasu sees? What she hears? That's real. We know for a fact it is.

Is HOPE good for Yasu? Fuck no, but that's not what I'm getting at. Yasu clearly has a troubled past with her father who was 'haunted' and her mother who hated her for her 'condition'. Not to mention what that creepy doctor did to her as a wizard by taking lewd pictures of her for his own pleasure...

Yasu Yasui's backstory is super depressing. She has no family she can count on. All she has is God. And with that now stripped away from her... she just doesn't know how to cope properly.

Yasu needs genuine rehabilitation and needs to learn how to live a life where she isn't solely reliant on her God... one step at a time. Of course, this won't happen overnight, but I'm confident that Touka in particular can eventually be a big help with this.

spoilers.title: Kaori/Pareidolia
spoilers.html:
Alright, so so so much happened here, so I don't quite know where to start...

How about the Pareidolia stuff? Okay. Wow...

Guys, when that Pareidolia reveal first occurred, I was floored. I thought Kaori was Pareidolia this entire fucking time and all of us were dead wrong. Do you know how absolutely insane that would have been?

I gasped, y'all. I'm not a man who gasps at anything. But that did it.

Of course, as we learn soon after, Kaori is just a 'hotel' for gods/entities, including Pareidolia and obviously Sekai, to take up residence in. True Kaori still exists, she just has to... share her body with these entities who have burrowed their way inside her like parasites.

I feel really bad for her, in all honesty. It reminds me of Yasu, and how HOPE has done the same thing with her. Only Kaori's body houses multiple guests who don't feel up to leaving anytime soon.

Well... except for Pareidolia, I guess, who... was a good guy all along?

Now maybe I just have a pea brain, but isn't Pareidolia literally the one who killed Maya Prime? I mean... that's still factual... isn't it? He was also behind the Molly rape in Lavender's Green, yeah? How is Pareidolia a 'scapegoat' now?

I dunno... I'm gonna have to let this one simmer in my mind a bit longer.

As far as the Kaori sex scene, first of all, it was also unexpected, but... kind of not? Due to the lack of Kaori previews leading up to the update, I was sure something bad was gonna happen to her, but luckily everything seemed... more or less consensual.

The sex was okay... Nothing groundbreaking beyond the setting and timing of everything. They're on the school rooftop fucking as the apocalypse goes down. That's pretty cool. And no one popped out of existence this time! So good.

I wasn't really into the fact Kaori was just suddenly on top of him and immediately into everything. Like... it just felt kinda out of nowhere. You could say Sekai is affecting her libido, but personally I would have preferred a different approach to the build-up of the sex itself.



This was hilarious, though. XD Future Kaori/Nao threesome?

spoilers.title: Sensei Quest
spoilers.html:
Ah yes... The Reset Puzzle.

To anyone who knows me on here, you may be aware that I actually enjoy the Reset Puzzles because I'm a masochist who lives for mental agony and problem solving.

...Not this time, though. I was not about to waste precious hours grinding that currency legit, nor was I gonna even try to trial and error my way through those battles.

Moonflare had an excellent guide for this puzzle, and I'd like to thank him for saving me valuable time. Even without his guide, though, the URM can pretty much get you through this one. It's a life saver for a reason.

What do I think of Sensei Quest overall? It's... alright. I'm not gonna foam at the mouth and call it a shit puzzle that should die, but I'm not gonna praise it as the best thing ever, because the truth is it's honestly neither of those things. The battle mechanics? Shit. The visuals? Interesting to look at. The grind? Shit. The dialogue itself? Freaking hilarious and got plenty of chuckles out of me. It's pure LiL.

Like c'mon... don't tell me you didn't click on Kenji the Suit Guy in the Fields of Despair and laugh your ass off at the absurdity of his overly dark backstory and at Akira's ridiculous appearance:



See what I mean? It has its ups and downs. The fighting and gameplay was clearly the low points, but the visuals and dialogue more than made up for the time spent in Fucklador.

...And speaking of things found in Sensei Quest...

spoilers.title: Kyoto Happy Event
spoilers.html:
...Guys...

Am I jumping the gun by calling this one of the best LiL events in the game? Because this answered so many things about Sekai, about Nozomu, about Akira's past and why he feels the way he does...

What an emotional trip, man...

I'm not gonna sing Sekai's praises or justify any of what she's done, but this situation is just really depressing...

Nozomu found out Sekai was pregnant with someone else's child. He goes on to beat her for it. Sekai tries to run away with the one person she feels safe and secure with, the one she loves, in a last ditch effort to leave it all behind...

Akira is understandably upset and calls her out for such a rash plan. He's angry she would carry his brother's child, when Sekai promised that she loved him. It felt to him like a betrayal. Little did he know... the child was his all along.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course knowing the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.

Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...


Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."

A question that was mirrored to Niki in "End of the Tour (Glasswalker)":


Sensei - "You really won't leave?"

Jesus...

spoilers.title: The Ending
spoilers.html:
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at minimum has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).

This opens up a lot of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?

Maya Prime is also clearly there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is that going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime also at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left?


Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.

So many questions... So many days to wait...

But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.

I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

"...I wonder what's happening in the latest update."

Sooo long story short, I cracked. Quite easily at that. Womp womp. Oh well. I have to deal with a cliffhanger now, but it's all good.

On the bright side, I can actually review this thing, because ohhhhhh man, was this update something...

I did read everyone's posts on here, and something I'm surprised no one has mentioned yet is wtf happened to Futaba's parents. Are they gone with the reset shenanigans as well? Did they get Masahiro'd somehow and died in a really tragic way, and no one has been able to contact Futaba about it?

The way it's being set up, I'm led to believe that's the direction Sel is heading. And considering Futaba's mind is already in a dark place?

Chika is fucking nuts! Moving on.

Okay fine.

So I'm gonna honest. I love this new direction that Ami is going in. The Prince Ami stuff has an appeal all on its own in that it opens the doors to plenty of interesting threesomes down the line. But beyond that... what's been happening recently is us seeing exactly how good Ami is as an actor and manipulator.

You can hate her for it, sure. You can think she's crazy as hell, fine. But she's smart. Ami is someone who's smart that feigns a lack of intellect. I'm not claiming her to be a super genius on Nodoka or Tsubasa's level, but she knows how to get what she wants, and she knows Akira better than most people in the game.

Not to mention that Ami was clearly testing New Maya in their dorm room to see whether or not she knew about the resets. We may not have a clear cut answer just yet, but Ami definitely is aware of the resets and time loops. There's no way she isn't. As far as her plan with New Maya and 'dragging Akira back'? Well... I suppose we'll see how that pans out.

Be extra mindful of her, especially in the near future. Ignore this. Ami Arakawa is so cute and perfect.

View attachment 4095228
You remember. The one that Noriko and Miku were looking at. The one that had the photos of them in costumes they didn't recognize. What could this mean?

A Halloween from a past update? Unlikely, since the girls in class reference past special events all the time. Even just this update, Kirin poked fun at Chika for rejecting Rin, which was very obviously at the Beach. So okay, no. That possibility is out.

Is it a Halloween from a different cycle entirely? I like this possibility the best, and as another user speculated, perhaps these boxes are able to act as time capsules that carry items over in perfect condition, completely unaffected. Hence why Maya Prime did the same with her boxes.

We know for a fact that items disappear otherwise, as evidenced in Reset 3 with Ami's blanket that Maya used for a picnic:

View attachment 4095291
View attachment 4095292 View attachment 4095293 Sensei - "Are we going to get it back? I think Ami really likes this blanket."
Maya - "Possibly."
- "I've never brought a blanket to the apocalypse before."

Event Name: "Sayonara" (Chapter 2 Main Event)

*One Reset Later*

View attachment 4095288
View attachment 4095289 View attachment 4095290 Maya - (regarding Ayane) Gone with the reset, I suppose."
- "Also, your blanket is gone."
- "Sorry."

Event Name: "Before the Sun Comes Up" (Chapter 2 Ayane Event)

So to reiterate: Boxes = potential time capsule for important items or mementos. And seeing as the box in question that Noriko found has Ami's name on it, that just adds more credibility to the fact that she's aware of the loops as well.
I really loved Yumi's conversation with Makoto in this update. No, actually, I loved Yumi in general this update. It's fascinating that we had some actual time to breathe with Yumi's revelation of the time loops, and just... got to see how she takes it all in.

Yumi wants to play shit out normally and see how it goes, and I don't blame her for that. "Seeing is believing", right? Not hearing? I'm optimistic Yumi will make it through the reset this time... She's been through it twice now, and to see her not make it yet again would be... admittedly disheartening.

But again, I'll touch more on the reset aspects when I discuss the actual ending of the update.

Oh, and apparently Yumi has both Makoto and Chika's blessing to fuck Akira now... If that's not a sign, I don't know what is.
I thought the nudes Rin sent Akira were super hot this update-

Wait...

They're still not in the game?? Really??

Bro... Even just... I dunno. A hot picture with Rin's Halloween costume posing all sexy or something would have been enough to hold that one over until the Reset stuff was done. Like, I understand. The reset is extremely important. I won't dispute that at all.

But c'mon... It's been, like...

*checks wiki*

Three whole updates... And sure, it doesn't sound like a long time when I put it that way, but it really is such a quick thing to do...

Sexy Rin render. Sent as a picture message. Some funny and flirty responses to hold us over until Rin's next event. Bam. Our imagination can keep us satisfied now that we know it's happening in-universe.

I'm not that torn up about it, really. I just hope that once everything is back to 'normal' in the game, maybe that subplot will finally pick up some steam again.
Wow, okay... That is... not what I expected at all out of this event. Nor did I expect this would be Tsuneyo's first ever h-scene/memory. Sekai's ghost is getting more active, it seems. She wants the collection to be completed, just like our good friend Pareidolia did (more on him soon).

The references to 'The Letter T' Happy Event and also to "Lavender's Green" were especially trippy and jarring... So Tsuneyo has been pretending not to care about love this entire time? About not wanting to fall? Sounds a lot like Maya Prime and her feigned disdain for Sensei...

"It should have been me." Well damn. I did... not see that one coming.

How this changes Akira and Tsuneyo's dynamic in the future remains to be seen, but now she has a lust value when she didn't before. So...

I don't think it'll take very long to add Tsuneyo to the collection at this rate. Which shocks me to say, considering I thought she'd be one of the last to ever put out... Time will tell, though.
I'll be honest, I don't have much to say about Yasu this update, but one thing of note is that I couldn't help but find the fact that she was once again put on medication to 'help' her 'delusions' quite sad. What Yasu sees? What she hears? That's real. We know for a fact it is.

Is HOPE good for Yasu? Fuck no, but that's not what I'm getting at. Yasu clearly has a troubled past with her father who was 'haunted' and her mother who hated her for her 'condition'. Not to mention what that creepy doctor did to her as a wizard by taking lewd pictures of her for his own pleasure...

Yasu Yasui's backstory is super depressing. She has no family she can count on. All she has is God. And with that now stripped away from her... she just doesn't know how to cope properly.

Yasu needs genuine rehabilitation and needs to learn how to live a life where she isn't solely reliant on her God... one step at a time. Of course, this won't happen overnight, but I'm confident that Touka in particular can eventually be a big help with this.
...Yeah.

I wish that the 'Walk Away' option was the Green Path too.

That conversation between them for seemingly the 'wrong' choice was so fucking wholesome, and honestly one of the most genuinely touching conversations in all of LiL. Io's immediate marriage proposal despite finding marriage a stupid concept? The fact she realizes she's a person again and not a 'tool'? It was some amazing stuff, man... 50 affection afterwards to top it off.

But of course, like many here, despite how much it hurts... I stuck with the Green Path. And I mean... their conversation was still... okay. But it had a bitter sort of aftertaste to it, y'know what I mean? We know Stomachache still happened. We know Io is still putting herself through Hell just to appease Akira so she doesn't lose him. It's just... depressing.

And I genuinely like Io... I've expressed as much since way before Stomachache was in the game. Sure, she was bitchy, but she didn't deserve what happened to her, and she especially doesn't deserve to relive it to appease someone. I hope even Green Path Akira can see this, but I have my doubts on that one.

Poor Io...
Nodoka was so close to the truth! She made it to the rooftop and everything, and honestly would have probably remembered post-reset. But of course... PareiKaori said 'nuh uh'.

The way my jaw dropped when the Otoha on the roof was revealed to be Himawari was something spectacular. XD It seems obvious in hindsight. I mean... we know Nodoka isn't 'crazy'. We know she's onto the truth. It was just sort of an effective mind-fuck.

For a moment in time, I was gaslit just like Nodoka and thought she was just talking to absolutely nobody on the phone. That transition was smooth asf.

I wonder what this means for Nodoka, though... Is she dead? I mean, obviously not forever, but... is Nodoka reset? Or is there any possible chance she could remember?

...Guess we'll see if Part 2 can shed some light on that.
Nao's events... okay, so... first off.

John is fucking gigantic again. And Akira and Nao rode on top of him like a steed.

View attachment 4095551

...Wicked.

Secondly, apparently Nao can open gates between completely different worlds/terminals... and she sent Akira to Terminal 22, to his home. To find 'the answers he was looking for'. All because... she wants him to be happy?

View attachment 4095578

...For what reason, exactly?

I mean, Akira asks her this, but we never do get a clear-cut answer. Who is Nao-chan, exactly? What are her motivations? There are still so many unknowns about this character, and I hope we can get some further insight very soon.

What an emotional trip, man...

I'm not gonna sing Sekai's praises or justify any of what she's done, but this situation is just really depressing...

Nozomu found out Sekai was pregnant with someone else's child. He goes on to beat her for it. Sekai tries to run away with the one person she feels safe and secure with, the one she loves, in a last ditch effort to leave it all behind...

Akira is understandably upset and calls her out for such a rash plan. He's angry she would carry his brother's child, when Sekai promised that she loved him. It felt to him like a betrayal. Little did he know... the child was his all along.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course knowing the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.

Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...

Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."

A question that was mirrored to Niki in "End of the Tour (Glasswalker)":

View attachment 4095818
Sensei - "You really won't leave?"

Jesus...
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at minimum has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).

This opens up a lot of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?

Maya Prime is also clearly there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is that going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime also at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left? View attachment 4095844

Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.

So many questions... So many days to wait...

But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.

I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

spoilers.title: Yasu
spoilers.html:
I'll be honest, I don't have much to say about Yasu this update, but one thing of note is that I couldn't help but find the fact that she was once again put on medication to 'help' her 'delusions' quite sad. What Yasu sees? What she hears? That's real. We know for a fact it is.

Is HOPE good for Yasu? Fuck no, but that's not what I'm getting at. Yasu clearly has a troubled past with her father who was 'haunted' and her mother who hated her for her 'condition'. Not to mention what that creepy doctor did to her as a wizard by taking lewd pictures of her for his own pleasure...

Yasu Yasui's backstory is super depressing. She has no family she can count on. All she has is God. And with that now stripped away from her... she just doesn't know how to cope properly.

Yasu needs genuine rehabilitation and needs to learn how to live a life where she isn't solely reliant on her God... one step at a time. Of course, this won't happen overnight, but I'm confident that Touka in particular can eventually be a big help with this.

Sure, she was bitchy, but she didn't deserve what happened to her, and she especially doesn't deserve to relive it to appease someone. I hope even Green Path Akira can see this, but I have my doubts on that one.

Poor Io...

spoilers.title: Kaori/Pareidolia
spoilers.html:
Alright, so so so much happened here, so I don't quite know where to start...

How about the Pareidolia stuff? Okay. Wow...

Guys, when that Pareidolia reveal first occurred, I was floored. I thought Kaori was Pareidolia this entire fucking time and all of us were dead wrong. Do you know how absolutely insane that would have been?

I gasped, y'all. I'm not a man who gasps at anything. But that did it.

Of course, as we learn soon after, Kaori is just a 'hotel' for gods/entities, including Pareidolia and obviously Sekai, to take up residence in. True Kaori still exists, she just has to... share her body with these entities who have burrowed their way inside her like parasites.

I feel really bad for her, in all honesty. It reminds me of Yasu, and how HOPE has done the same thing with her. Only Kaori's body houses multiple guests who don't feel up to leaving anytime soon.

Well... except for Pareidolia, I guess, who... was a good guy all along?

Now maybe I just have a pea brain, but isn't Pareidolia literally the one who killed Maya Prime? I mean... that's still factual... isn't it? He was also behind the Molly rape in Lavender's Green, yeah? How is Pareidolia a 'scapegoat' now?

I dunno... I'm gonna have to let this one simmer in my mind a bit longer.

As far as the Kaori sex scene, first of all, it was also unexpected, but... kind of not? Due to the lack of Kaori previews leading up to the update, I was sure something bad was gonna happen to her, but luckily everything seemed... more or less consensual.

The sex was okay... Nothing groundbreaking beyond the setting and timing of everything. They're on the school rooftop fucking as the apocalypse goes down. That's pretty cool. And no one popped out of existence this time! So good.

I wasn't really into the fact Kaori was just suddenly on top of him and immediately into everything. Like... it just felt kinda out of nowhere. You could say Sekai is affecting her libido, but personally I would have preferred a different approach to the build-up of the sex itself.

View attachment 4095736

This was hilarious, though. XD Future Kaori/Nao threesome?

spoilers.title: Sensei Quest
spoilers.html:
Ah yes... The Reset Puzzle.

To anyone who knows me on here, you may be aware that I actually enjoy the Reset Puzzles because I'm a masochist who lives for mental agony and problem solving.

...Not this time, though. I was not about to waste precious hours grinding that currency legit, nor was I gonna even try to trial and error my way through those battles.

Moonflare had an excellent guide for this puzzle, and I'd like to thank him for saving me valuable time. Even without his guide, though, the URM can pretty much get you through this one. It's a life saver for a reason.

What do I think of Sensei Quest overall? It's... alright. I'm not gonna foam at the mouth and call it a shit puzzle that should die, but I'm not gonna praise it as the best thing ever, because the truth is it's honestly neither of those things. The battle mechanics? Shit. The visuals? Interesting to look at. The grind? Shit. The dialogue itself? Freaking hilarious and got plenty of chuckles out of me. It's pure LiL.

Like c'mon... don't tell me you didn't click on Kenji the Suit Guy in the Fields of Despair and laugh your ass off at the absurdity of his overly dark backstory and at Akira's ridiculous appearance:

View attachment 4095790

See what I mean? It has its ups and downs. The fighting and gameplay was clearly the low points, but the visuals amd dialogue more than made up for the time spent in Fucklador.

...And speaking of things found in Sensei Quest...

spoilers.title: Kyoto Happy Event
spoilers.html:
...Guys...

Am I jumping the gun by calling this one of the best LiL events in the game? Because this answered so many things about Sekai, about Nozomu, about Akira's past and why he feels the way he does...

What an emotional trip, man...

I'm not gonna sing Sekai's praises or justify any of what she's done, but this situation is just really depressing...

Nozomu found out Sekai was pregnant with someone else's child. He goes on to beat her for it. Sekai tries to run away with the one person she feels safe and secure with, the one she loves, in a last ditch effort to leave it all behind...

Akira is understandably upset and calls her out for such a rash plan. He's angry she would carry his brother's child, when Sekai promised that she loved him. It felt to him like a betrayal. Little did he know... the child was his all along.

Sekai stays behind with her abuser, of course knowing the child belongs to him, but knows Akira would leave with her if he knew the truth. She does a double take, especially knowing he has Niki now. Someone who can be there for him. Someone 'normal'.

Akira asks Sekai if she'll truly never leave him, and thus she makes a promise that would come back to haunt him for years to come...

spoilers.title: The Ending
spoilers.html:
One of the craziest cliffhangers we could have left off on! Not only was everything 'restarted', but our current RAS (including New Maya) at minimum has retained their memories and is spread across three different special events: Halloween 1 (Akira and Makoto), Halloween 2 (New Maya), and Halloween Dorm Wars (Ayane).

This opens up a lot of possibilities, and even questions... Is everyone minus the RAS going to... lose their progress? Are we starting from scratch, or at least an earlier point? Will everything go back to normal by the end?

Maya Prime is also clearly there during the Halloween Dorm Wars, so how is that going to go? Could she be saved? Is Maya Prime also at Halloween 1 where Akira and Makoto are? Because who else would Ami be talking to here on the left? View attachment 4095844

Everyone else is already accounted for in the picture at this point in the timeline, save for Makoto, but she's shown to be on Akira's right in the very next frame.

So many questions... So many days to wait...

But at least we'll have the previews to hold us over until then.

I thoroughly look forward to the conclusion of what has already been an absolute banger of a Reset.

barglenarglezous said:
I think you're attributing someone else's theory to me.

I don't think we're in different timelines. I think they're witnessing a memory of past parties within the reset itself, and they need to navigate to the school rooftop to finish the journey.

Because of this, they might witness things they didn't during the actual party -- for example, Maya might walk in on Akira and Molly, but they're not actually travelling through time. This is all just reset fuckery.
Click to expand...
You're right, I misread one of your previous posts, apologies.

I am not yet convinced though that those are merely memories. And I also don't necessarily think they are time traveling per se. Just slipping to different planes.

How I imagine those work, is that once a cycle ends, i.e. because someone broke a rule, another one is created in that instance so that the original "aware" inhabitants, in "our" case the RAS, Maya and maybe also Yumi, can be moved there, making it a "true" reset.
This has, apparently, happened about a million times for Maya Prime.

What's obviously different here is the starting point. Those are all on Halloween, instead of the start of the school year.
Also, ultimately, it would mean that the "original" inhabitants would have been replaced by "our" cycle's version of Akira, Ayane, Makoto and Maya. Technically that would mean, those would have had to slip somewhere else too?

In any case, I might be very wrong of course.

What arguments are there against this?
Obviously the fact that in all of those instances, the guests are wearing costumes they all actually wore in the cycle we know. In alternate timelines, some might have opted for different costumes. However, one must take into account that this would also amount to extra work for Sel, so it might just be out of convenience to reuse assets. Alternatively, it could be argued that in those different timelines, they could have just all worn the costumes from the first Halloween party, since those cycles probably didn't have the "true" and aware Akira from ours and therefore the cycles should end and not continue with the next season. But I think that would be a bad decision story-telling wise, as it would make it difficult for the player to differentiate in which timeline we are. The reveal would be weak, as it would look like they are all in the same one.

What arguments would support my theory though?
The fact that the situations are clearly different. Someone already provided screenshots, comparing one of the Halloween events that happened with this new scenario and people were in different positions, talking about different things. If those were actual memories, it would be very easy for Sel to make this clear and copy the position of all characters and the dialogues 1:1 from the past events, yet it was deliberately chosen to differ slightly.
I also don't think this is typical reset fuckery, as the situations they landed in seemed fairly normal, with seemingly nothing too supernatural or weird going on.

Ultimately, I am sure they will find a way to get back to their "original" timelines, and slip back. It would be impossibly inconvenient to keep 3 (or even more) timelines, and therefore plots, parallel to each other for very long.
But I do think that the reset is complete and that they won't necessarily get back through the roof. It just won't take as long as a typical cycle.
And in the end, when they are all back, time will have moved on in "our" cycle and will have been filled with "fake" memories, just like when they all slipped after the Dorm Wars straight to the beach event.

DeanNorris said:
What arguments would support my theory though?
The fact that the situations are clearly different. Someone already provided screenshots, comparing one of the Halloween events that happened with this new scenario and people were in different positions, talking about different things. If those were actual memories, it would be very easy for Sel to make this clear and copy the position of all characters and the dialogues 1:1 from the past events, yet it was deliberately chosen to differ slightly.
I also don't think this is typical reset fuckery, as the situations they landed in seemed fairly normal, with seemingly nothing too supernatural or weird going on.
Click to expand...
I can't put any real stock in the timeline being wholly different because people were standing in different spots or Ayane told a joke she didn't tell in the original scene. People move around at parties, and there are moments during the party where we don't see what's going on in the main room -- and there are multiple conversations happening at the same time iwthin that room and we're only being shown the relevant ones. We aren't shown every waking moment of Sensei's day, either, so just because we didn't see Ayane rehearsing her routine doesn't mean it didn't happen, and it doesn't even mean Akira wasn't present for it.

Further -- we've gotten no real confirmation that the reset has ended. Which means it is most likely that none of this is real.

OK, I've made a timeline draft due to the recent mass confusion regarding Noriko's presence in Kyoto.

Some disclaimers are:
1. This timeline is constructed under the assumption that there is no time fuckery or developer oversight or any other shenanigan. I.e., assuming everything shown is from a linear timeline and Selly did not fuck up at all.
(not that I don't think it's impossible. It's just those two possibilities are the absolute trump cards that overrule literally every argument without needing much reasoning. If there is a way to fit things into one flawless linear path then it'd be my go-to until it can no longer be done)

2. I try using ONLY "what's written in the textbox" as the sole determinant, avoiding judging ages based off character models (unless a vastly different model is used), or using conjectures from the conversation no matter how logical they might be.
As in, ONLY using "what is stated here".

3. Following up, "what is stated here" is regarded as absolutely factual without considering the chances of the characters lying unless it is VERY overt.
(this is to avoid rabbit holes like "your evidences are lying while mine are not!")

4. Other events not within the window between Noriko's birth year and the year of The Accident are omitted, with the exception of Present that serves as a reference point.

For me, the confusion that I got is probably due to the fact that there exist only two character models in the game, and the teen version only represents "time during the past" as a broad stroke and will not reflect on "when exactly". For example, if you are willing to believe this timeline draft, that means Niki was in her 20 during Kyoto and she looked almost identical to the Niki when she was 14.

In addition, if one depends too much on character models to place a scene on the timeline, the following scene will make absolutely no sense whether you agree with this timeline or not.


Again the purpose is not meant for defending Selly. This is to, if it's at all possible, fit everything together in the simplest way. Let me know if I screw up somewhere.

Longtime reader first time poster and all that, but: hi

I think the proposed 2005-2020 timeline for Sekai and the Nakayamas would work if we assume, as it's already been posited in multiple occurrences, that Ami might not be 100% real and, in fact, somewhat fictional/fabricated, not unlike the G̶O̶D̶S̶ gods, but based on a human that existed/was about to exist.
If we accept Pareidolia's words as an actual honest and truthful explanation of what a god is (or at least how they come into existence, with Akira pulling aspects out of a wishing well of forgotten deities) and take into account how frequent 'reality rewrites' seem to be within the Kumon-mi bubble, I believe it isn't so far fetched to suggest that:
  1. Sekai in 2011 ('Kyoto' event) is pregnant with Ami (Akira's child)
  2. Akira refuses to flee with her
  3. Sekai dies shortly thereafter (2012) in the car crash
  4. Ami is created by either one of the gods or Akira himself as a manifestation/result (or taking advantage) of his feelings of guilt: "if only i had left with Sekai and accepted to be a father to her baby, she'd still be alive". Akira makes himself be the caretaker of the baby he rejected and Ami gets retconned into existence, but as being born at a point in time (2005) where it would make sense for her to be the right age to be his niece/student in the present. Also, convienient tool to keep Akira in Kumon-mi and alive: he has to take care of Ami. But if she was still in the womb during the car crash, he couldn't possibly assume that mantle, so she "was already there" and was left orphaned by the car crash.
    Akira never mustered the strenght to shake himself out of depression stasis to go get her out of an orphanage, instead while in his episode/stasis he willed her into existence and deluded himself in having gone retrieve her.
  5. Maya 'the stray with no past' gets created (or drawn from the well) to be his perfect distraction/coping mechanism and an outlet for the predatory urges on minors he "inherited" from his abuser Sekai. Entities hate her because by obsessing on her Akira doesn't focus on what they want him to do: abuse Ami, continue the cycle, thus making her into a new vessel for the voices/gods, as Akira, Sekai and Yuu have been as a result of a 'gifted' relative abusing them.
    I am here also taking for valid the convoluted incestuous NiB family tree theory
  6. Later on Pareidolia comes into being has the perfect scapegoat to blame for urges and actions Akira feels remorseful for
It si, obviously, speculation since there's a lot we still don't know and all LiL narrators are, each to their own degree, unreliable, but i think this could work. Still, I'd be honored if Moonflare and the other loremasters pointed out flaws in my reasoning, love the work you guys do on here

I still find it more likely that Sel is just a dumb dumb and made a mistake mentioning Noriko in that scene and the proofreaders having dunce caps on. It's human to make mistakes.

OK, I've made a timeline draft due to the recent mass confusion regarding Noriko's presence in Kyoto.

Some disclaimers are:
1. This timeline is constructed under the assumption that there is no time fuckery or developer oversight or any other shenanigan. I.e., assuming everything shown is from a linear timeline and Selly did not fuck up at all.
(not that I don't think it's impossible. It's just those two possibilities are the absolute trump cards that overrule literally every argument without needing much reasoning. If there is a way to fit things into one flawless linear path then it'd be my go-to until it can no longer be done)

2. I try using ONLY "what's written in the textbox" as the sole determinant, avoiding judging ages based off character models (unless a vastly different model is used), or using conjectures from the conversation no matter how logical they might be.
As in, ONLY using "what is stated here".

3. Following up, "what is stated here" is regarded as absolutely factual without considering the chances of the characters lying unless it is VERY overt.
(this is to avoid rabbit holes like "your evidences are lying while mine are not!")

4. Other events not within the window between Noriko's birth year and the year of The Accident are omitted, with the exception of Present that serves as a reference point.
View attachment 4097196
For me, the confusion that I got is probably due to the fact that there exist only two character models in the game, and the teen version only represents "time during the past" as a broad stroke and will not reflect on "when exactly". For example, if you are willing to believe this timeline draft, that means Niki was in her 20 during Kyoto and she looked almost identical to the Niki when she was 14.

You're missing the point: it's not the fact that he argues, but rather the manner in which he does so, if you want to even call it "argument". I think you're referring to argument in the idealized sense of philosophical debate - that is not what he engages in
Click to expand...
Yeah, absurd psychoanalysis. Minds are infinite in their complexity and motives are infinite in their arbitrariness. Going around making absent-minded theories as to the inner workings of someone's mind and explaining behavior in a way convenient to you is pretty absurd. If you did that to people in real life they'd punch you in the face or otherwise ostracize you. Ever heard of the fundamental attribution error? It's a bias in which people observing others explain behavior by identifying them as "fundamental attributes," like someone kicking a vending machine to get a drink is just "an angry person" and that's why they're kicking the machine. Whereas if they are the one kicking the machine they instead explain it with momentary or circumstantial reasons, like, "I'm not an angry person today is just a bad day." The position that authors are in is one where thousands of readers are constantly psycho-analyzing them and reading into statements and assigning them fundamental attributes to explain any given act of behavior. That is more depressing than anything. And so far from Selebus being a particular misanthrope in this regard, it's weird people online being weird but not getting the normal social rebukes since it's the internet.

> I'm talking about how he treats people on his discord: he's just a dickhead at times

I would be much more offended by an author lying to my face and talking circles around me to extract more income than one being frank and honest even if their honest opinion happens to be a hostile one. Seriously, why do people bemoan dishonesty so much but then react with such violent negativity to actual honesty when they come across it? Really says a lot.

> I think you're referring to argument in the idealized sense of philosophical debate - that is not what he engages in

Almost nobody engages in idealized philosophical debate. It's too hard for people. Their minds are too inflexible and focused on arguing against what instinctively feels wrong to them rather than searching for a deeper truth. The litany of Tarski is a rare and forgotten song. Ergo, I don't see any reason to demean Selebus's aggressive manner of argumentation. People are, indeed, fragile things, and it is the case that any ounce of hostility can shatter fragile hearts. But one concerned about and focusing all of their dialogue on not upsetting anyone will likely not be able to find themselves honestly speaking about anything. If some shattered hearts are what it takes for honesty I will take it. And those who can't handle it are indeed free to hide away out of side while bemoaning what a meanie someone was to them.

PrincessEuphy said:
Yeah, absurd psychoanalysis. Minds are infinite in their complexity and motives are infinite in their arbitrariness. Going around making absent-minded theories as to the inner workings of someone's mind and explaining behavior in a way convenient to you is pretty absurd. If you did that to people in real life they'd punch you in the face or otherwise ostracize you. Ever heard of the fundamental attribution error? It's a bias in which people observing others explain behavior by identifying them as "fundamental attributes," like someone kicking a vending machine to get a drink is just "an angry person" and that's why they're kicking the machine. Whereas if they are the one kicking the machine they instead explain it with momentary or circumstantial reasons, like, "I'm not an angry person today is just a bad day." The position that authors are in is one where thousands of readers are constantly psycho-analyzing them and reading into statements and assigning them fundamental attributes to explain any given act of behavior. That is more depressing than anything. And so far from Selebus being a particular misanthrope in this regard, it's weird people online being weird but not getting the normal social rebukes since it's the internet.

> I'm talking about how he treats people on his discord: he's just a dickhead at times

I would be much more offended by an author lying to my face and talking circles around me to extract more income than one being frank and honest even if their honest opinion happens to be a hostile one. Seriously, why do people bemoan dishonesty so much but then react with such violent negativity to actual honesty when they come across it? Really says a lot.

> I think you're referring to argument in the idealized sense of philosophical debate - that is not what he engages in

Almost nobody engages in idealized philosophical debate. It's too hard for people. Their minds are too inflexible and focused on arguing against what instinctively feels wrong to them rather than searching for a deeper truth. The litany of Tarski is a rare and forgotten song. Ergo, I don't see any reason to demean Selebus's aggressive manner of argumentation. People are, indeed, fragile things, and it is the case that any ounce of hostility can shatter fragile hearts. But one concerned about and focusing all of their dialogue on not upsetting anyone will likely not be able to find themselves honestly speaking about anything. If some shattered hearts are what it takes for honesty I will take it. And those who can't handle it are indeed free to hide away out of side while bemoaning what a meanie someone was to them.

posts.content_html_raw:
There is so much to talk about from this update that everytime I stop to think about it, another thing surfaces.

I had brought up in the past about how we might not ever see "normal" Nodoka in LiL due to the absurd weight that was thrust upon her by her mother, and I think in her last moments that became even more evidently clear. Otoha questions her over the phone about her obssession over her mother, and well, it really is a curse. Nodoka can't break free of it.
It falls on her to save not only 23, but 22 as well (one would assume that's what she means by two worlds).

Also, who is Nodoka referencing here? Her own past self? Shiori? Or her mother? Who came into contact with Himawari? One would assume it was one of her past selves.

Btw, I wonder if there's a hidden meaning to Nodoka being erased by Pareidolia here, since it's the same thing that Sekaori/True Sekai says to Sana:
I'm being led to believe that erasing is something different from resetting. But I guess we'll find out as we discover what happened to Nodoka.

All in all, Nodoka truly has a tragic tale as it became more apparent with each of these last updates. This update just reinforced that point, and also threw our preconceptions of other hated characters (Pareidolia and Sekai) out of the window (or at least made them less black and white).

Edit: Oh, another very relevant thing: gods have to go inside someone, and yet Himawari can fully materialize without a host. What gives? I mean, both Pareidolia (inside a host) and Nodoka are seeing her, right? This isn't an "Akira imagining her there deal".

There is so much to talk about from this update that everytime I stop to think about it, another thing surfaces.

I had brought up in the past about how we might not ever see "normal" Nodoka in LiL due to the absurd weight that was thrust upon her by her mother, and I think in her last moments that became even more evidently clear. Otoha questions her over the phone about her obssession over her mother, and well, it really is a curse. Nodoka can't break free of it.
View attachment 4100398
It falls on her to save not only 23, but 22 as well (one would assume that's what she means by two worlds).

Also, who is Nodoka referencing here? Her own past self? Shiori? Or her mother? Who came into contact with Himawari? One would assume it was one of her past selves.
View attachment 4100406
View attachment 4100409
Btw, I wonder if there's a hidden meaning to Nodoka being erased by Pareidolia here, since it's the same thing that Sekaori/True Sekai says to Sana:
View attachment 4100410
I'm being led to believe that erasing is something different from resetting. But I guess we'll find out as we discover what happened to Nodoka.

All in all, Nodoka truly has a tragic tale as it became more apparent with each of these last updates. This update just reinforced that point, and also threw our preconceptions of other hated characters (Pareidolia and Sekai) out of the window (or at least made them less black and white).
Click to expand...
Presumably, Kyoko dreamed of Himawari which is what Nodoka was probably referring to:
Kyoko Narrator (?) - "An excerpt from a waterlogged journal:"
- "I had a dream of a girl with blue eyes last night."
- "But I guess that's why I've been putting so much emphasis on my dreams lately."
- "On that girl with blue eyes."
DOUBT - "Kyoko? What are you doing? I thought you were going to take a shower?"
(Chapter 3 'An Excerpt From A Waterlogged Journal' Main Event)
This Narrator mentions Ai and Yuko, among other things like making the world, and seems to be Kyoko, Nodoka's mother.

In theory: Himawari has been fucking with the timestream for a while, considering all the hints about her being from a future, she's probably one of the main culprits when it comes to timeline manipulation. Albeit, who knows who else is also from a future or something like that.

After the whole Miu Miyahara possibly being Sekai's mother thing (where does her Red eyes come from?) from last update, with Saki seemingly becoming a stalker (Miu and Saki hated eachother and loved Yuu), I've wondered if that's from an alternative route from 'Nothing Is Beautiful'. Like Miu's route led to Sekai, and Saki's led to Nozomu and Akira.

Something then maybe merged certain aspects of alternative timelines for the main timeline, which became 'Lessons in Love'.

Also, Ami now seems to have two grandmas from the Upside Down House apparently. Grandma Saki (Father's side) and Grandma Miu (Mother's side).

I'm also wondering why Yasu claimed 'Nothing is Beautiful' aka Terminal 22 is gone:
Yasu - "I know it wasn't twenty-two because twenty-two is gone. And twenty-four is wrong, so twenty-three is right! I did a good job!"
(Chapter 3 'Happy Memories' Main Event)
Yet Sensei has traveled to it at least twice it seems, which would imply that he's been time traveling to the past, making him possibly a lot like Himawari. ('Kyoto' takes place after he warned Sekai's mother Miu about Sekai's name, so who knows if he created a new timeline or something)

Theoretically, if one can travel to the past(s) from the present, and back again, there could be some possibility of traveling to the future(s) as well, which may have been shown through timeskips like the one at beachmas. Where Ayane, Maya, and Sensei just wound up 2 months later on the beach.

Overall: Effing time travel.

Also, kind of figured things likely weren't going to go well for Nodoka and she was probably aware of it as well:
Nodoka - "I just want to make memories while I still can."
(Chapter 2 Nodoka 'Coloring Book' Event)
Although, Sensei may have given her some misplaced Hope:
Nodoka - "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't! I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CAN'T...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "A...Akira! You know too! I...can tell! You know...I'm not insane! But she...she never had that! She never had...someone like you!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)

LessonsInDissonance said:
The reason why Himawari was never reset is because she was raised in the slipped dimension, where resets are unnaffected, she keeps getting older despite her mother not being able to.
The reason why Ami had pictures of the girls wearing cosplays they never wore before is because they are memories from distant realities that were hard reset, and they were in boxes because it's just the convenient place to put pictures when you want to move a lot of stuff. The boxes themselves are ordinary, but as long as you slip them, they will be safe until the world is back to normal and you can bring them back.

This means that Maya has always been able to slip, and every time a reset ocurred, she didn't do anything special, she just slipped herself and all of her guests alongside.

Ami can also slip but is pretending to be unaware.

Ayane, my new priest, has learned to slip just recently. If Tsuneyo and Yumi didn't remember anything, it's because she willingfully left them all behind. If I wanted things to stay the same forever, I'd pick someone who also wanted the same.
Click to expand...
So you think that the boxes that Maya was having Sensei lug around were full of photos and memories? That's a sold theory, I like it. Possibly why they would be in Ayane's house, since she saw them after that reset and is trying to "bring Maya back".

Side note: I was thinking about why Kaori was ignoring Maya, if she has Sekai in her it makes sense because Sekai hates Maya. In Something Everyone Knows and Ignores that's all Sekai does is ignore Maya. Wild ass event too.

skwada said:
In that case, how did you install the game? Did you apply the update patch? I'd suggest doing a fresh re-install

edit: actually before reinstalling, another thing you can try is close all the other programs on your computer and see if that makes a difference. a simple way to do this is to restart your pc and then launch LiL without launching any other programs (any programs that auto-run would still be running but ideally, none of those would be particularly RAM-hungry)

also, out of curiosity could you share how much memory your computer has? you can follow this guide to find out: https://www.howtogeek.com/435644/how-to-see-how-much-ram-is-in-your-pc-and-its-speed/
Click to expand...
I went ahead with the fresh re-install and so far it's back to normal! Everything works well hopefully it stays that way. Thanks for the help.

Presumably, Kyoko dreamed of Himawari which is what Nodoka was probably referring to:
View attachment 4100425 View attachment 4100426 View attachment 4100427 View attachment 4100428 View attachment 4100429 Kyoko Narrator (?) - "An excerpt from a waterlogged journal:"

(Chapter 3 'An Excerpt From A Waterlogged Journal' Main Event)
This Narrator mentions Ai and Yuko, among other things like making the world, and seems to be Kyoko, Nodoka's mother.

In theory: Himawari has been fucking with the timestream for a while, considering all the hints about her being from a future, she's probably one of the main culprits when it comes to timeline manipulation. Albeit, who knows who else is also from a future or something like that.

After the whole Miu Miyahara possibly being Sekai's mother thing (where does her Red eyes come from?) from last update, with Saki seemingly becoming a stalker (Miu and Saki hated eachother and loved Yuu), I've wondered if that's from an alternative route from 'Nothing Is Beautiful'. Like Miu's route led to Sekai, and Saki's led to Nozomu and Akira.

Something then maybe merged certain aspects of alternative timelines for the main timeline, which became 'Lessons in Love'.

Also, Ami now seems to have two grandmas from the Upside Down House apparently. Grandma Saki (Father's side) and Grandma Miu (Mother's side).

I'm also wondering why Yasu claimed 'Nothing is Beautiful' aka Terminal 22 is gone:
View attachment 4100453 Yasu - "I know it wasn't twenty-two because twenty-two is gone. And twenty-four is wrong, so twenty-three is right! I did a good job!"
(Chapter 3 'Happy Memories' Main Event)
Yet Sensei has traveled to it at least twice it seems, which would imply that he's been time traveling to the past, making him possibly a lot like Himawari. ('Kyoto' takes place after he warned Sekai's mother Miu about Sekai's name, so who knows if he created a new timeline or something)

Theoretically, if one can travel to the past(s) from the present, and back again, there could be some possibility of traveling to the future(s) as well, which may have been shown through timeskips like the one at beachmas. Where Ayane, Maya, and Sensei just wound up 2 months later on the beach.

Overall: Effing time travel.

Also, kind of figured things likely weren't going to go well for Nodoka and she was probably aware of it as well:
View attachment 4100494 Nodoka - "I just want to make memories while I still can."
(Chapter 2 Nodoka 'Coloring Book' Event)
Although, Sensei may have given her some misplaced Hope:
View attachment 4100509 View attachment 4100495 Nodoka - "I can't...end up like her! I can't! I won't! I...NGAAAAH! FUCK YOU, BRAIN! FUCK YOU, GOD! YOU CAN'T...HIDE...FOREVER!!!!"
- "A...Akira! You know too! I...can tell! You know...I'm not insane! But she...she never had that! She never had...someone like you!"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)
Click to expand...
Didn't Sensei time travel in Good Boy to see Sara? And that one time on the beach with Maya. I'd bet she got it from him.

And if Lessons in Love is 23 and NiB is 22, does that make that upside down house 24? I also had thoughts that it might be the well, for gods that don't have anyone believing in them. Turned into people and thrown in.

Moonflare said:
There is so much to talk about from this update that everytime I stop to think about it, another thing surfaces.

I had brought up in the past about how we might not ever see "normal" Nodoka in LiL due to the absurd weight that was thrust upon her by her mother, and I think in her last moments that became even more evidently clear. Otoha questions her over the phone about her obssession over her mother, and well, it really is a curse. Nodoka can't break free of it.
View attachment 4100398
It falls on her to save not only 23, but 22 as well (one would assume that's what she means by two worlds).

Also, who is Nodoka referencing here? Her own past self? Shiori? Or her mother? Who came into contact with Himawari? One would assume it was one of her past selves.
View attachment 4100406
View attachment 4100409
Btw, I wonder if there's a hidden meaning to Nodoka being erased by Pareidolia here, since it's the same thing that Sekaori/True Sekai says to Sana:
View attachment 4100410
I'm being led to believe that erasing is something different from resetting. But I guess we'll find out as we discover what happened to Nodoka.

All in all, Nodoka truly has a tragic tale as it became more apparent with each of these last updates. This update just reinforced that point, and also threw our preconceptions of other hated characters (Pareidolia and Sekai) out of the window (or at least made them less black and white).

Edit: Oh, another very relevant thing: gods have to go inside someone, and yet Himawari can fully materialize without a host. What gives? I mean, both Pareidolia (inside a host) and Nodoka are seeing her, right? This isn't an "Akira imagining her there deal".
Click to expand...
The her Nodoka mentioned is likely to be Kyoko, who had once dreamed of a girl with blue eyes. I didn't think Nodoka has any other third party source that ever mentioned Himawari's presence.

Some other minor thoughts on this event:
- I was confused about saving the two worlds as well. I thought it was either "this world that is about to be reset" and "the next world that comes after reset" or more metaphorically "Kyoko" and "herself", as figuring out what exactly happened to Kyoko has always been Nodoka's top motivation.

Meanwhile, terminals on the other hand feel less like "worlds or dimensions" and more focus on "gods' favorite toy". That's why it looked like Akira simply went back in time instead of something more unimaginable (like going back a cycle, entering a completely incomprehensible domain, anything of that nature) when he allegedly traveled to terminal 22; that was Yuu's world; that was when Yuu was gods' favorite toy. But all these are just gut feelings.

- I didn't even think about the possibility of Nodoka receiving a selective memory wipe until much later when I first played through the update because, I seriously thought she got bluejayed (I took the "melting her wings very literally"). So when Kaori was having the sex on the roof, I kept thinking "Wait is now a good time to fuck our favorite waitress when Nodoka is probably down there being all splat and everything??" Disclaimer: I didn't think this was the case.

So, on to my general recap of this update. Or more so, things I found interesting and were not talked about yet (or enough).

Starting with one thing that really warmed my heart and gave me confidence that maybe not following the green path might actually be viable in some form. At least that's my copium for now, because this scene was just too beautiful:
View attachment 4095095
View attachment 4095096
View attachment 4095097
View attachment 4095098

Chika is even more delulu and bat-shit insane than I thought after the last update. This is bound to become interesting. Or is it?
Because, hear me out, now that the story, judging by the cliffhanger and the previews so far, is being split and played out in alternative cycles (as some have mentioned, I don't think these will be just previous "states" of the current "canon" cycle) what will happen with current cycle? Will it be "paused", in a perpetual state of limbo until the RAS return somehow from the other cycles? Will they create a new cycle that is shaped by their individual actions in their different timelines?

I'm very interested in how Sel attempts to weave everything back together, as time fuckery is often something writers mess up in the end and that causes the plot to crumble and plot holes to amass.
I'm not as pessimistic as Moonflare on this and believe Sel still has control over this and manages to make sense of it, but I also still get the feeling that it gets more and more convoluted and more difficult to fit into everything else.
We will see.

Now on to a few points that I would like to ask the help of the lore master squad (LMS) for.
There is a few things here. First off, who is the handsome man planting the tree supposed to be?
View attachment 4095154
This whole section where Sekai narrates Tsuneyo's "wet dream" of having sex with Akira is confusing me. Is Sekai projecting her experience on her? Is she talking about how she was deflowered at a young age by her father (Yuu?)? How it made her hear the voices of the gods, i.e. letting the gods reside in her? Is that why Yuu did it, because the gods told him to do so, like the gods told Sekai to molest Akira so they can reside in him? And why they tell Akira to cum inside the other girls, so the gods can use them as vessels as well? Is this all just a perpetual chain of gods finding vessels in which they can take form?

Why else would Akira be so obviously possessed and driven to impregnate Molly in this scene? This gives very clear HOPE vibes.
View attachment 4095167

Now I really liked this scene. Not only because I like both of the girls a lot, I feel like the narrator's words will become very significant. I just can't tell who it is.
View attachment 4095200
I feel like this line specifically suggests it would be someone who actually was invited to this specific party, as they stress that there are other alternate timelines/cycles/planes of this version of the event taking place where they are technically not invited, but another version of them. Am I reading too much into it?
In that case I would say it could be either current Maya (not Maya Prime) from the future with her knowledge returned. Or current Akira, again with future knowledge, who has become a god/narrator of some sort. Or even Ayane or Makoto with a similar fate. Or even Sana? Nodoka?

Now let's look at the transcript so far:
View attachment 4095211
This is pretty obviously foreshadowing the cliffhanger, that the RAS is spread around different timelines, different parties "they were not invited to". That it's not important only where they are but when they are.
What is additionally mentioned is that what is going to happen in those other timelines might be more dangerous or worse than what happens in this one. That there or "other walls" that are "even harder to scale". That gods don't want them to just slip jump to other planes and timelines, fearing that, they will end up too close to the truth, just like Nodoka? That sometimes it's better to remain unaware and be happy with what you have, to just be complacent.

Now the next section becomes even more interesting and more personal:
View attachment 4095226
So the narrator says that this opinion is just the ones of the gods, basically. Though the narrator still comes to the same conclusion, just even more drastic. They don't want you to stand out, to do anything at all, just remain in place because they fear you might leave. Also someone who wants to suffocate? That brings to mind the image of Maya hanging in the room full of clocks...
Who are they addressing now anyway? Is it Akira? Or maybe the player directly? After all, the end of Sensei Quest suggests that there is a player who is playing the game.
View attachment 4095244
It could all be a simulation after all. An experiment.
Though, it could just as likely be Sel throwing in red herrings and misguiding us.

But let's leave it at that for now and focus on the rest of the narrator's monologue:
View attachment 4095356
So here they clearly mention that they built this world. It has been mentioned several times that the world has been built for Akira, but never that he was the one building it. At this point I really don't think Akira is the narrator.
One thing I absolutely didn't get is what the multicolored glow is supposed to mean. Could this be a reference to the trinity of gods? The only character that would really fit here directly would be Nao I guess.
This would will remain as long as the rules are followed. A.k.a. as long as nobody makes it break like Maya did with several of the ones she destroyed when trying to explain it to Akira, etc. Would that suggest it's Maya, since she knows all about the rules?
And maybe the most significant line: "Don't leave me alone again."
Who was left alone? Prime Maya when she was snapped out of existence and forced into another plane? Or Ayane, who has now slipped jumped to another cycle? Makoto is still with Akira in hers. But New Maya isn't.
Or, was Himawari the narrator all along?

I'm really confused by this, someone with a wrinklier brain needs to spoon-feed me answers to this eventually.

This was quite beautiful. First of all, I have to send my apologies to our man Pareidolia. My very first message in this thread was about comparing him to a user who posted a negative review for this game on here. If the things he said this update are true, and they surprisingly make sense actually, then it seems like he was a scapegoat and didn't deserve the hate I harbored for him. Let's see if this will remain true.

Similarly, I found it very satisfactory that we got some direct lore for Sekai, showing her "true" self and making her more humane and understandable in my eyes now. Given that she has been most likely plagued by the same voices/gods as Yuu and Akira, it paints her past actions in a different light.
I also am 100% convinced now that Ami is Akira's child. Here is where, I believe, Sekai is excited to tell Akira about how the child is his once they are in Kyoto, she really looks like she considers the pregnancy a good thing, like it's a manifestation of their love and an anchor that will hold them together.
View attachment 4095313
It's only once she realizes that he would be unhappy when forced away from Niki, that she decides not to tell him Ami is his, as it would make him change his mind and go with her. She knows she would be the one that made him unable to fulfill his desires, robbing him of the chance of a somewhat normal life with a partner his age, without the burden of a scandalous child, so in a twisted sense, her love for him made her keep it a secret from him. Which becomes even more tragic considering she dies basically because she stayed.

I really liked this scene, it was one of the very few ones that shows how she was really a good person deep down. And it makes me question whether the ghost Sekai really is the true Sekai or some other, more obsessed, form.

Also on a side note: The party scenes where Good Kid was playing made me realize once more that those songs clash with having to read text and being able to process them properly, it's just too distracting. Even though that particular song wasn't that bad.
In fact, I actually really liked the 8bit version in Sensei Quest. Call me a filthy millennial, but it was a bop.
So in conclusion, I like their music. It just doesn't always fit unfortunately.

This will be a huge block of text until I can get to my pc and format it right.

1. There is a very real possibility that the time travel is part of the reset and it isn't done yet. Failing that, they can all slip back without altering anything. If they do alter stuff then the timeline cohesion is doomed. Reconstructing any sort of timeline from this point forward would be a fool's errand.

2. The scene with Uta and Kirin really is interesting because we have two girls that are marked by being perceived as sluts (either by others or by themselves). Yet the freaking good kid song makes concentrating on any of it super hard.

Other than that, about the walls closing in, it's also what the vigenere cipher says at the end of Yasu's event (I missed that when writing the triggers post).

3. Who's this world made by and who got left behind. There are a ton of possibilities. Amy's boyfriend left her at the mall with her mom. Ami has mentioned on their bus ride backwards that when they are alone at the end of the world it would be nice if Akira could ride them around, suggesting Ami (or the entity inside her aka super Ami) has been left my Akira multiple times at the end of a cycle. In Perfect Harmony, the narrator states that their perfect gate could never be reached in their world because Akira (assumed) left it.

As for who the world is for, we just got confirmation that 22 is likely Yuu's world and 23 is Akira's. Unless Selebus wishes to bring in the concept of a world made for the interloper/player that takes agency on that world by inserting itself into Yuu or Akira, then it's likely made for them (as they're in the center of it).

That however begs the question what their objective is, since, if it's to prepare a vessel to ride around in, then from Kyoto we get the feeling that Kaori/Sekai was that objective achieving fruition, and yet, there is no terminal 22.5 that is for Sekai/Kaori.

Another possible solution is that 23 was never Akira's to begin with, but Sekai's world. Akira doesn't reside in apartment 23, it's Kaori/Sekaori that do. It would certainly explain why the gods, although interested in him, don't seem to place him at the center of their plans. Mind you, we could also interpret Pareidolia saying that he waited such a long time to board Kaori as "boarding Kaori is what allows him to make spring arrive".

In that sense, HOPE, Wires, Pareidolia and USER4 control the seasons from inside Kaori, which makes Kaori the real center of 23 (or rather, True Sekai).

anothersilo said:
I know this question has been asked on this thread a dozen times already, but I haven't seen an answer I actually like yet. Are there any games out there that match this game's quality? It doesn't have to be like LiL plotwise in literally any way. But despite all of his (many) flaws, Selebus clearly puts his soul into this game. There are reveals now that have clearly been planned out for years. And the characters just feel so. so. human. And when I go from LiL to playing literally any other game on this site, they all just feel so bland and one-dimensional in comparison. I just want a game that doesn't feel like an immediate downgrade. Something I can immerse myself in, with characters I'll genuinely care about. Something I'll actually think about after I'm done playing it.

It's going to be a month until the next update, and I really want another game to play while I'm waiting. Anyone have any suggestions?

anothersilo said:
I know this question has been asked on this thread a dozen times already, but I haven't seen an answer I actually like yet. Are there any games out there that match this game's quality? It doesn't have to be like LiL plotwise in literally any way. But despite all of his (many) flaws, Selebus clearly puts his soul into this game. There are reveals now that have clearly been planned out for years. And the characters just feel so. so. human. And when I go from LiL to playing literally any other game on this site, they all just feel so bland and one-dimensional in comparison. I just want a game that doesn't feel like an immediate downgrade. Something I can immerse myself in, with characters I'll genuinely care about. Something I'll actually think about after I'm done playing it.

It's going to be a month until the next update, and I really want another game to play while I'm waiting. Anyone have any suggestions?
Click to expand...
I'll try to suggest a few that aren't that well known. It will be a downgrade either way, but you can try these:

renpy - BOAT (finished); Monster girl 1000 (finished); My tuition academia (finished); harem hotel; corrupted kingdoms; mythic manor; goddesses' whim; Long live the princess (finished).

rpgm - The last sovereign (free on steam); Noblesse oblige (free on steam); Renryuu's ascension; Demons roots (finished).

unity (?) - Hush hush (finished); how to build a magnificent kingdom (finished); Unveiling the unknown (finished).

*all that are finished have either compelling stories or at least some sort of twist. From these, the best is magnificent kingdom but it's also the one with the most troublesome gameplay to get to that story. The easiest is BOAT. The most unexpected would be tuition academia's true end.

**from the unfinished ones, the best in terms of story is last sovereign, the other rpgm also try to tell a story but tls is almost done. The renpy ones are not that great in story, but lacking willpower to power through better stories with worse gameplay, they'll do.

Edit: As always, Higurashi; Tsukihime; Steins;Gate (original and 0); and the Fate series (especially stay/night and hollow/ataraxia) stand as overall recommendations due to their legacy to the genre.

The most relevant recommendation would be for you to watch the entirety of the Monogatari Series though, since it's on par if not superior to LiL in every way and deals with a lot of the same themes.

I'm not sure "Kyoto" actually breaks the time line. Why do people assume the "It's probably just Noriko trying to sneak in like she always does" line, has to be her spying on their sexual exploits, it could simply just be Noriko crawling around, trying to get in for standard baby curiosity/exploring and crawling around reasons.
It wouldn't be particularly strange if you say Ami is around a year younger, as an around 1 year old can start to sort of "walk" around and will definitely be crawling around fairly effectively by around that age. The sneaking in line could probably just a bit of a joke from Niki about Noriko always crawling around into places she shouldn't be or something like that. The stuff I think I remember Noriko saying about secretly watching Akira and Niki doing Things can easily happen later in the timeline.

So I don't see why this breaks It? unless I missed something someone has already posted.

Wait... I am dumb!

I realised after I typed this that you would have to subtract Sekai's pregnancy months off Noriko's age in that scenario, If they are 1 year apart. So I can see why it could slightly break the time line. But even then it's still somewhat feasible. Although you might have to lean heavily on the Noriko child prodigy stuff and decide that she might have been a bit ahead of the curve development wise.

Lets say for argument's sake, Sekai told Akira she was pregnant around the end of the 2nd month. (I guess you could go a bit later if you wanted.) If you go off the listed birthdays Niki and Ami are 1 month apart. Then you add 3 months for the approximate date of conception. Then 2 more for Sekai telling Akira (More if you want, 1 possibly 2 at the most I think.). You endup at 6-8 months. Google says baby can start crawling at around 7 months. Then say she is super child prodigy that started crawling around mid 5 or 6 months age. It still fits the timeline I think? Although perhaps it is a bit of a stretch.
