General thoughts / notes / questions about installment 44:

  • An 'older' destiny 'awaits several others' around Christmas? Obvious foreshadowing, but what could it be? Sounds like some of the girls are bound for trouble on January 1. Ref:
  • Futaba's parents are gone, which seems to be the prompt for the next step of her story. Too bad it's only going to get worse.
  • Glad to see Chika, Kirin, and Rin gleefully violating Halloween Rule 2.
  • Like Touka, I too am more and more sure that Tsuneyo is an exhibitionist. Excellent.
  • It's still weird how on-board Ami seems about Niki moving in. I keep thinking she sees it as an opportunity to kill Niki somehow.
  • I see things a little better from the current Maya's perspective after her outburst. It must be pretty scary having Sensei change overnight like that. Further development with her could get interesting.

  • Good conversation between Makoto and Yumi. It gets to the important point that even in an eternal world, your actions truly matter.
  • Makoto told Miku to put the ghost decorations wherever she wanted, then Miku made a joke about Makoto pretending to be an interior designer. Awfully uncalled-for!
  • The box found by Noriko... I believe that it's information from a forgotten past, but within the resets or before? Why label it 'Ami'? Could that be the mechanism of preservation, or is it simply the box?
  • Rin's crotch is shown far too little.
  • Chika is spouting utter nonsense. What would it mean for her to 'infect' Yumi?
  • The interaction with Io on the false path is absurd. Sensei's words don't fit his character at all. Further proof that the choices are illusions and missing events is wrong.
  • The interaction with Io on the true path is sad, but it makes sense.
  • Touka and Yasu deep in Ayane's house having a repeating conversation, almost like they've already been caught up in the reset. I was sad to see Yasu so unwell.
  • 'the walls are closing in'... Perhaps this new green :) marks the start of the reset proper.
  • Tsuneyo is crazy hot, but really, no shots of her crotch or butt? Molly oiling her up naked is a pretty great thought. She has a crazy sex daydream facilitated by the free-roaming Sekai 'ghost'. Cool to see her tied up, I guess.
  • In her dorm room with Maya, Ami positively confirms that she is aware of the resets. Not sure we've seen that before.
  • Impressive detective work by Nodoka continues. The switch from Otoha to Himawari-as-Otoha was perfectly done and had me as confused as Nodoka for a minute. Again we see Himawari trying to rescue someone. She doesn't always succeed.
  • More English lyrics made it near-impossible to read and temporarily ruined the atmosphere.
  • Conversation between Akira and five girls was weird. Sana could hear selectively, while Noriko could hear nothing. They're all reset to the beginning of the conversation and then interrupted.

  • An abrupt end to the party with Nao-chan's arrival. Few interactions with or between the girls. This one felt even more abbreviated than last Halloween!
  • A couple times it seemed like Nao-chan was about to speak for the first time. I wonder whether these were intentional teases and whether she'll ever talk.
  • Akira is relieved to depart the party again. They ride on Kaori's giant cock... is he real? Have other characters seen him?
  • What's going on with the shot of Maya kneeling next to a sunflower? It's memorable to Akira. Have we seen that before?
  • Akira appears by a lake, speaks with a woman who is evidently Sekai's mother. This scene gives the strong impression that Sekai and Akira were born by the same man. What an incestuous mess.
  • Would it make sense for Yuu to have impregnated both Miu (Sekai) and Saki (Nozumu), then later Saki again (Akira)?
  • Why does Nao-chan want Akira to be happy? How was she created?

  • Akira heads to the roof, and we're really in it now.
  • Kaori certainly does not behave like she did when we first met her.
  • What did the possessed Kaori do to Nodoka, exactly? I think it's most likely she'll remember nothing.
  • I don't put much stock in Pareidolia's speech. He even says he's lying! I don't think we can possibly tell now what it means.
  • He also stops speaking through Kaori before saying he has sacrificed himself. Are we dealing with two different entities?
  • I knew that we were going to just jump to full penetration of Kaori... Is one shot of stripping or foreplay too much to hope for? Apparently so. Sensei's expression mirrors my own.
  • We do seem to be interacting with some sort of mix between Kaori and Sekai. Kaori starts speaking for Sekai, which is an interesting dynamic. The sex is kind of hot.
  • The shot of Nao-chan drawing another picture of The Old One and hitting Akira with a thumbs-up is hilarious.

  • Suddenly we're not on the roof, but in a reset room. No surprise here at all.
  • SENSEI-QUEST, by Shiawase group... did Himawari create this experience? Is it an alternative to a worse reset?
  • Metal Dogslime is huge and hard and shiny and ready to fuck.
  • Kenji is now my favorite transient character.
  • I actually like the 8-bit GK tracks a lot. Look up the soundtrack for "Ghost King's Revenge".
  • Boss fights are silly but not too bad, and the text is really funny, classic reset fare.
  • It seems like there's some meaning to the appearance of youdidit and Moyo. Who is The Hyphenated One? And what is the Dark Entity the two of them go to feed themselves to?

Take and hypotheses about the culmination:

Kyoto is a catalyst that revealed severe inconsistency in all the material we've been shown regarding Akira and Niki's relationship timeline. It appears to me that no matter which way you cut it up, you're still left with obvious violations of causality. These troubles are pervasive and existed long before this update. I don't think this is any kind of mistake on Selebus's part. We're just getting more pieces to a complex puzzle.

Here are some items I think we can take as true-as-it-gets:
  • Through the entire story, the current year is 2020
  • Akira Arakawa is 31 years old
  • Akira was 23 years old at the time of the accident that killed Sekai
  • The main girls are all either 14, 15, or 16 years old
Here's what I think is near-certainly true within the context of Kyoto:
  • By the first phase (Niki and Akira together), their romance started 1+ year prior, and Noriko is at least 3 years old.
  • During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.
  • The third phase (portrait of Sekai) depicts her funeral, just after the accident.
I think the following are the "cleanest" places to put these phases in the timeline based on the information depicted. The first phase (Niki's room) takes place in 2008 or later, Akira being 19 years old. The second phase takes place in 2005, Akira being 16 years old. The third phase takes place in 2012, Akira being 23 years old.

However, even taking the first two phases as distinct times, they still don't fit! Confounding factors:
  • Akira and Niki determinedly call each other 'friends' even though they should have started "officially" dating by 2007, according to Niki. (Note: 'friend' may be a pet name! Niki also uses it during the tour.)
  • Niki pushes Akira to have sex and he resists, even though they never had sex while dating because Akira 'never pushed [her]', according to Niki.
  • Based on the tour, Noriko was 5 or older when Niki and Akira were playing in the woods, pretending to be 'an underground crime-fighting organization', at a time predating the start of their romance. That would make Noriko at least 18 years old in 2020. Her information card from the care packages refutes this.
  • Akira tutored Noriko after the accident, likely from 2014 to 2017, when she should have been 13 years old. This makes her 3 years old at the absolute most at the time of the first kiss. The last point could not have happened in that case.
Between the flashback, the tour, and Kyoto, every interpretation has apparently irreconcilable failures.

That brings me to the most important point about Kyoto I have not seen anyone mention: this is a Happy Event! Throughout the story, these events have taken us to places beyond the regular world of Kumon-mi, shown us fantastically unreal happenings, and used baffling collages of imagery to confuse us.

Should we consider Kyoto much more "real" just because it appears to show real events at first glance? I think not. I think that we should regard it, like the others, as a confusing melange that points directly at only part of the truth.

I think the confusion over timelines is intentional and part of what marks this as a Happy Event, along with the aforementioned Windows XP wallpaper and train platform full of Kenji. Kyoto could essentially be a dream constructed in Sensei's reset-addled mind out of elements that never really coexisted.

In any case, I think the most we can take from the event for the moment is that Sekai was likely more sympathetic than we have previously been led to believe, as well as some points in favor of Ami being Akira's true daughter, and further evidence that Niki and Noriko are somehow not as they seem.

The Orb, as has been mentioned, is the same entity shown in the Ayane-Maya selfie from a prior reset. At this point it seems like the Sensei-Quest world is crossing back over into the real world. Perhaps Akira was on the roof the entire time?

Meowri calls the Orb a 'dark entity', so I suppose this is what the Red Twins fed themselves to? I wonder whether we'll see those two again. Maybe this is a significant inflection point.

A successful Orb fight incurs no damage, then once the final attack is made, the Orb deals immense damage to Sensei without killing him. I think Sensei's desperate plea is notable:

s "Stop! Please! I’ll leave you alone! I’ll be good! I’ll stay here forever!"

These are the answers to Akira's deepest worries. When he's at his lowest, these are the things he desperately tries in order to make things right. He tries to leave the girls alone. He tries to be a good person. He (almost) decides to stay in the room for the rest of his life.

This makes me think that the Orb is the darkness within Akira, and the battle is a doomed metaphorical attempt to defeat it. But something prevents it from consuming him entirely.

In the final moments on the roof, the name above the Orb's health bar changes to 'GOD' and the view warps, breaking down into horizontal bands and primary colors as if it were the last render of a crashing computer program. I also feel as if there's a head or some other image behind the Orb, here, but I don't know what.



Then everything stops and we see a Windows BSOD memory error on a cracked screen, accompanied by an intense electronic hum. Then we zoom out and the error is revealed to be on a curved computer monitor. We seem to have the perspective of the individual sitting at the console. Who or what is this?



We hear the gun cocking sound from Paper City, followed by a single shot, and then the opening messages to Lessons in Love play. Did the person at the console shoot the computer? Did somebody else shoot the person at the console? Was this moment part of Akira's conscious experience?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

A stab at theory-crafting:

There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

This was a good update, lots to think about, and it's been a while since I've anticipated the next installment so much. It really is amazing that this story has been going strong, fueling so much genuine interest, for so long. It's the only thing I've ever read that has almost felt like another life.

For thematic similarity, Dissonance is the only real contender.
For pure quality, all I can do is second the recommendations for Perfect Pitch and Pale Carnations.

Here's what I think is near-certainly true within the context of Kyoto:
  • By the first phase (Niki and Akira together), their romance started 1+ year prior, and Noriko is at least 3 years old.
  • During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.
  • The third phase (portrait of Sekai) depicts her funeral, just after the accident.
I think the following are the "cleanest" places to put these phases in the timeline based on the information depicted. The first phase (Niki's room) takes place in 2008 or later, Akira being 19 years old. The second phase takes place in 2005, Akira being 16 years old. The third phase takes place in 2012, Akira being 23 years old.

However, even taking the first two phases as distinct times, they still don't fit! Confounding factors:
  • Akira and Niki determinedly call each other 'friends' even though they should have started "officially" dating by 2007, according to Niki. (Note: 'friend' may be a pet name! Niki also uses it during the tour.)
  • Niki pushes Akira to have sex and he resists, even though they never had sex while dating because Akira 'never pushed [her]', according to Niki.
  • Based on the tour, Noriko was 5 or older when Niki and Akira were playing in the woods, pretending to be 'an underground crime-fighting organization', at a time predating the start of their romance. That would make Noriko at least 18 years old in 2020. Her information card from the care packages refutes this.
  • Akira tutored Noriko after the accident, likely from 2014 to 2017, when she should have been 13 years old. This makes her 3 years old at the absolute most at the time of the first kiss. The last point could not have happened in that case.
Between the flashback, the tour, and Kyoto, every interpretation has apparently irreconcilable failures.

That brings me to the most important point about Kyoto I have not seen anyone mention: this is a Happy Event! Throughout the story, these events have taken us to places beyond the regular world of Kumon-mi, shown us fantastically unreal happenings, and used baffling collages of imagery to confuse us.

Should we consider Kyoto much more "real" just because it appears to show real events at first glance? I think not. I think that we should regard it, like the others, as a confusing melange that points directly at only part of the truth.

I think the confusion over timelines is intentional and part of what marks this as a Happy Event, along with the aforementioned Windows XP wallpaper and train platform full of Kenji. Kyoto could essentially be a dream constructed in Sensei's reset-addled mind out of elements that never really coexisted.

In any case, I think the most we can take from the event for the moment is that Sekai was likely more sympathetic than we have previously been led to believe, as well as some points in favor of Ami being Akira's true daughter, and further evidence that Niki and Noriko are somehow not as they seem.

spoilers.title: The Orb
spoilers.html:
The Orb, as has been mentioned, is the same entity shown in the Ayane-Maya selfie from a prior reset. At this point it seems like the Sensei-Quest world is crossing back over into the real world. Perhaps Akira was on the roof the entire time?

Meowri calls the Orb a 'dark entity', so I suppose this is what the Red Twins fed themselves to? I wonder whether we'll see those two again. Maybe this is a significant inflection point.

A successful Orb fight incurs no damage, then once the final attack is made, the Orb deals immense damage to Sensei without killing him. I think Sensei's desperate plea is notable:

s "Stop! Please! I’ll leave you alone! I’ll be good! I’ll stay here forever!"

These are the answers to Akira's deepest worries. When he's at his lowest, these are the things he desperately tries in order to make things right. He tries to leave the girls alone. He tries to be a good person. He (almost) decides to stay in the room for the rest of his life.

This makes me think that the Orb is the darkness within Akira, and the battle is a doomed metaphorical attempt to defeat it. But something prevents it from consuming him entirely.

In the final moments on the roof, the name above the Orb's health bar changes to 'GOD' and the view warps, breaking down into horizontal bands and primary colors as if it were the last render of a crashing computer program. I also feel as if there's a head or some other image behind the Orb, here, but I don't know what.



Then everything stops and we see a Windows BSOD memory error on a cracked screen, accompanied by an intense electronic hum. Then we zoom out and the error is revealed to be on a curved computer monitor. We seem to have the perspective of the individual sitting at the console. Who or what is this?



We hear the gun cocking sound from Paper City, followed by a single shot, and then the opening messages to Lessons in Love play. Did the person at the console shoot the computer? Did somebody else shoot the person at the console? Was this moment part of Akira's conscious experience?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Sekai
spoilers.html:
There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Noriko
spoilers.html:
Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

A stab at theory-crafting:

There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

This was a good update, lots to think about, and it's been a while since I've anticipated the next installment so much. It really is amazing that this story has been going strong, fueling so much genuine interest, for so long. It's the only thing I've ever read that has almost felt like another life.

For thematic similarity, Dissonance is the only real contender.
For pure quality, all I can do is second the recommendations for Perfect Pitch and Pale Carnations.
Click to expand...
Maya's crouching down scene is from the first reset, in which a being dressed as Maya (unlikely to be her) sends Akira into 22 to meet Saki.

We haven't really touched upon the orb, so I think it's appropriate to draw attention to the fact that Akira had to recover 4 different orbs, in order to put them together to form a black orb that changes its name to "GOD", as it keeps trying to consume him by the end. As in 4 different parts of a god, that are drawn together to make the whole god - and it's angry. Pareidolia also sacrificed itself to something that was angry.

This doesn't need to mean that Akira put the god together in this reset, but it could be foreshadowing to what's going to happen eventually. Also, the random god that appears after Pareidolia is gone has already appeared when Akira tries to kill himself, but the four "heroines" show up to convince him otherwise (at the dorms).

Interesting theory on Kyoto, no one had theorized that Kyoto could be two differents parts put together. I don't buy it, but at this point we're welcoming anything.

Akira Arakawa is 31 years old

During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.

spoilers.title: Kyoto
spoilers.html:
Kyoto is a catalyst that revealed severe inconsistency in all the material we've been shown regarding Akira and Niki's relationship timeline. It appears to me that no matter which way you cut it up, you're still left with obvious violations of causality. These troubles are pervasive and existed long before this update. I don't think this is any kind of mistake on Selebus's part. We're just getting more pieces to a complex puzzle.

Here are some items I think we can take as true-as-it-gets:
  • Through the entire story, the current year is 2020
  • Akira Arakawa is 31 years old
  • Akira was 23 years old at the time of the accident that killed Sekai
  • The main girls are all either 14, 15, or 16 years old
Here's what I think is near-certainly true within the context of Kyoto:
  • By the first phase (Niki and Akira together), their romance started 1+ year prior, and Noriko is at least 3 years old.
  • During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.
  • The third phase (portrait of Sekai) depicts her funeral, just after the accident.
I think the following are the "cleanest" places to put these phases in the timeline based on the information depicted. The first phase (Niki's room) takes place in 2008 or later, Akira being 19 years old. The second phase takes place in 2005, Akira being 16 years old. The third phase takes place in 2012, Akira being 23 years old.

However, even taking the first two phases as distinct times, they still don't fit! Confounding factors:
  • Akira and Niki determinedly call each other 'friends' even though they should have started "officially" dating by 2007, according to Niki. (Note: 'friend' may be a pet name! Niki also uses it during the tour.)
  • Niki pushes Akira to have sex and he resists, even though they never had sex while dating because Akira 'never pushed [her]', according to Niki.
  • Based on the tour, Noriko was 5 or older when Niki and Akira were playing in the woods, pretending to be 'an underground crime-fighting organization', at a time predating the start of their romance. That would make Noriko at least 18 years old in 2020. Her information card from the care packages refutes this.
  • Akira tutored Noriko after the accident, likely from 2014 to 2017, when she should have been 13 years old. This makes her 3 years old at the absolute most at the time of the first kiss. The last point could not have happened in that case.
Between the flashback, the tour, and Kyoto, every interpretation has apparently irreconcilable failures.

That brings me to the most important point about Kyoto I have not seen anyone mention: this is a Happy Event! Throughout the story, these events have taken us to places beyond the regular world of Kumon-mi, shown us fantastically unreal happenings, and used baffling collages of imagery to confuse us.

Should we consider Kyoto much more "real" just because it appears to show real events at first glance? I think not. I think that we should regard it, like the others, as a confusing melange that points directly at only part of the truth.

I think the confusion over timelines is intentional and part of what marks this as a Happy Event, along with the aforementioned Windows XP wallpaper and train platform full of Kenji. Kyoto could essentially be a dream constructed in Sensei's reset-addled mind out of elements that never really coexisted.

In any case, I think the most we can take from the event for the moment is that Sekai was likely more sympathetic than we have previously been led to believe, as well as some points in favor of Ami being Akira's true daughter, and further evidence that Niki and Noriko are somehow not as they seem.

spoilers.title: The Orb
spoilers.html:
The Orb, as has been mentioned, is the same entity shown in the Ayane-Maya selfie from a prior reset. At this point it seems like the Sensei-Quest world is crossing back over into the real world. Perhaps Akira was on the roof the entire time?

Meowri calls the Orb a 'dark entity', so I suppose this is what the Red Twins fed themselves to? I wonder whether we'll see those two again. Maybe this is a significant inflection point.

A successful Orb fight incurs no damage, then once the final attack is made, the Orb deals immense damage to Sensei without killing him. I think Sensei's desperate plea is notable:

s "Stop! Please! I’ll leave you alone! I’ll be good! I’ll stay here forever!"

These are the answers to Akira's deepest worries. When he's at his lowest, these are the things he desperately tries in order to make things right. He tries to leave the girls alone. He tries to be a good person. He (almost) decides to stay in the room for the rest of his life.

This makes me think that the Orb is the darkness within Akira, and the battle is a doomed metaphorical attempt to defeat it. But something prevents it from consuming him entirely.

In the final moments on the roof, the name above the Orb's health bar changes to 'GOD' and the view warps, breaking down into horizontal bands and primary colors as if it were the last render of a crashing computer program. I also feel as if there's a head or some other image behind the Orb, here, but I don't know what.

View attachment 4106721

Then everything stops and we see a Windows BSOD memory error on a cracked screen, accompanied by an intense electronic hum. Then we zoom out and the error is revealed to be on a curved computer monitor. We seem to have the perspective of the individual sitting at the console. Who or what is this?

View attachment 4106737

We hear the gun cocking sound from Paper City, followed by a single shot, and then the opening messages to Lessons in Love play. Did the person at the console shoot the computer? Did somebody else shoot the person at the console? Was this moment part of Akira's conscious experience?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Sekai
spoilers.html:
There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Noriko
spoilers.html:
Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

It was mentioned, albeit briefly, that there is echo'd dialogue between Sekai and Niki





In general, I would be interested in more exploration into "Echo Theory" as it's been dubbed, which is the presence of echoing dialogue, poses, framing, etc throughout the loops. It is most natural to imagine that the significance of such echoed content is that it came from the same source - but it is somewhat hard to imagine Sensei hallucinating Niki as Sekai, or Sekai as Niki (although he does hallucinate Sekai in this scene). What exactly is the significance of a line being used 1:1? Why do all the girls want to him to be stupid with them? Why is it that everyone says "Tell me you see me" and "Are you okay"? I think one may begin to think that the source could be Sensei, and that he is projecting it all; looping his life. But it is surely more than that, too?

  • An 'older' destiny 'awaits several others' around Christmas? Obvious foreshadowing, but what could it be? Sounds like some of the girls are bound for trouble on January 1. Ref: View attachment 4107226
  • Futaba's parents are gone, which seems to be the prompt for the next step of her story. Too bad it's only going to get worse.

  • It's still weird how on-board Ami seems about Niki moving in. I keep thinking she sees it as an opportunity to kill Niki somehow.
  • I see things a little better from the current Maya's perspective after her outburst. It must be pretty scary having Sensei change overnight like that. Further development with her could get interesting.

  • Good conversation between Makoto and Yumi. It gets to the important point that even in an eternal world, your actions truly matter.
  • Makoto told Miku to put the ghost decorations wherever she wanted, then Miku made a joke about Makoto pretending to be an interior designer. Awfully uncalled-for!

  • The interaction with Io on the true path is sad, but it makes sense.
  • Touka and Yasu deep in Ayane's house having a repeating conversation, almost like they've already been caught up in the reset. I was sad to see Yasu so unwell.
  • 'the walls are closing in'... Perhaps this new green :) marks the start of the reset proper.
  • Tsuneyo is crazy hot, but really, no shots of her crotch or butt? Molly oiling her up naked is a pretty great thought. She has a crazy sex daydream facilitated by the free-roaming Sekai 'ghost'. Cool to see her tied up, I guess.
  • In her dorm room with Maya, Ami positively confirms that she is aware of the resets. Not sure we've seen that before.

  • Akira is relieved to depart the party again. They ride on Kaori's giant cock... is he real? Have other characters seen him?
  • What's going on with the shot of Maya kneeling next to a sunflower? It's memorable to Akira. Have we seen that before?
  • Akira appears by a lake, speaks with a woman who is evidently Sekai's mother. This scene gives the strong impression that Sekai and Akira were born by the same man. What an incestuous mess.
  • Would it make sense for Yuu to have impregnated both Miu (Sekai) and Saki (Nozumu), then later Saki again (Akira)?
  • Why does Nao-chan want Akira to be happy? How was she created?

  • He also stops speaking through Kaori before saying he has sacrificed himself. Are we dealing with two different entities?
  • I knew that we were going to just jump to full penetration of Kaori... Is one shot of stripping or foreplay too much to hope for? Apparently so. Sensei's expression mirrors my own.
  • We do seem to be interacting with some sort of mix between Kaori and Sekai. Kaori starts speaking for Sekai, which is an interesting dynamic. The sex is kind of hot.
  • The shot of Nao-chan drawing another picture of The Old One and hitting Akira with a thumbs-up is hilarious.

  • Suddenly we're not on the roof, but in a reset room. No surprise here at all.
  • SENSEI-QUEST, by Shiawase group... did Himawari create this experience? Is it an alternative to a worse reset?
  • Metal Dogslime is huge and hard and shiny and ready to fuck.
  • Kenji is now my favorite transient character.

  • Boss fights are silly but not too bad, and the text is really funny, classic reset fare.
  • It seems like there's some meaning to the appearance of youdidit and Moyo. Who is The Hyphenated One? And what is the Dark Entity the two of them go to feed themselves to?

Take and hypotheses about the culmination:

Kyoto is a catalyst that revealed severe inconsistency in all the material we've been shown regarding Akira and Niki's relationship timeline. It appears to me that no matter which way you cut it up, you're still left with obvious violations of causality. These troubles are pervasive and existed long before this update. I don't think this is any kind of mistake on Selebus's part. We're just getting more pieces to a complex puzzle.

Here are some items I think we can take as true-as-it-gets:
  • Through the entire story, the current year is 2020
  • Akira Arakawa is 31 years old
  • Akira was 23 years old at the time of the accident that killed Sekai
  • The main girls are all either 14, 15, or 16 years old
Here's what I think is near-certainly true within the context of Kyoto:
  • By the first phase (Niki and Akira together), their romance started 1+ year prior, and Noriko is at least 3 years old.
  • During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.
  • The third phase (portrait of Sekai) depicts her funeral, just after the accident.
I think the following are the "cleanest" places to put these phases in the timeline based on the information depicted. The first phase (Niki's room) takes place in 2008 or later, Akira being 19 years old. The second phase takes place in 2005, Akira being 16 years old. The third phase takes place in 2012, Akira being 23 years old.

However, even taking the first two phases as distinct times, they still don't fit! Confounding factors:
  • Akira and Niki determinedly call each other 'friends' even though they should have started "officially" dating by 2007, according to Niki. (Note: 'friend' may be a pet name! Niki also uses it during the tour.)
  • Niki pushes Akira to have sex and he resists, even though they never had sex while dating because Akira 'never pushed [her]', according to Niki.
  • Based on the tour, Noriko was 5 or older when Niki and Akira were playing in the woods, pretending to be 'an underground crime-fighting organization', at a time predating the start of their romance. That would make Noriko at least 18 years old in 2020. Her information card from the care packages refutes this.
  • Akira tutored Noriko after the accident, likely from 2014 to 2017, when she should have been 13 years old. This makes her 3 years old at the absolute most at the time of the first kiss. The last point could not have happened in that case.
Between the flashback, the tour, and Kyoto, every interpretation has apparently irreconcilable failures.

That brings me to the most important point about Kyoto I have not seen anyone mention: this is a Happy Event! Throughout the story, these events have taken us to places beyond the regular world of Kumon-mi, shown us fantastically unreal happenings, and used baffling collages of imagery to confuse us.

Should we consider Kyoto much more "real" just because it appears to show real events at first glance? I think not. I think that we should regard it, like the others, as a confusing melange that points directly at only part of the truth.

I think the confusion over timelines is intentional and part of what marks this as a Happy Event, along with the aforementioned Windows XP wallpaper and train platform full of Kenji. Kyoto could essentially be a dream constructed in Sensei's reset-addled mind out of elements that never really coexisted.

In any case, I think the most we can take from the event for the moment is that Sekai was likely more sympathetic than we have previously been led to believe, as well as some points in favor of Ami being Akira's true daughter, and further evidence that Niki and Noriko are somehow not as they seem.

The Orb, as has been mentioned, is the same entity shown in the Ayane-Maya selfie from a prior reset. At this point it seems like the Sensei-Quest world is crossing back over into the real world. Perhaps Akira was on the roof the entire time?

Meowri calls the Orb a 'dark entity', so I suppose this is what the Red Twins fed themselves to? I wonder whether we'll see those two again. Maybe this is a significant inflection point.

A successful Orb fight incurs no damage, then once the final attack is made, the Orb deals immense damage to Sensei without killing him. I think Sensei's desperate plea is notable:

s "Stop! Please! I’ll leave you alone! I’ll be good! I’ll stay here forever!"

These are the answers to Akira's deepest worries. When he's at his lowest, these are the things he desperately tries in order to make things right. He tries to leave the girls alone. He tries to be a good person. He (almost) decides to stay in the room for the rest of his life.

This makes me think that the Orb is the darkness within Akira, and the battle is a doomed metaphorical attempt to defeat it. But something prevents it from consuming him entirely.

In the final moments on the roof, the name above the Orb's health bar changes to 'GOD' and the view warps, breaking down into horizontal bands and primary colors as if it were the last render of a crashing computer program. I also feel as if there's a head or some other image behind the Orb, here, but I don't know what.

View attachment 4106721

Then everything stops and we see a Windows BSOD memory error on a cracked screen, accompanied by an intense electronic hum. Then we zoom out and the error is revealed to be on a curved computer monitor. We seem to have the perspective of the individual sitting at the console. Who or what is this?

View attachment 4106737

We hear the gun cocking sound from Paper City, followed by a single shot, and then the opening messages to Lessons in Love play. Did the person at the console shoot the computer? Did somebody else shoot the person at the console? Was this moment part of Akira's conscious experience?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

A stab at theory-crafting:

There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

This was a good update, lots to think about, and it's been a while since I've anticipated the next installment so much. It really is amazing that this story has been going strong, fueling so much genuine interest, for so long. It's the only thing I've ever read that has almost felt like another life.

For thematic similarity, Dissonance is the only real contender.
For pure quality, all I can do is second the recommendations for Perfect Pitch and Pale Carnations.

spoilers.title: Kyoto
spoilers.html:
Kyoto is a catalyst that revealed severe inconsistency in all the material we've been shown regarding Akira and Niki's relationship timeline. It appears to me that no matter which way you cut it up, you're still left with obvious violations of causality. These troubles are pervasive and existed long before this update. I don't think this is any kind of mistake on Selebus's part. We're just getting more pieces to a complex puzzle.

Here are some items I think we can take as true-as-it-gets:
  • Through the entire story, the current year is 2020
  • Akira Arakawa is 31 years old
  • Akira was 23 years old at the time of the accident that killed Sekai
  • The main girls are all either 14, 15, or 16 years old
Here's what I think is near-certainly true within the context of Kyoto:
  • By the first phase (Niki and Akira together), their romance started 1+ year prior, and Noriko is at least 3 years old.
  • During the second phase (Sekai and Akira together), Sekai is carrying her first child (Ami) and Akira is pubescent.
  • The third phase (portrait of Sekai) depicts her funeral, just after the accident.
I think the following are the "cleanest" places to put these phases in the timeline based on the information depicted. The first phase (Niki's room) takes place in 2008 or later, Akira being 19 years old. The second phase takes place in 2005, Akira being 16 years old. The third phase takes place in 2012, Akira being 23 years old.

However, even taking the first two phases as distinct times, they still don't fit! Confounding factors:
  • Akira and Niki determinedly call each other 'friends' even though they should have started "officially" dating by 2007, according to Niki. (Note: 'friend' may be a pet name! Niki also uses it during the tour.)
  • Niki pushes Akira to have sex and he resists, even though they never had sex while dating because Akira 'never pushed [her]', according to Niki.
  • Based on the tour, Noriko was 5 or older when Niki and Akira were playing in the woods, pretending to be 'an underground crime-fighting organization', at a time predating the start of their romance. That would make Noriko at least 18 years old in 2020. Her information card from the care packages refutes this.
  • Akira tutored Noriko after the accident, likely from 2014 to 2017, when she should have been 13 years old. This makes her 3 years old at the absolute most at the time of the first kiss. The last point could not have happened in that case.
Between the flashback, the tour, and Kyoto, every interpretation has apparently irreconcilable failures.

That brings me to the most important point about Kyoto I have not seen anyone mention: this is a Happy Event! Throughout the story, these events have taken us to places beyond the regular world of Kumon-mi, shown us fantastically unreal happenings, and used baffling collages of imagery to confuse us.

Should we consider Kyoto much more "real" just because it appears to show real events at first glance? I think not. I think that we should regard it, like the others, as a confusing melange that points directly at only part of the truth.

I think the confusion over timelines is intentional and part of what marks this as a Happy Event, along with the aforementioned Windows XP wallpaper and train platform full of Kenji. Kyoto could essentially be a dream constructed in Sensei's reset-addled mind out of elements that never really coexisted.

In any case, I think the most we can take from the event for the moment is that Sekai was likely more sympathetic than we have previously been led to believe, as well as some points in favor of Ami being Akira's true daughter, and further evidence that Niki and Noriko are somehow not as they seem.

spoilers.title: The Orb
spoilers.html:
The Orb, as has been mentioned, is the same entity shown in the Ayane-Maya selfie from a prior reset. At this point it seems like the Sensei-Quest world is crossing back over into the real world. Perhaps Akira was on the roof the entire time?

Meowri calls the Orb a 'dark entity', so I suppose this is what the Red Twins fed themselves to? I wonder whether we'll see those two again. Maybe this is a significant inflection point.

A successful Orb fight incurs no damage, then once the final attack is made, the Orb deals immense damage to Sensei without killing him. I think Sensei's desperate plea is notable:

s "Stop! Please! I’ll leave you alone! I’ll be good! I’ll stay here forever!"

These are the answers to Akira's deepest worries. When he's at his lowest, these are the things he desperately tries in order to make things right. He tries to leave the girls alone. He tries to be a good person. He (almost) decides to stay in the room for the rest of his life.

This makes me think that the Orb is the darkness within Akira, and the battle is a doomed metaphorical attempt to defeat it. But something prevents it from consuming him entirely.

In the final moments on the roof, the name above the Orb's health bar changes to 'GOD' and the view warps, breaking down into horizontal bands and primary colors as if it were the last render of a crashing computer program. I also feel as if there's a head or some other image behind the Orb, here, but I don't know what.

View attachment 4106721

Then everything stops and we see a Windows BSOD memory error on a cracked screen, accompanied by an intense electronic hum. Then we zoom out and the error is revealed to be on a curved computer monitor. We seem to have the perspective of the individual sitting at the console. Who or what is this?

View attachment 4106737

We hear the gun cocking sound from Paper City, followed by a single shot, and then the opening messages to Lessons in Love play. Did the person at the console shoot the computer? Did somebody else shoot the person at the console? Was this moment part of Akira's conscious experience?

In any case, we pick back up with Akira in the midst of a past Halloween. It seems that Makoto is there with him. Ayane has appeared in the midst of another Halloween, and Maya is seen in yet another. I hope that Yumi is in a similar situation.

I think this is all still part of the reset, as actually breaking up the timelines would lead to outright insanity.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Sekai
spoilers.html:
There are three different manifestations of Sekai:
  • A pure hallucination, entirely in Akira's head - This is marked by the simultaneous appearance of a monitor with static
  • A free-roaming ghost - This is marked by any apparent interaction with the world; such as the appearance in front of Yasu; the supernatural threesome with Makoto and Futaba; or the manipulation of Tsuneyo
  • A fragment in partial possession of Kaori - This is marked by Kaori having red eyes, or evidently by Kaori speaking Sekai's mind
I believe Akira's hallucination is the most malicious, while the fragment inside Kaori is the least malicious.

spoilers.title: Controversial Suggestion: Noriko
spoilers.html:
Noriko did not age during the time Akira tutored her.

It seems to me this is the simplest detail we can assert to make the information we have about the Nakayarakawayama timeline make sense.

1989: Akira born
1991: Niki born

2001: Noriko born (Akira is 12, Niki is 10)

2005: Second phase of Kyoto (train platform)
2005: Ami born (Akira is 16, Noriko is 5)
2006: Noriko old enough (5-6) to invade Akira & Niki's forest hideout
2006: Akira and Niki's first kiss (Akira is 17, Niki is 15)
2007: Akira and Niki start dating
2008: First phase of Kyoto (Noriko's room)

2012: Sekai dies, Akira disappears

2014: Akira starts tutoring Noriko, she stops aging (he is 25, she is 12)
2017: Akira disappears with Maya, Noriko starts aging again at 12

2020: Noriko appears in Akira's class (Noriko is now 16)

This is of course supernatural and I'm not sure what the mechanism would be. It's notable that during the tutoring period, Akira is only close to Ami, Maya, and Noriko. All these girls are unique and possibly have a tenuous connection with reality. In any case, this tutoring period seems to be the most confusing aspect of the story's timeline.

I had this thought while considering the situation surrounding Kyoto, and I'm interested to know whether anyone thinks it remotely plausible. Is there evidence for or against this idea?

For those wondering what I mean by Nodoka pulling a fast one then:
Nodoka - "There's a code. One that I've figured out because I'm a fucking genius. Also probably because it was me who made it. But even finding where I hid them is-"
- "Don't 'Nodoka' me you angel-voiced idol fucker! You haven't the faintest idea how many of times I've done this and failed! And neither do I! That's the whole fucking point!"
- "Because you have never smelt the dead! She was loved! There's no way they didn't know! Something- someone rewrote them! The same thing is probably happening to us!"
Himawari-Otoha - "You can have an entire rotisserie chicken, two lemonades, and some JagaRico."
Nodoka - "I've never really contemplated the fact that I've been actually seeing things before. This is a huge fucking curveball, huh? Why didn't past me say anything?"
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'When The Well Runs Dry' Event)

Presumably, Nodoka is aware of being rewritten, having failed previously, has deciphered codes from her past self, and may have used the whole list of food and drinks as a code for her next self once she realized that something about Otoha wasn't right, while making it sound like she and her past selves never realized she could hallucinate, to make the supernatural stuff think she'll never realize that, causing them to let down their guard and presumably rewrite her to a point where she is more compliant.

In this instance she established that she'd be more compliant with the Rotisserie Chicken, Two Lemonades, and a JagaRico.

Assuming she wasn't just erased completely, the next Nodoka might wake up with those items and they might be part of a code that the next Nodoka can use to perhaps have more success next time.

Presumably, RCLLJR. Which might translate to Recall Journal or something akin to that.

Nodoka has also implied that she figured shit out before due to a misplaced stain:
Nodoka - "I was following myself. I had carried this cross before. And it did not matter how many times my knees would buckle along the way as I had already reached the end once."
- "But when the new end finally came, it was the beginning --- for the words were the same..."
- "But the crescent-moon shaped coffee stain in the upper right corner was now in the bottom left."
- "Don't you idiots get it?"
- "It's all a broken record. We're repeating."
(Chapter 4 Nodoka 'Mille Crepe' Event)

Overall: When faced with Memory and Time as opposing factors, surely she'd have some contingencies in place, and if she's smart, I don't see why she'd claim to overlook the possibility of hallucinations unless she was trying to gaslight the hallucinations in this instance.

TLDR: The next Nodoka may inherit the mission with more intel than the supernatural stuff is aware of.

Nodoka cares too much and each Nodoka gets closer and closer.

Unless of course, she just gets erased or changed into a completely different person, but that doesn't really seem likely considering this likely wasn't the first time this even happened, which is why she ended up there in the first place. Retracing her steps.

Vega Cifer said:
but how would I go about reading the script files for puzzles and stuff
Click to expand...
notepad ++, search, find in files, set the directory to the game folder and set filter to *.rpy*, search for whatever is in the text box to get you close to the right place in the correct ".rpy" file. Then read around a bit. If its a text box puzzle question its usually pretty easy to see the answer straight away.

If it's something like these boss fights, you can try to find if it's using a variable to track progression, or something else like that. Then search for all instances of that variable to see where its being referenced and then read what button you need to click to progress. For example the worm boss progression is tracked with "mannykillpts" and with that you can find the if statements that refer to it. Then go back up from there to see what button the if statement is under. In the case of these boss fights the correct choices all increment the variable by 1 so its easy to see what order they go in because the "if" statements are all checking for numbers in order, "if mannykillpts == 0, if mannykillpts == 1, if mannykillpts == 2," etc.

Although I usually avoid doing this when playing new updates unless I get really sick of a puzzle. Because its easy to end up reading things further down the page and accidentally ruining a reveal for yourself. Also really good for finding stuff when you don't remember what event it was from, be it text or images. I sure hope Sel doesn't realise that you can ship the game without the .rpy files and just include the .rpyc files because it will make doing this a bit more annoying. Although I fell like Sel must know that by now and leaves them there intentionally for some kind of meta reason, like he wants us to start reading them and get further entangled into the game or some shit like that.

  • In 2020, Sensei and Maya reunites with Noriko. Noriko is 16, Maya 15, Sensei 31, and Niki 29.

Keeping in mind that my suggestion is an exercise meant to select a single element we can change to make the timeline optimally coherent based on what we know, I think it can be adapted to this reality:

--> Noriko was born around 2001, stopped aging around age 6, and started aging again when Sensei began tutoring her.

This supposition gives her reasonable ages for the events of the tour, the first kiss, and Kyoto. I think we still have to either split Kyoto, or assume that Akira and Niki were having overt sexual interactions for years before deciding to 'get together'. So far I feel the former fits better.

I'd like to point out some relevant parts:
1. "What is that thing?" "A new beginning.". Akira collected four different orbs to spawn a whole being to create a new beginning, could this have to do with Himawari's plan? You'll soon see why I mention this.

2. "There is a dark entity within each and every one of us and this one is yours.". The orb might very well be Akira. If it's corruption, a hungry hole made out of what's missing inside him, or just another deity I have no idea. But it's been seen before in prior resets, so it's doubtful that it really is that important cause there was no ritual to summon it in previous events, and yet it showed up in Ayane's phone.

3. "Good luck, hero." "The final battle begins now!". This is why I brought up Himawari's name, this isn't the first time Akira has been called a hero. In fact, he's called a hero during a pivotal moment in which an unnamed narrator says they're going against Pareidolia's command to stop the auto-pilot. Could Kaori have been that unnamed narrator? That was when I first theorized that it would be very cool if a Kaori that could speak properly was narrating some events. Or it could just be that both Meowri and that narrator are allies.

4. Okay, the actual important part: The Orb does not move. But as Sensei begins to fade away, he can faintly make out the sounds of whispers bleeding from the dark entity's center. "Believe...in...God..." But is that what the whispers are actually commanding? Or is that just what he expects to hear? In his final moments, he changes everything about himself. He becomes a better man. He finally learns what it is that makes the earth move. But it is too late for belief alone to change anything.

"Is it what the orb is saying or what he expects to hear?" is such a powerful question. But even more important than that, to me, is the notion that in his final moments he changes everything about himself. This fits very well with the theory that the entire reset is taking place in his final moments of life, either mid-flight from jumping, or just generally dying. There is also an interesting notion that Akira is able to grasp the truth of the resets by dying, well, what does that mean? Could it be a sort of bluejay revelation, or is it something deeper? That by dying he's about to be placed back in the room of the clocks and given all his authority back until resetting everything again?
I think the most relevant out of all these things is the use of the word "hero", as I have pointed out, it's also used by the narrator of the auto-pilot disengage sequence. If that's an actual clue I don't know.

Edit: Mentions of hero:
"Frankly, that girl had it coming for being such an incorrigible, single-minded bitch all the time."
"And if my premonitions are correct, it is this exact turning of the tides that will help you swim your way back to shore and remember your rightful place in all of this."
"Not as the main character. "
"Not as the hero."
"But as one of several manifestations of the falling action in a story that will never end."
"And while that may sound implausible or meaningless, your descent shows us otherwise. Your infinite falling is a priceless work of art in a universe left out of the light."
"You will break for now. But soon, you will become the Collector."
"The scene opens with our former hero positioned in the center of his bed, wearing a festive cap while surrounded by fish."
"Drool leaks from his mouth, the remnants of an unending dream left there to air dry until his {b}CARETAKER{/b} returns home."
"The former hero peeled away from the target of these torturous words. Who's managed to evade them, just as he's evaded {i}everything{/i} with the help of his broken doll."
"I know you can hear this. But I know it won't stick, so I'll say it with emphasis-"
"We are coming for you."

scene black
with dissolve2

"I have disregarded the letter from the desk of the ninth god. And I have pulled the plug on AUTO-PILOT as I know from experience that wires can only do so much."
"Pareidolia will have my throat for it, but it will all be worthwhile if the two of {b}US{/b} return to form."

Right now i'm still on page 2216 due to circumstances, but some might have realised because of likes for a week old post.

I've already seen enough posts where i'd like to add but might not, because i'll have forgotten by reaching 2239 while writing this.

What i do want to write about is something that became way more apparent with the last update, and that is how we perceive certain characters after a certain update. And this time it was Sekai, and i saw that other people already mentioned it.

Together with Lil, i want to break this down into three sections, because i also want to mention other media that fit into that topic.
Hopefully i can make those as short as possible.

So in LiL we already had several characters that were acting horrible and then got some kind of short redemption arc to explain how things came to be, or how they became bad people. Sometimes they try to be better.

Ami: Dead Parents/Mother -> Knife incident, several changes in character (kind of unbeliebable though)
Kirin: Neglected by parents -> Tries to be better, kind of.
Osako: Insecurities -> Knows about her insecurites now, tries to be better
Most pominent - Sekai: We know she's also a abuse victim.
Others...

I can hear you laugh there

For those who don't know: It's an Anime (borderline hentai) about, yeah, mostly rape. So watch it if you can stomache it, or don't.

If you watched:
Gotta say, besides the dick slap, that made me laugh pretty hard, after watching it, some interesting thoughts came up.

Imagine:
A woman gets raped.
How does society think about her perpetrator?
Throw him (presumably male) into a cell and throw the key away? Kill Him?
What if it was a guy that was raped? (Nah i don't care?)
What if the woman takes revenge, before the perpetrator got caught and rapes him with a cactus or whatever?
Throw her in prison or kill her, still?
Now, what if a guy got raped and takes revenge?

Watch this one if you can. Though, the animation only picks up half of it's source material (1st half), so you'd have to switch to the comics for the full experience.

This one is harder to explain.
In general it's about a woman, with a predating trauma, who gets raped (offscreen/prestory) and through all that and more dragged between reality and a supernataural world (the outback).
The thing here is, and i think it shares similarities with LiL, that her perpetrator (Mr. gone) also has a history of being abused as a child by a family member.

So, where do i want to get with these?
In short i think Sel wants to get his audience to think about morals and ethics about certain, yet obvious topics.

Is a villain still a villain if they get a sad background that explains their wrongdoings, because they lived through the same or similar experience?

What bugs me though is the 4th wall breaking, and a lingerering felling of Sel trying to shove his audience opinions into whatever direction.

This is an interesting discussion, but I don't feel the same way about it as it relates to LiL.

Osako was never really a villain and neither was Otoha, for all that I dislike her. Osako was just an adult behaving as, well, her age - she's a young adult amd clearly hasn't found herself, as most her age haven't. She was dick to Akira but that was hardly done out of malice, and more that she was a dumbass.

Nodoka was a villain and it certainly makes her a sort of extreme reverse Makoto in retrospect. She's trying to save everyone and honestly, if I was in her shoes I would care less about people's feelings as well. Let's care about that after they're free. However, Nodoka's situation is so unique in its fiction that it's hard to compare to real life in any way.

The real actual villain of the story would be Sekai, if anything, and the easiest to apply your pov, however, all Kyoto did was reveal a possible real Sekai for which we had no context so far. I don't feel like it's trying to justify her actions so much as presenting the reader with the realisation that real life is complex.

NAO (the xeonon) had said previously that both Akira and Sekai loved eachother for real. However twisted that might have been to others, it was real for them. Is that so far from Maya and Akira's relationship that most of us came to love? yes. Yes, it is. But both relationships have similarities, and I think what's Selebus is trying to portray here is that more often than not things can be uncomfortably complicated.

An avatar of corruption that toys with her underage prey and calls that love is certainly easier to stomach (as a villain) than a miserable girl tormented by voices, abused since childhood, that goes on to be abused by her husband, and finally finds solace in providing her version of "pure" love to a child, giving Akira what perhaps she wished someone would have given unto her, and truly wishing and willing to start over by his side.

That's just one possible reading. And I think that if there is one thing Selebus has been hammering on since the start was that things are complicated. Isn't that the whole point of Akira as a character in the first place? Therefore all characters should eventually be shown as complicated. Does that complication redeem them? I think, if anything, Selebus has been strongly positioned on the camp of "no, it does not". After all, he's constantly calling Akira out on it.

Moonflare said:
This fits very well with the theory that the entire reset is taking place in his final moments of life, either mid-flight from jumping, or just generally dying. There is also an interesting notion that Akira is able to grasp the truth of the resets by dying, well, what does that mean? Could it be a sort of bluejay revelation, or is it something deeper? That by dying he's about to be placed back in the room of the clocks and given all his authority back until resetting everything again?
Click to expand...
Very good post, as per usual, and an excellent point.

I always felt that the theory that everything that is happening in this game is just Akira's brain trying to process various jumbled up memories, what-if scenarios, dreams and traumas within basically milliseconds, is almost too obvious or convenient, given a lot of the scenes from just the beginning of the game. But you're right that this whole scene fits that a lot.

The vibe I personally got from the "whispers" was that they could be of his loved ones that stand at his hospital bed as he is fighting for his life after his suicide attempt - it's a commonly used trope at least. "Believe in God", or something along that line (Akira is in a coma and would only hear very faint voices, if anything, after all), could easily be said by a relative (to someone else) who has HOPE that he will still make it, as faith is often the last resort for many people in such scenarios.
Akira, becoming "a better man" in his mind, trying to come to terms with the fact that he was a twisted man and feels immense regret, right as the great darkness is enveloping him (i.e. he loses his fight and dies in real life -> game over screen).

It would still leave a bitter taste in my mouth though, if a majority of the plot and the mysteries could be explained simply by "LEL Akira was just a suicidal pedo and he just imagined all the girls to fit his tastes and make him love him, but still made them flawed so that he wouldn't feel bad about abusing them (Harem route), but eventually feels guilty about being a bad man (he punishes himself = dark route) before he eventually "becomes a better man" by helping "them" overcome "their" traumas (that he was mostly projecting onto them) so that he has some closure in the end (purity routes), right before he dies ".

It would feel kind of lazy if it were to go this general direction, there's too many nuances and seemingly real and meaningful developments and relationships for it to all just be fabricated within a dying brain in essentially nanoseconds.

Then again, this is pretty much what happened to LOST (the TV series about the stranded people on the island), the end was very anti-climactic and felt like it destroyed a lot of the mystery and worldbuilding that has been established in previous seasons, for it to just end up being
things that have been imagined (?) by a character, some religious and magical mambo jambo, basically a lot of "actually, this was never real life, most of what happened had no impact on anything". This is an interesting discussion, but I don't feel the same way about it as it relates to LiL.

Osako was never really a villain and neither was Otoha, for all that I dislike her. Osako was just an adult behaving as, well, her age - she's a young adult amd clearly hasn't found herself, as most her age haven't. She was dick to Akira but that was hardly done out of malice, and more that she was a dumbass.

Nodoka was a villain and it certainly makes her a sort of extreme reverse Makoto in retrospect. She's trying to save everyone and honestly, if I was in her shoes I would care less about people's feelings as well. Let's care about that after they're free. However, Nodoka's situation is so unique in its fiction that it's hard to compare to real life in any way.

The real actual villain of the story would be Sekai, if anything, and the easiest to apply your pov, however, all Kyoto did was reveal a possible real Sekai for which we had no context so far. I don't feel like it's trying to justify her actions so much as presenting the reader with the realisation that real life is complex.

NAO (the xeonon) had said previously that both Akira and Sekai loved eachother for real. However twisted that might have been to others, it was real for them. Is that so far from Maya and Akira's relationship that most of us came to love? yes. Yes, it is. But both relationships have similarities, and I think what's Selebus is trying to portray here is that more often than not things can be uncomfortably complicated.

An avatar of corruption that toys with her underage prey and calls that love is certainly easier to stomach (as a villain) than a miserable girl tormented by voices, abused since childhood, that goes on to be abused by her husband, and finally finds solace in providing her version of "pure" love to a child, giving Akira what perhaps she wished someone would have given unto her, and truly wishing and willing to start over by his side.

That's just one possible reading. And I think that if there is one thing Selebus has been hammering on since the start was that things are complicated. Isn't that the whole point of Akira as a character in the first place? Therefore all characters should eventually be shown as complicated. Does that complication redeem them? I think, if anything, Selebus has been strongly positioned on the camp of "no, it does not". After all, he's constantly calling Akira out on it.

I've written up some thoughts on The Orb. For best ambience, please listen to theholelol.mp3 on loop while reading this post.
View attachment theholelol.mp3
Someone already pointed out the orb appears in Ayane's picture from the fifth reset. It also shows up in "The End of the Tour" when Sensei is blocking out the accident, and he sees a sakura tree inside of it.
In Sensei Quest, Meowri creates the orb after a car crash. When you put these together, it seems likely to me that the orb was created when Sekai was killed in the accident. My guess is it's the manifestation of Akira's feelings of grief and guilt, and desire to punish himself for not preventing her death by leaving with her - which is consistent with Meowri calling it the dark entity inside of him.

In the fifth reset photo, the orb is in the place where the moon should be. During the reset itself, there's a red moon and Kaori is on the roof wearing Sekai's dress (identified by the nail polish).
So the orb is a black void where a moon should be - probably the moon that Ami wants to use her wish to bring back. We've theorized before that moon is the real Sekai, which seems consistent with the other appearances of the orb.
SeKaori says that bringing the moon back would require rewriting history, i.e. preventing the accident or at least Sekai's death.
As chronox pointed out, the orb's name changes to GOD when it's consuming Sensei.
It's a GOD that is composed of four parts and came into being after a car accident. The narration from "First Contact" also talks about the USER gods being created by a (possibly metaphorical) car crash.
It's also likely that it has something to do with the thing that sings in its sleep, which is missing the orb meant to guide it and has something to do with a god that encompasses everything. This is from an event in the same update as "First Contact" and they both use itsingsinitssleep.mp3
Later we're told it's the middle of the four-sided cross, i.e. it encompasses all four gods.
What I'm unclear on is whether the orb is itself that thing that sings in its sleep - in which case the orb that's supposed to guide it is the missing moon - or if this means that the returned orb is going to wake some other sleeping entity.

John might have warned about the orb in "Sasom i en Spegel". He talks of a dead god that will return after the death of someone of equal value, which is very similar to how SeKaori describes the return of the moon.
Just before that John warns of an entity coming in its "purest form" with bloody tendrils. The orb attacks Sensei with tendrils.

...
This might also be related to the mighty sky tendrils that Yasu talked about when Makoto's dad died.
Yasu was prewarned of that event by hearing the whispers of the world itself, something she's heard on many occasions. Sensei hears whispers coming from the orb.

The four orbs of power that make up the orb are plant, worm, fist, and red. These could be random, but if we try to match them to the trinity: in Life of Prizes a worm crawls out of the Lust Eater's book (USER1), Wires is regularly connected to growing plants (and they're both green), and Pareidolia's color is red. So fist might represent USER4 - I can't think of any implications there, but maybe someone else can come up with something.

I've got some more thoughts on the orb coming in a tinfoil theory I'm working on, so stay tuned.
