Seeing as this question and other things regarding the URM gets asked fairly often on here, I figured I may as well put together a FAQ post that may prove helpful that I can refer others to in the future:

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:


Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:



Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:



It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.



Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!



And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.



You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:


Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:



Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".



Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.



Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.



Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.



'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.



Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.



That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.



Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.



Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?


Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to that I say... let me explain.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:



Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:



Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:



Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.

Well, with the URM, you can! It's rather simple, actually.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.



More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:



'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:



Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.



'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.



From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.



Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.



Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.

Now look, I don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.

Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.

Let's use the most recent puzzle, "SENSEI-QUEST", as our example:

Step One: once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.



Step two: Click the prompt and look for the end label.



Step three: Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.



You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.

Commonly Used Variables:

[charactername]_love = A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love

[charactername]_lust = A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust

rinbetrayed = Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's "Schadenfreude" event in Chapter 1 before the "What's Done is Done" Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is True, you are considered a Bad Homie and will miss certain events. If this variable is False, you didn't betray Rin and are a Good Homie. No events will be missed.

amifingered = Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her "No One Can See Us" Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is False, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the Good Uncle Route. You will miss countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is True, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the Bad Uncle Route, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

*May edit this section a bit more later*
These are both very useful tools I thought I should include along with the post as well. I strongly recommend making use of them, especially as a new player.

Lessons in Love Wiki

LiL Guide Mod

! It's rather simple, actually.

Main Event.

event in Chapter 1 before the

Bad Homie
and will

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:


Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:



Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:



It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.



Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!



And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.
So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.
Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:
It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.
Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!
And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?
By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.
You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

spoilers.title: Rin Event Miss
Unlock Missed Scenes Guide
spoilers.html:
Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:



Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".



Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.



Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.



Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.



'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.



Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.



That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.



Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.



Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

spoilers.title: View One Time Scenes Again!
spoilers.html:
First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.



More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:



'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:



Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.



'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.



From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.



Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.



Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Seeing as this question and other things regarding the URM gets asked fairly often on here, I figured I may as well put together a FAQ post that may prove helpful that I can refer others to in the future:

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:

View attachment 4139622

Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:

View attachment 4139065

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:

View attachment 4139037

It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.

View attachment 4139038 View attachment 4139039

Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!

View attachment 4139066

And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

View attachment 4139040

You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339

Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to that I say... let me explain.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:

View attachment 4139382

Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:

View attachment 4139383

Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:

View attachment 4139384

Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.

Well, with the URM, you can! It's rather simple, actually.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.

View attachment 4139442

Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.

View attachment 4139434

Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.

Now look, I don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.

Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.

Let's use the most recent puzzle, "SENSEI-QUEST", as our example:

Step One: once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.

View attachment 4139531

Step two: Click the prompt and look for the end label.

View attachment 4139533

Step three: Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.

View attachment 4139534 View attachment 4139535

You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.

Commonly Used Variables:

[charactername]_love = A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love

[charactername]_lust = A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust

rinbetrayed = Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's "Schadenfreude" event in Chapter 1 before the "What's Done is Done" Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is True, you are considered a Bad Homie and will miss certain events. If this variable is False, you didn't betray Rin and are a Good Homie. No events will be missed.

amifingered = Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her "No One Can See Us" Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is False, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the Good Uncle Route. You will miss countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is True, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the Bad Uncle Route, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

*May edit this section a bit more later*

These are both very useful tools I thought I should include along with the post as well. I strongly recommend making use of them, especially as a new player.

Lessons in Love Wiki

LiL Guide Mod
Click to expand...

spoilers.title: URM Bible
spoilers.html:
What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:

View attachment 4139622

Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:

View attachment 4139065

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:

View attachment 4139037

It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.

View attachment 4139038 View attachment 4139039

Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!

View attachment 4139066

And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

View attachment 4139040

You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339

Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to that I say... let me explain.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:

View attachment 4139382

Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:

View attachment 4139383

Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:

View attachment 4139384

Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.

Well, with the URM, you can! It's rather simple, actually.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.

View attachment 4139442

Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.

View attachment 4139434

Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.

Now look, I don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.

Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.

Let's use the most recent puzzle, "SENSEI-QUEST", as our example:

Step One: once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.

View attachment 4139531

Step two: Click the prompt and look for the end label.

View attachment 4139533

Step three: Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.

View attachment 4139534 View attachment 4139535

You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.

Commonly Used Variables:

[charactername]_love = A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love

[charactername]_lust = A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust

rinbetrayed = Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's "Schadenfreude" event in Chapter 1 before the "What's Done is Done" Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is True, you are considered a Bad Homie and will miss certain events. If this variable is False, you didn't betray Rin and are a Good Homie. No events will be missed.

amifingered = Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her "No One Can See Us" Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is False, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the Good Uncle Route. You will miss countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is True, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the Bad Uncle Route, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

Moonflare said:
Maya claims
that Noriko doesn't know what she's talking about,
that there was no molestation,
that she was the one that came onto him,
that their hands touched by accident,
that he thought for so long before giving in -
Click to expand...
Speaking of which, I've always wondered whether what Noriko stated about "Maya being molested" in Taco Tuesday truly is pointing at Sensei's relation with wizard Maya. Objectively speaking, there is almost no doubt in that according to the entire context of that event; you know, the whole tutor room flashback, the lil conversation about handjobs, some kind of prying at Sensei x Wizard Maya from Noriko, etc.

It's just......this means Noriko is righteous enough to be willing to, years later, describe behaviors of a person she likes for as long as she could remember as "molesting", but is also love-drunk enough to keep loving the said molester even today. This is more or less OK considering how Noriko's personalities are established; I guess this is a gasp at how Noriko defies "love is blind".

What I am trying here instead is presenting a minor possibility that pins the statement "Maya being molested" even further back in time, to before Maya even met Sensei. In this update we got a confirmation about Maya's favorite place being a random vending machine somewhere near the halfway point between the home she had and the home she wanted. This resonates quite well with the little unknown story told in S.E.K.A.I., which is seemingly about "the fateful rendezvous of a runaway girl and a guy in front of vending machines".

I am not sure whether this vending machine is the exact same one which Maya Prime bought canned coffees for Sensei in early chapters, but that's besides the point. The point is IF this story REALLY is about Maya, then the proof of her being molested even further back in the past will be established by "She'd been previously exposed to the evils of man in the form of a distant relative", which could be what Noriko is referring to. Even if this isn't what Noriko is talking about due to the fact that Noriko might not have a way to know all this, but what she said might ring a different bell in Maya's head.
(in simpler sentences: Noriko still thinks Sensei molested wizard Maya, but Maya fires back with something else in mind, implying "Sensei was not molesting me; you don't fucking know the first thing about being molested)

Regardless, this remains a much minor possibility because 1) the little S.E.K.A.I. story has to be about Maya and not someone else, and 2) we have to ignore a good amount of subtexts in Taco Tuesday.

Fire Lord Zuko said:
Seeing as this question and other things regarding the URM gets asked fairly often on here, I figured I may as well put together a FAQ post that may prove helpful that I can refer others to in the future:

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:

View attachment 4139622

Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:

View attachment 4139065

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:

View attachment 4139037

It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.

View attachment 4139038 View attachment 4139039

Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!

View attachment 4139066

And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

View attachment 4139040

You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339

Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to that I say... let me explain.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:

View attachment 4139382

Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:

View attachment 4139383

Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:

View attachment 4139384

Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.

Well, with the URM, you can! It's rather simple, actually.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.

View attachment 4139442

Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.

View attachment 4139434

Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.

Now look, I don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.

Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.

Let's use the most recent puzzle, "SENSEI-QUEST", as our example:

Step One: once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.

View attachment 4139531

Step two: Click the prompt and look for the end label.

View attachment 4139533

Step three: Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.

View attachment 4139534 View attachment 4139535

You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.

Commonly Used Variables:

[charactername]_love = A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love

[charactername]_lust = A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust

rinbetrayed = Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's "Schadenfreude" event in Chapter 1 before the "What's Done is Done" Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is True, you are considered a Bad Homie and will miss certain events. If this variable is False, you didn't betray Rin and are a Good Homie. No events will be missed.

amifingered = Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her "No One Can See Us" Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is False, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the Good Uncle Route. You will miss countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is True, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the Bad Uncle Route, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

*May edit this section a bit more later*
These are both very useful tools I thought I should include along with the post as well. I strongly recommend making use of them, especially as a new player.

Lessons in Love Wiki

LiL Guide Mod
Click to expand...
in URM bible we believe, praise be!

something I could think to add, even if the solutions to puzzles are added after a bit on the first page, is that any word to "guess" like in reset 4 is easily findable by taking a look at the rpy files where the event is stored


probably not very useful for old resets, but if anything similar to "guess the word!" comes back in the future, it's a good thing to know

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:

View attachment 4139622

Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:

View attachment 4139065

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:

View attachment 4139037

It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.

View attachment 4139038 View attachment 4139039

Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!

View attachment 4139066

And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

View attachment 4139040

You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

spoilers.title: Unlock Missed Scenes Guide
spoilers.html:
Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

spoilers.title: View One Time Scenes Again!
spoilers.html:
First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.

View attachment 4139442

Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.

View attachment 4139434

Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

animexmangafan said:
This reminded me of I finally understood, you were just as broken as me from sleepsong.mp3, was that Maya too?.
Click to expand...
yes. I'll add some of the quotes about Maya, mind you, only the first two are "confirmed" to be about her. The rest could be, but it's unclear.
1. Do you remember the first time we touched hands? It happened by accident on the floor of your bedroom. At first I thought there was no way you'd ever see me in that light. But when all the other lights burned out, and I was still there, I finally understood: You were just as broken as me. And I knew then and there that I would fall unto you.

2. Do you remember the first time you told me you loved me? It was snowing. I confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. When you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. Like everything I've ever wanted was finally mine. And I could finally be happy. You took me to your room and took my panties off. You put your fingers inside me and I started crying. But they were happy tears - because I finally knew what it meant to be loved.

3. Forget everything you know about love. Forget everything you know about her. Give unto me what you're incapable of giving to anyone else. Only then can you be saved. I'm doing this for your own good.

4. The coarseness of the ground upon which you sit tears microscope holes in the fabric of a young girl's dress. It captivates you, like an unobscured horizon, or a beautiful bird you are seeing for the first time; A heron comes to mind. You find yourself pondering the difference light can make and why some things are so much prettier when left unlit. You forget this. Your mind goes somewhere else. You follow it. You end up in front of a well. You look down. But when your eyes make contact with the bottom, you realize that it is you that you are looking down upon. When you blink, you are back at home. Safe and sound. Perhaps it is time to start wearing denim.
fdsasdf_p said:
Speaking of which, I've always wondered whether what Noriko stated about "Maya being molested" in Taco Tuesday truly is pointing at Sensei's relation with wizard Maya. Objectively speaking, there is almost no doubt in that according to the entire context of that event; you know, the whole tutor room flashback, the lil conversation about handjobs, some kind of prying at Sensei x Wizard Maya from Noriko, etc.

It's just......this means Noriko is righteous enough to be willing to, years later, describe behaviors of a person she likes for as long as she could remember as "molesting", but is also love-drunk enough to keep loving the said molester even today. This is more or less OK considering how Noriko's personalities are established; I guess this is a gasp at how Noriko defies "love is blind".

What I am trying here instead is presenting a minor possibility that pins the statement "Maya being molested" even further back in time, to before Maya even met Sensei. In this update we got a confirmation about Maya's favorite place being a random vending machine somewhere near the halfway point between the home she had and the home she wanted. This resonates quite well with the little unknown story told in S.E.K.A.I., which is seemingly about "the fateful rendezvous of a runaway girl and a guy in front of vending machines".

I am not sure whether this vending machine is the exact same one which Maya Prime bought canned coffees for Sensei in early chapters, but that's besides the point. The point is IF this story REALLY is about Maya, then the proof of her being molested even further back in the past will be established by "She'd been previously exposed to the evils of man in the form of a distant relative", which could be what Noriko is referring to. Even if this isn't what Noriko is talking about due to the fact that Noriko might not have a way to know all this, but what she said might ring a different bell in Maya's head.
(in simpler sentences: Noriko still thinks Sensei molested wizard Maya, but Maya fires back, implying "he was not; you don't fucking know the first thing about being molested)

Regardless, this remains a much minor possibility because 1) the little S.E.K.A.I. story has to be about Maya and not someone else, and 2) we have to ignore a good amount of subtexts in Taco Tuesday.

View attachment 4139737

View attachment 4139741
View attachment 4139742
Click to expand...
I think that Noriko's stance is rather understandable, actually. It's not that different from what we ourselves have discussed plenty of times. Noriko gets that Akira didn't force himself on Maya, and that Maya loves him dearly. I think this doesn't destroy Akira for her because it's like one of those cases that we talk about like "what if Akira and Maya never separated, and you only found out he molested her after they have been married for 20 years and are a happy family?"

The molestation still happened, it's still a crime, but what is the answer here? Have him go to jail for having sex with his wife of 20 years before the law approved of it? Who would even stand against him in the trial, his wife?

Obviously his relationship with Maya hasn't got to that point yet, but I think that, under its possible comparison, this is where Noriko goes for justification of his actions "he didn't intend to do harm and he was in a fucked up place, he didn't do this to anyone else, and they've been together ever since". The other part of it is the actual sensible interpretation of the event which is "Maya was molested, and she was of an age where she simply couldn't give consent, and the fact that she 'loves' him matters little since its grooming."

But Noriko is still at a bizarre position because she's been in love with him even longer than Maya, and for all her attitude of pointing out how it's fucked up, would she really not be in Maya's position if she had the chance? I seriously doubt that. She was masturbating to her sister giving him blowjobs even before Maya arrived. There is no way she would have refused his advances, she'd probably think of it as even more romantic than Maya did.

So, imo, even though Noriko is 100% correct in telling Maya it was molestation regardless, she's deluding herself in saying she'd never envy being molestated by Akira. Bullshit. And ironically enough, it would be a much more clear cut molestation in Noriko's case than it would have been (potentially) in Maya's - given her past.
I wonder if Maya's family is even real, and that would create implications in both directions. First because it would mean Akira was the first one to molest her, and second because it would be hard to call it molestation if she was an actual god conjured up to serve that function.

On the route of Maya being human, I think that was the point of her words though, I agree. Noriko doesn't know anything because she's just calling what she had with Akira molestation, when the actual "worse" molestation happened to her before and she had to run away from home because of it. For Noriko to call someone that took her in and (potentially) resisted laying hands on her the same as the actual fucked up person that made her run away would be deeply insulting, and I can see why Maya would get mad.

Noriko's still right obviously, but I can see Maya's point.

Edit: added Maya quotes.

spoilers.title: potential Maya quotes
spoilers.html:
1. Do you remember the first time we touched hands? It happened by accident on the floor of your bedroom. At first I thought there was no way you'd ever see me in that light. But when all the other lights burned out, and I was still there, I finally understood: You were just as broken as me. And I knew then and there that I would fall unto you.

2. Do you remember the first time you told me you loved me? It was snowing. I confessed my feelings to you weeks prior and you had been sitting on your decision ever since. When you uttered those words, it was like my heart stopped. Like everything I've ever wanted was finally mine. And I could finally be happy. You took me to your room and took my panties off. You put your fingers inside me and I started crying. But they were happy tears - because I finally knew what it meant to be loved.

3. Forget everything you know about love. Forget everything you know about her. Give unto me what you're incapable of giving to anyone else. Only then can you be saved. I'm doing this for your own good.

4. The coarseness of the ground upon which you sit tears microscope holes in the fabric of a young girl's dress. It captivates you, like an unobscured horizon, or a beautiful bird you are seeing for the first time; A heron comes to mind. You find yourself pondering the difference light can make and why some things are so much prettier when left unlit. You forget this. Your mind goes somewhere else. You follow it. You end up in front of a well. You look down. But when your eyes make contact with the bottom, you realize that it is you that you are looking down upon. When you blink, you are back at home. Safe and sound. Perhaps it is time to start wearing denim.

spoilers.title: about Noriko
spoilers.html:
I think that Noriko's stance is rather understandable, actually. It's not that different from what we ourselves have discussed plenty of times. Noriko gets that Akira didn't force himself on Maya, and that Maya loves him dearly. I think this doesn't destroy Akira for her because it's like one of those cases that we talk about like "what if Akira and Maya never separated, and you only found out he molested her after they have been married for 20 years and are a happy family?"

The molestation still happened, it's still a crime, but what is the answer here? Have him go to jail for having sex with his wife of 20 years before the law approved of it? Who would even stand against him in the trial, his wife?

Obviously his relationship with Maya hasn't got to that point yet, but I think that, under its possible comparison, this is where Noriko goes for justification of his actions "he didn't intend to do harm and he was in a fucked up place, he didn't do this to anyone else, and they've been together ever since". The other part of it is the actual sensible interpretation of the event which is "Maya was molested, and she was of an age where she simply couldn't give consent, and the fact that she 'loves' him matters little since its grooming."

But Noriko is still at a bizarre position because she's been in love with him even longer than Maya, and for all her attitude of pointing out how it's fucked up, would she really not be in Maya's position if she had the chance? I seriously doubt that. She was masturbating to her sister giving him blowjobs even before Maya arrived. There is no way she would have refused his advances, she'd probably think of it as even more romantic than Maya did.

So, imo, even though Noriko is 100% correct in telling Maya it was molestation regardless, she's deluding herself in saying she'd never envy being molestated by Akira. Bullshit. And ironically enough, it would be a much more clear cut molestation in Noriko's case than it would have been (potentially) in Maya's - given her past.

PrincessEuphy said:
I think there's two angles to this: general cognitive dissonance, and a sense of power.

There are few things online which engender cognitive dissonance on the level of piracy, which explains all sorts of cringeworthy behavior online dating all the way back to the LOL, LIMEWIRE animation from like 2007. The fact is that piracy is an anti-social act which harms creators, but the convenience of the act (the lack of legal consequences) combined with the personal benefit of saving money means almost everyone does it anyway. And what happens when people who consider themselves good or reasonably moral people are faced with the fact they are regularly committing an immoral, harmful act? Their brain twists over itself to resolve the dissonance. "Ah, actually there is no real harm, you see I never would have bought the thing anyway." "Ah, actually, I would have bought it (I'm a good person), but I just can't afford to right now." "Yeah I'm kind of an asshole, I pirate, but in a lovable edgy way, I'm the cool uncle." Etc. And in a vacuum, the brain's natural self defense mechanism will protect someone from self-reflection or the need to acknowledge personal guilt. But GSwole doesn't allow that to happen and repeatedly confronts people with reality, thereby throwing the false harmony into disarray and forcing one to confront the cognitive dissonance again, which is unpleasant. Nobody likes that.

Secondly is the sense of power. There's almost nothing worse (metaphorically) you can do on the internet than care about something, because caring is weakness. The seminal visual novel Cross Channel (one of my top 5 "everyone should play" visual novels) has a line where someone observes that love is a battle wherein whoever falls in love first loses, because the other person will have all the power over them. Similarly, online, expressing that you care about something opens up an avenue for strangers to have power over you, and this power they WILL notice having. The meaning here is obvious. GSwole doesn't want people to pirate their game. Person B pirates the game. Person B has the power in this dynamic. They feel a sense of dominance and superiority surge through them like pure energy, as ridiculous as that may sound. On a subconscious level (and sometimes conscious) one begins to feel that they are genuinely just better than the other person on some level - they are in some kind of dominant position. And this leads to looking down on them. There is an almost compulsion within people's minds to belittle and mock those one perceives as beneath them. It's a famous theme in fiction for even those trying to repress this to end up belittling in the other direction, where they reveal they look down on others through their efforts to not do just that. It's a very nasty, primal aspect of the human mind.

And so what happens in this thread is that GSwole openly expresses that he cares about piracy, ergo inspiring those in the thread to look down on him, then he confronts them with their cognitive dissonance, giving them impetus to lash out. Consider "cool" h-game devs who are "chill" with pirates. It doesn't really matter if on the inside they are seething too. On the outside if they present themselves as chill, then there is no power imbalance, and pirates dont feel superior to the devs - they aren't encouraged to belittle them. Then if the dev does not thrust dissonance in people's faces, they are content to remain satisfied and content with themselves, no need to go out of their way to prove a point or establish any aspect of their being or be snarky or self-defensive and so on. That is much wiser in every way, so it's what most people do where they can help it. The problem is just that sometimes, a person may care too much to do that.
